👀

Read the warning- they give you an option of a cash account versus a margin account. 

Idk. Not sure if anyone else has dealt with this and knows what I’m talking about. But I posted a screen pic of what comes after the warning. I felt like I was pulled over by the police lol!

In summary:

i like the idea of still having access to options selling without the 24 hour wait. I don’t think I’ll use any of the other fancier  spreads and clearly my accounts below 25K.

oh well you live and you learn.

title: Need the rain to make things grow
body:
Longish summary for today- thought process. 

Still gathering my final game plan for tomorrow will post that in am. 

As any farmer knows - you need the rain to make things grow. 

So the dipping market is not bothersome to me. Again, I look at it as going to the mall when everything is on clearance, so just looking around at Stocks, I wanna grow into and seeing what I can pick up for cheap.

I put a summary slide of the “ponies I own”-100 shares in each company. I call it “checking the stable”or “looking out on the pasture” —as you can see they’re all down which doesn’t bother me. Again, if I was really savvy, it looks like I would sell puts, on the ones that were approaching 10% loss to blunt. This may be a trick. I learn in the future and utilize. but for now will hold steady. 

I try to keep sell calls out on all my ponies at all times. - “This is making all the horses work hard all the time.”

This strategy limits me a bit in a down market. as well because I think I would have to sell out of my call , likely for a loss of what I received in the premium, To free up the shares and then sell the hundred shares of stock in the market at a loss.   I think this is why it is important to pick companies you feel comfortable. “spending the rainy days with

my $LUNR. roll call option was picked up and I am happy about that. received about nine dollars. Which I will add to positions while everything is on sale. 

I was kind a hoping that,  $WU and maybe even $ASX would’ve gotten called away. those options are currently in the money, but I am asking a high price, so they do have a low fill likelihood

I like $WU, $ASX, and even $RXRX. stocks, but have been just trying to jump into some different positions..  E.g. Upgrade to horse breed I think better for the kind of work I want to do on this farm. right now it looks like things are going on clearance, and I don’t have a lot of cash to take advantage.

I look at crypto  as more of a place to park money that I want to grow quickly I can liquidate it for cash and use it in circumstances like this. When the market is down and I want to buy things on sale.

title: A confession
body:
This post is exclusively for all the poor people on this app that are following me.

If you are rich and/or can trade options: please excuse yourself from the room. 

if you have a mortgage and a car payment and feel poor sometimes:  I’m not talking to you either. Please leave the room as well. 

I'm talking for real poor.  
Like a couple of hundred of dollars is life changing poor. 
Like The idea of working to get 200 dollars to “play with” seems impossible and far away. Exhausting even. 

To You: 

I want to confess. 

I briefly forgot what that was like.  I forgot how the deck is stacked against you and stacked against poor people in general. I'm sorry. 

Did not realize that it is NOT automatic that you can trade options on Robinhood.  I tried to help a family member by buying them straight up 100 shares of a stock. Put the money in their account. They bought the stock. They can not trade the option.

They are not even given a button to select. “ Trade options “ 
Just buy and sell. 
Nope. Nada. 
Tried to enable it in account settings. They say give us a call and we will think about it. 
So if you are poor. Have trouble with English. Anxiety issues whatever.  Calling someone is like saying no. 

Again I'm sorry. Had no idea. Robinhood had levels like that. 

I must develop another strategy. 
I have forgotten where I came from. I swore I would never do this. Yet here I am. I confess this as a sin. Please forgive me. 

Yes. That's the only apology you will get out of me. We are family get over yourself. 

So moving on. 

this is what I'm going to do. 

Going forward: I'm going to post a general summary of the levels below and what I am ACTUALLY doing to help (family) manage these accounts at each stage. They are free to import and export money as they wish. I'm just learning with them with smaller accounts. 

I will continue to focus on myself and race to 10M in this account. Again any posted pics will be from my Robinhood account and this will be the focus. 

So you are free to pick the level that fits you: 

Level 1:  you have no access to options trading on Robinhood. 

Level 2: you have access to Level 2,options but learning the whole options game. Your only experience is you previously bought shares and held them. 

Level 3:  ME: Level 3 options access but Cautiously learning. Mostly covered calls. Looking for semi -safe ways to make some extra money with buying calls. Without YOLOing the retirement account.

If you are Level 4 :  This means, experienced, can read candlestick charts. Can spot a doji from down the street and sometimes get depressed about making 20k in one day because it could have been 40k, and you need help with figuring out where you went wrong. - I have nothing for you except pink horses.  You might as well unfollow me now.  Just being honest.  Not jealous. Hope I will join you one day soon. 

Wait? I thought I told all Level 4 folks to exit a while ago?! Out! Get outta here! 

Oh you You got a thing for pink horses?  Okay cool. No judgment. You can stay 😎

title: Level 1: Homework
body:
This assuming you have no access to options whatsoever 


Like: 

When you buy a stock / fractional shares and look at the highlighted button.  It only says buy and sell.   There is literally no option that says “ trade options “ 

ATTENTION👀
It is my personal opinion that all Level 1 : Robinhood users 
Practice with setting a sell limit order. This is literally what I am teaching my family. 

You want... No... You NEED to know how to trigger sell all shares of a stock when the price per share hits a certain price. 

Your money is precious! You are not rich - Yet.  😎Absolutely Do not go down with a sinking ship! 

Feel free to alter, set your own prices etc

Pics to play with using IAG as an example stock. 

Learn this setting now. Do not be scared of it! Make it your bestie!  Do it at least 5 times!

body:

Why? 

Because you need a steady stream of extra money. 
You are not rich- Yet.
You need extra income…
While you gamble away cash on the market. 

Eventually you may learn you don't have to gamble. 

You will buy better, better blocks of stocks and hold them
They will make you higher and higher monthly streams of income.  
You will get instant rewards that will keep you invested in the market. 

It will be incentive to learn more about stocks.  
It will become less of a gamble and more calculated risk. 

(I think)

This is a necessary skill that will make money when the stock is up AND when the stock is down. 

To sell a covered call: 
you need 100 shares of a stock. 
Hopefully a good one. 
But for now make it one you can afford. 

Make money on it. Continue to work hard.  
Use premium to Add 100 shares to your position 
OR level up to a better stock.
Or for bills and grocery 
Or for gambling on risky trades 
Whatever

body:
Some of those who’ve been following me for a while, will know that after joining this app— With the knowledge gained and insight provided. I made the decision to rearrange my investments portfolio on and off Robinhood. 

Feel free to look at my post history to get details. Or you can ask at any point. I try answer all questions if tagged. 

I closed out my investments on stockpile completely. 

That cash will be going to my long-term investments on Fidelity . 


I have since met with a Fidelity representative in person. 

Will be taking many of the stagnant, uninvested IRAs from previous employment and rolling it into one active IRA 

Because of income limits I do not qualify for Roth. Not bragging just being honest in case everybody suggest a ROTH to me on here. 🤣

Opened up a traditional IRA with Fidelity combining all the previous random coins in one. I plan to contribute to that Fidelity account regularly. That will hold more of my stable boring set it and forget it investments. My ETFs, as well as crypto that I plan on sitting on and forgetting about. 

Fidelity rearrangement is a 3 to 5 day process.


In the meantime, I wanted to catch the tax break and max out my IRA for 2024. So I decided to import 7K  over a 2-3 day period into an IRA on Robinhood. The match is nice! 

Not me cheating or covering up Losses. Just me trying to stash cash in an IRA to catch tax advantages of this year before Dec31.

title: JKatniss: My overall crypto strategy
body:
Another super late update I know . Was exhausted last night. 

⭐️Level 1: JKATNISS : My Crypto strategy:

I am a big fan of KISS.   Not the band. I like them too but the saying “Keep It Simple Stupid“

When it is getting confusing, scary, lots of indecision. I usually err on the side of whatever keeps things simple and makes sense.  

This thought process has taken me far in my life. Not going to abandon it now - So

1. 
Following @mastergroove:  Why?  He Signals crypto trades every day and often. Makes big profit . Makes small profit. Makes and Posts losses. Yeah he is A bit aggressive . A bit flashy. But I like that . I need that energy.  I’m scared money by nature.  

But More Importantly:  He has enough trades where I can pick and choose. which ones I want to follow. For me this is important while learning. I have a busy schedule and I can’t follow every trade. In fact, I worry that I may miss signals. So traders need to be frequent to be a good fit for me. I want to be able to hop on and hop off like tour bus and still get to where Im going 🤑


2.
Signed up for BloFin: I did  this not just  because a mastergroove is using this. But reportedly this is the only site that Americans can use without something called KYC, VPN. One of the few sites that you can use leverage as American. Twice profit but also twice losses.  Gambling I know.  Choose wisely. 

3. transferred 2k money over to BloFin via Robinhood. 
Deposited- bought Solarium- Used Solarium button under Solarium to send to Blofin .   

Coinbase is still super confusing to me. I don’t even check on  $Kekius Maximus. Every day because it is painful process. Also it seems coinbase takes a significant amount of fees to transfer. Robinhood was smooth claims “no fee”and after securing your account with email, government ID and a two factor passcode. It was super simple to move money over to BloFin was there instantly. I did 1K at a time. No, I don’t have a referral link. No I do not work for Robin Hood No  I don’t take tips. I’m just being honest.


4. I used solarium to transfer. Apparently you could transfer $BTC and $ETH on Blofin . But those two I consider more like assets. I don’t wanna mess with them too much.
5. BloFin offers true copy trading. Like literally you give a trader  money and they trade it for you. I know I’m on this AfterHour app but the BloFin concept was amazing. Of course traders have Records. There’s no such thing as a perfect trader. They receive a 10% commission. There’s no guarantee they won’t blow your account.


6. 1k will be divided up amongst two copy traders. 500 each.


7. 1K  will be following master groove on a few of his crypto trades that I understand have time to follow signals on.  I can’t follow every trade. 


8. Exit strategy:  COPY TRADER: 1k if recovered. Will take those profits immediately.  The rest can stay and i will see how far I grow. Maybe will take 10% every profitable trade?  MasterGroove: starting with 1k. Same thing. Will take 10% profits if and when it come.  


Trying hard to keep a running list of YT videos I found helpful in this space.  So many good ones.  But if you want a specific topic just ask. I watch a little bit of everything. The good ones i watch twice. 

Questions ?Comments? Criticisms? Just tag me. I do my best to respond on to them all. Eventually.

title: JKatniss crypto journey Update
body:
⭐️Level 1: JKATNISS : Keeping myself honest 

As an update- 

Spent my entire day figuring out how to change Sol to USDT and selecting a master trader .  

Soo embarrassing.  It should NOT have taken that long. Learning a new platform is brutal if this is not second nature.  

Soo that is exactly why im investing time in now so I can move quickly in the future. 

It’s probably easier for people who live in this world. Im sure high schoolers are laughing at this —But for an outsider this stuff is confusing!! 

Anyhow will out line a few steps just in case people want to bookmark this post . Focus will be on the stuff people think is obvious but I had no idea. 

1.  To move money from Robinhood to Blofin you must use crypto. It seems $BTC, $ETH and $Sol are popular— remember crypto has an electronic signature. So you can follow it if it goes to the wrong wallet.  ( Im sure this will be a budding field in criminology). 

1. Once received in Solarium - in the Funding portion of your wallet. Even though it says USDT-  it is still solarium.  Just like solarium in robinhood the price will continue to fluctuate with the “share “ price. — So if solarium is going down- it will literally continue to decline in value after transfer. 😭

2..To select a master trader or fund your futures account- you must change sol to usdt.  

3.This involves- moving sol to the “spot” portion of your wallet - while in spot selling your sol —by selecting the sol/usdt — into usdt. — then you can move the usdt into futures ( for leverage trading)— or spot ( for 1:1 trading that only bets if the market will go up). —or earn ( where you can sit the cash to earn interest) 

4. To select a master trader - you must have $BTC, $ETH or $USDT.

5. You can only select ONE master trader to copy trade.  You will be prompted to exit out of your previous selection if try to select more than one — So because of this ended up putting my entire 1 k with one carefully selected master trader. 

6.  My other 1 k i moved to Earn to gain interest as i get ready for crypto plays with @mastergroove. 

7. Sidenote: Blofin offers lots of “rewards “ for moving money over BUT i think to get them- your crypto must be changed over to USdT.. which I think I missed out on because i didn’t switch it fast enough. 

Phew! 

Pics are of a few key decision points. :  

Oh Almost forgot!  My Master trader!! The point of doing all this!!!🤣

The master trader selection criteria is  a bit more complicated than it looks.  Lots of criteria to consider. Again- great you tube videos on this. 

There was one that used a Trump meme as well as a Biden meme. I thought it would be nice to pick both but again you are allowed only one.  

The Biden one had better stats.  

Of course there were other more serious criteria than pictures 🤣.  But thought that was hilarious.  

No I will not order a recount. 

Will pause there to answer any questions.

body:
⭐️Level 1: JKATNISS : Progress

Im feeling pretty good. 

Dare i say confident .

This Post here showing i (FINALLY) understand the settings on Blofin.  AND So now I can accurately follow the trades.  

I hear ya laughing.  Took me long enough right?   Its all good.  Horse hair. Dont care. 

This is literally like learning a foreign language. I have had submit myself to total immersion. 

I just want to say 

Thank Goodness $BTC is projected to decline. 🙏🏾This gives me a little extra practice time. I truly consider a blessing from up above so I can get my act together.  Todays curses are preparing you for tomorrows blessings. 

Numbered pic: Signal interpretation 

1.  Buy ( Long) the coin $Sui. Which is attached to “tether” that is USDT.  (This is the only pair you can trade crypto with on BloFin). because this is a “long” position, this means he believes the price will go up and we’re betting on that movement.  You can also short the position this is kind of like a put where you believe the price or movement will go down.


2. He wants to make an entry point at current market (CM) price 5.1342. He wants to bet a margin of $730 at this point


3. AND 4.  Three and four are also entry points and the margins amount of money to be placed are listed.

5. He has a stop loss at the share price of 4.76. Once I set this. If the share price falls to this amount, BloFin will trigger a sale market order.

6. Proof of my own desperation that I had no idea of what he was talking about on this day.  But times are a changing!! 

Okay now for the App: 💪🏻


A. This is from the demo trading app feature. It is showing that I’m using Ethereum with USDT tether.  I have a cross margin selected, (. but I am aware that it might be better for me to change this to isolated margin so that way if I get liquidated, it will only liquidate this position and not all my other positions or my entire account. ). I have it currently set at 3X leverage and I’m where it can change. ( I plan to keep this less than 3X in the beginning.) 


B. Is  where I can place the amount or margin I want to bet with. I can also use the slider function to designate the percentage of money in my account I want to use. For now, I will just use $100 at a time.

C. TP/SL. Is where I can set my take profit and stop loss. I am aware that I can set this after the trade is made as well.

D. Is. the estimated liquidation share/coin price this is the number or value the coin has to get to it which point it would liquidate my entire account at the settings above 

E. This is where my current open positions. Will be found, and the status

F. Close  -  is where I would close the position/exit the position if I wanted to manually. I can also exit percentages of the position.

G. Is the current market price for the tether coin pair above.  Above are all the ask prices for long contracts populating and below are all the short prices or contracts populating. 

H. At the very top is the funding amount. This is a fee that fluctuates every several hours and can make holding contracts pricey if it is significant.

title: Remedial trading lessons? Tuition assignment? Anyone? 🤚
body:
Oh dont worry if you could not make the class  this week! 

I was there.  I took notes. 

Lets tally up my trading school tuition, shall we?

Experience:  $TSLA call 
Tuition: $88
Lessons: 
1. OTM calls are quite the longshot. Buy ITM calls Yes they are more pricey but so is tuition. If you cant afford ITM calls - buy fractional shares and popcorn. Watch from the sidelines 
2. Delta doesn’t lie . 0.7 or greater for buying a call.
3. Expiring worthless means just that- Do not waste time on any thing else.  You can not sell to close. You will not be able to roll the position down, up or sideways because no one will buy it from you. You are better off just starting over and buying an entirely new call. 
4. Tesla stock not invincible - Tax harvesting is kryptonite for all super heroes. Beware December. 

Experience: Copy Trading 
Tuition: $394.98 -ongoing 
Lesson: 
1. Thou shalt Follow the rules for the selection of copy trading or suffer complete and utter port liquidation 

(So have you ever argued with someone who was giving you excellent advice about copy trading.  You ignored that advice IN ADDITION TO other advice you have spent precious time accumulating from knowledgeable you tube gurus. Then the very same day a copy trader liquidates your account because you chose to ignore all the red flags? Have any of you done this? 

Well I have. ) 

Thank goodness for isolated mode not cross.  
Thank you @average_advisor  For your words of wisdom. Although ignored. They were heard. 

This was NOT @mastergroove.

trading more than 30 days
PL ratio greater than > 1:1

Keep those dogies rollin…

Wanted to share what bad money management looks like. 😇

I started a new job in the Fall of 2024.  It pays less but benefits are better and I am closer to home to my kiddos. So super grateful 🤗

Anyhow made a staggering error filling out my tax information. I requested additional Taxes To be taken out as if I was still getting paid monthly. But in reality, I went to a biweekly check😧

One does not need to know the mathematical specifics of how disastrous this can be to an income 🙃

Yes, I am just now realizing this ! even after working this job for several months. Because I try to live way below my means and I usually keep a good bit of cushion around in my account. 🥴

title: Covered calls on red days :Teaching points
body:
Remember when I sell covered calls on my  hundred shares “ponies “.  I  get the premium instantly. It’s already gone and spent. I use the premiums to buy more shares or save up in an ETF to enter into a call on this account.

🤑As long as your selecting covered, call premiums of pretty low  deltas- you’re covered calls will likely expire out of the money. They are rarely exercised early if ITM. Trust Theta to dip them for you. Make Theta your bestie 

💰Consider these mindsets and find the one that works for you:

You keep the premiums and you keep your shares.
You’re getting paid to babysit stocks
You’re putting your ponies to work for you to generate an income that you can use as you wish.

💚 ☀️💚
Red days become green days for you.
Literally, you’re watching all the people lose money on their contracts
You become the casino, the house. 

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Donate all my  tips to @stonkenstein .  Tell him to consider a covered call strategy. Tell him there’s nothing wrong with bag holding and that he should get some sleep .

title: When do I roll? @SCHC
body:
⭐️The answer is simple: ⭐️

👀The current price of the covered contract has decreased beyond what I received for it 

👉Column A is much less than column B 


🤑Remember i have already received the premium. It has been spent and long gone. I don’t have to give it back. 

💰Its time to go looking for new money.

Here is ChatGPT’s explanation of the term, death cross below👇

The death cross is a technical analysis indicator used in financial markets to signal a potential major downtrend in the price of an asset (like a stock, index, or cryptocurrency).

Here's what it is:
A death cross occurs when the short-term moving average (usually the 50-day moving average) crosses below the long-term moving average (typically the 200-day moving average).

Why it matters:

* It suggests that momentum is weakening.
* Traders and investors often view it as a bearish signal, indicating a possible prolonged decline.

Yes, **Nvidia** does have parts of its **supply chain connected to China**, though it designs its chips in the U.S.

Here’s a breakdown:

### 1. **Manufacturing & Assembly**
- Nvidia outsources **manufacturing** of its chips to companies like **TSMC** (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company), but many **components, assembly, packaging, and testing** are handled by contractors with operations in **mainland China**.

### 2. **Component Suppliers**
- Some of the materials and parts used in Nvidia’s products come from **Chinese suppliers** or are processed in Chinese facilities, especially for things like printed circuit boards (PCBs), capacitors, and other electronic components.

### 3. **Revenue Dependence**
- Nvidia earns a **significant portion of revenue from China**. In fiscal 2023, **more than 20%** of Nvidia’s total revenue came from Chinese customers — including large firms like Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu.

### 4. **Geopolitical Impact**
- U.S. restrictions on high-end chip exports to China (especially for AI and data center chips) have directly affected Nvidia, which has led it to **develop modified chips** that meet export compliance rules while still serving the Chinese market.

So, while Nvidia isn't a traditional manufacturer based in China, it **relies on Chinese suppliers and contractors**, and China remains a **critical market** in its global strategy.

title: For @huskerpotato : My covered call strategy
body:
So in brief cover calls are a great safe strategy to have in the market. 

If you have 100 shares of a stock, you can sell a covered call. 


You can do this for two reasons.

1) part of the wheel strategy: in which you’re trying to sell your shares for a little bit more than what you got them and you don’t mind losing them. I either contract being exercised. Because you’re going to take the money and use that to sell a cash cover put.

2) to earn weekly or monthly or quarterly, passive income on shares you want to keep. (I.e. to make babysitting money off watching a sibling when you had to stay home anyway.)

🤪It sounds like husker you want to do number two.  (Ewww gross🤣🤣 sorry for the weird jokes. I have young kids.)


🧐So sidenote, remember you don’t have to sell cover calls on all of your shares. Cause it sounds like you have 500 $ INTC. You can do one contract or five contracts

👀Looking very briefly, though, the market is a little bit green today. So this might be a good time to sell a quick covered call because we cannot guarantee it will look like that all this week with the current political climate. 

For number 2) 💩. just make sure your Delta’s are less than 0.4., And make sure that you’re selling at least two weeks out. When things settle down, I would do more 30 to 45 day covered calls. But right now the market I feel is too volatile for that. Just check on them every week if you can. To be honest and Angel make slightly more money, but it is slightly more work.

I put an example of a covered call based on today’s rates. 

👀Take a look at that one and look around. I used arrows to indicate the important things. 

⚠️Make sure you’re selling a call not buying a call.


 📖Check the date to expiration. You want at least two weeks if not 30 days. 


💰The premium you get will be instant. Once you agreed to sell. 

I think $INTC is at low risk of being exercised early. The chip makers are going to have a tough time with Chinese tariffs on the horizon. That’s why the price is dropping. Also if you stay within the two week window that will likely serve you well , cause most people don’t exercise their contracts two weeks early.

😎So don’t worry if the share price rises into the money like up towards $20 and hovers there for a bit. Likely it will just drop back down before date of expiration. If it’s getting close to date of expiration just roll the call up like to a share price of 22 or $23 and then out another two weeks. We can talk about that later.

I will probably roll some of my calls today actually. But just trying to see what happens at the end of the day with this market. I’ve got new covered calls. I need to place on some of my other stocks as well. So I expect some money coming in not as much as $INTC but hey, it’s something.

title: Rolling a covered call: green means go:$RIOT
body:
@huskerpotato

Here is a quick example in rolling calls. Using $RIOT.

Right now under these market conditions I like to keep my covered calls within 14 days. 

That way, I really don’t have to worry about my calls being exercised early. They’re greater than seven days away from my DTE. 

I am collecting premium every week, and stashing that to buy some more shares( $SQQQ )i.e. increasing my positions 

$SQQQ-is inverse leverage. So on a market Green Day it will appear as if I’m losing money. Which is fine with me.

I just want the money to grow on a market red day so that I could use the capital plus gains to buy a beer position in shares that I want on a dip. 


1) ✅when you’re covered call contracts turn green that can be a Go￼signal to roll them. When you’re covered call contract turns green: ￼They’ve lost value and are likely getting out of the money in your favor.

2) 🤔if you want, you can wait a little longer like until they’ve lost 50% of their value or until they turn green with a -50.

3) 💰for me I just make sure that they are green just enough, or lost enough value so that when I roll them for a Delta of .4 or less on receiving some profits. I’m not really greedy in this market. Remember, I get another chance to roll them next week

title: “If you’re not cheating, then you’re not trying “
body:
(I Will be in the chat this evening 2300 EST to discuss )

5 Famous Gamblers 
5 Famous World Leaders
One Question 

😱 not going to lie; the first time I heard this advice, 

  “If you’re not cheating, then you’re not trying”

I was appalled.

I do not advocate cheating 👎

🤔But life experiences have made me do a full 180°. 

😎I regularly use this phrase around my kids.

Why?

👶If you enter an arena where money, time, or goods are being exchanged AND are not well aware of all the ways manipulation may occur - you will lose. 

💯My kids need to understand this

ignorance of cheating = ignorance winning 

👂 I hear ya. I hear ya. Gambling and investing are different breeds.

😏but they share a bloodline when you look closely. They speak a similar language.  👇By Comparing the two, I am not trying to take down investing, but to elevate the science behind gambling.

BOTH involve extensive research, strategy, speculation, and sometimes... a little cheating. 

❓Now for the $6.6 trillion dollar question❓

🌟Is this presidential-level manipulation?🌟

😈Has the oval office become the podium for Gambling with the economy

Or

🌟Is this an admirable administrative achievement ?🌟

😇The executive branch is trying to win a cutthroat global game for the American people. 
💪

Here are five notorious cheating scandals from across the gambling world—and how they mirror both investment psychology and market manipulation by world leaders.

  TLDR: Is it cheating or is it trying to win?

---
🏇. The Fine Cotton Horse Racing Scam (Australia, 1984)🏇

👀What happened👀 

A syndicate of bettors led by John Gillespie substituted a faster horse—Bold Personality— instead of the slow-performing Fine Cotton in a race at Eagle Farm Racecourse. They dyed the horse’s coat and even tried to paint its legs to complete the disguise.

😮The catch😮

The paint ran during the race, and insiders noticed something off. Rumors exploded as betting surged on the long shot. The plot unraveled within hours.

🌪️The aftermath🌪️   

Multiple racing officials were banned for life. This scandal shocked the Australian racing world and highlighted how insider knowledge can sway betting markets, much like insider trading can rock stock markets.

The Fine Cotton ring-in racing scandal cost Wendy her career, but she's bounced back - ABC News
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-19/fine-cotton-racing-scandal-dig-podcast/100899712

---

🦋🐝2. Sonny Liston and the Phantom Punch (USA, 1965)🐝🦋

👀What happened👀  

In one of boxing’s most debated moments, Muhammad Ali (then Cassius Clay) knocked out Sonny Liston with what appeared to be a barely visible punch just 1:44 into the first round.

😮The catch😮

Conspiracy theories spread like wildfire. Some believed Liston took a dive to settle mob debts or to avoid FBI scrutiny. Others blamed fear of Ali’s association with the Nation of Islam.

🌪️The aftermath🌪️  

 No charges were ever filed, but the controversy lives on in boxing lore. It’s a classic example of perceived manipulation shaking public trust—something also familiar to investors watching flash crashes or suspicious stock halts.

Hauser, Thomas. Muhammad Ali: His Life and Times, Simon & Schuster, 1991.

---

⚾3. The Black Sox Scandal (USA, 1919)⚾

👀What happened👀 

Eight players from the Chicago White Sox were accused of accepting money from gamblers—most famously Arnold Rothstein—to throw the World Series against the Cincinnati Reds.

😮The catch😮

They intentionally made errors, struck out, and botched plays in exchange for cash.

🌪️The aftermath🌪️  

Though acquitted in court, all eight were banned for life from Major League Baseball. This scandal triggered the appointment of baseball’s first commissioner, Kenesaw Mountain Landis, to clean up the sport.

Asinof, Eliot. *Eight Men Out: The Black Sox and the 1919 World Series*, Henry Holt & Co, 1963.ff

---

♣️♦️4. The MIT Blackjack Team (USA, 1980s–2000s)♦️♣️

👀What happened👀 

A group of students and graduates from MIT, Harvard, and other top universities formed a secret blackjack team using card counting and team play to beat casinos at their own game.

😮The catch😮

They weren’t breaking laws—but they were exploiting a mathematical edge in ways casinos hadn’t anticipated.

🌪️The aftermath🌪️  

Casinos banned team members, shuffled decks more often, and implemented facial recognition. Their story was immortalized in the book Bringing Down the House and the film 21.

Mezrich, Ben. Bringing Down the House. Free Press, 2002.

---

🐶5. Greyhound Doping in the UK (1970s) 🐶

👀What happened👀
Trainers in the UK were found drugging racing dogs—either to enhance performance or sabotage favored competitors. 

😮The catch😮

sedatives were used to ensure long shots could win and deliver major payoffs for select bettors.

🌪️The aftermath🌪️  

Regulatory authorities implemented random drug testingand disqualified dogs and trainers caught cheating. As in horse racing, the pursuit of quick profit through manipulationechoes the pitfalls of unethical trading in financial markets.

British Greyhound Racing Board Reports; The Guardian, “Greyhound racing rocked by doping,” 1975.

---

🌎How World Leaders Have Manipulated the Markets🌏

Just like in gambling, even entire economies have been "rigged" by the powerful.

🇮🇹1. Mussolini and the Overvalued Lira🇮🇹

In the 1920s, Italian dictator Benito Mussolini artificially supported the lira’s exchange rate at “Quota 90,” buying up lira with gold and reserves to boost national pride. It worked short-term—but it destroyed competitiveness and triggered inflation later.

De Cecco, Marcello. *The Lira and the Dollar: Stability and Inflation in Italy and the USA*, Cambridge University Press, 1974.

---

🇷🇺2. Stalin’s Market Manipulation 🇷🇺

Joseph Stalin falsified economic output and manipulated grain exports to industrialize Russia—leading to the 1932–33 Holodomor famine. He deliberately underreported shortages to maintain export deals.

Applebaum, Anne. Red Famine: Stalin’s War on Ukraine, Doubleday, 2017.

---

🇩🇪3. Hitler’s Shadow Currency🇩🇪

Adolf Hitler used MEFO bills, a secret credit instrument to finance Germany’s rearmament off-budget. It delayed inflation and let Germany rearm in secret without alerting global creditors.

Tooze, Adam. The Wages of Destruction: The Making and Breaking of the Nazi Economy, Penguin, 2006.

---

🇵🇭4. Ferdinand Marcos and Crony Capitalism🇵🇭

Philippine dictator Ferdinand Marcos manipulated stock markets and issued sovereign bonds while channeling money to cronies. Billions were siphoned from the treasury under the guise of national growth.

Bello, Walden. Development Debacle: The World Bank in the Philippines, Institute for Food and Development Policy, 1982.

---

 🇨🇳 5. China’s 2015 Market Crash 🇨🇳

During the 2015 crash, China banned large shareholders from selling stocks, froze trading on hundreds of companies, and ordered state-backed firms to buy up the market. The result? A temporary recovery. followed by deeper distrust.

Bloomberg News, “China Intervenes in Stock Market,” July 2015; Wall Street Journal, Inside China’s Stock Market Rescue,” 2015.

---

🌟So what do you think? 🌟

Is this cheating😈 
or is this trying 😇.

This Friday he had epiphany about some “real talk.”

If this is a popularity contest I want him to win for just one day.

Give him a tip and welcome him to the dysfunctional. AfterHour family 🤗

body:
Do you see how I’ve selected the call. 

And the Greeks are available. Remember these can dramatically change. Once market opens. They can change for the better and they can change for the worse.😬

That’s why many traders just wait until 30 minutes after market opens.

In the box with the white arrow. You can select a bid price. Robin Hood will stick with that. 

You can also set a trigger limit.- upper right hand corner.

remember, you can only buy and sell whole shares on the 24 hour market. 
M
This option order even if I had enough money in my account would be just queued for market open. 

So it just sit and wait until someone picks up the contract at market open

Depending on the conditions at market open, no one may pick up the contract at which point it’ll be in the pending spot. You can always just click on it and keep changing your bid price marked with the arrow.

It will fluctuate because things are fluctuating. Just think about a crowded trading floor. People are constantly making bids and buys. So there’s no guarantee the range will stay still. It will literally be flipping before your very eyes. Like it’s final destination airline tracker or something.


💫 if this is a lot of money for you. And you’re scared of this order. Maybe practice with a smaller contract setting a buy and sell limit after hours and seeing how it execute. Tesla is super volatile on a normal day. Now they’re coming up on earnings . So those there is no guarantee you’re going to get that order. It literally will be chaos. It will be like asking your mom to sign a permission slip for a field trip while she’s getting six kids ready in the morning. You’re probably should’ve asked Friday afternoon.😂

🤨Now remember the special thing about Tesla is that it has a high options volume. So you can be picky about your sale and bid limit orders within range. That’s why some people like to only trade things with a high volume.

Things with a lower volume let’s say $LUCID, have “wide bid ask spreads”. So you’re not guaranteed to get the exact price that you’re trying to aim for.

title: 🍍AH Degenerate Lessons I have learned: swinging🍍
body:
A word to the wise. And the broke😎 

👶When I first got on AfterHour. I was super cautious and looking for a way to make money quickly for family. 

👵Yes that really hasn’t changed but hear me out.

🪙This type of thinking inevitably lead you to the penny stocks. 

🤗Not hating on other people strategies. I think at @gorillagang does an excellent job with penny stock shot outs 

Warning

‼️ However, if you have a level one Robin Hood account. You’ve probably recognize that you will be hit with a pattern day trading warning if you engage in this. 

‼️Another negative is that you must watch the stock very closely and be ready for when it dumps. This may be hard to do if you have obligations outside of AfterHour. 

‼️Lastly, you may not be really learning a lot about long-term companies and investing. Remember overtime, every trading strategy loses. ETF and index funds are usually the way to go.😔

🤔So those following me on my J KATNISS contest challenge may recognize. To “double the money” I did NOT do any penny stocks.

I intentionally selected large, familiar companies for swinging shares. 

Why ? To demonstrate the lessons below. 
￼

👉 You don’t have to worry about pricey options that might go to zero. You don’t have to worry about fighting with theta. You can hold the shares as long as you want. 

👉Note most mag seven stocks even in this market. Will not dump into fractions of a dollar. Penny stocks can, and they will .You can sleep at night, even in this crazy bear market knowing.

👉 Even if they drop 5% or greater, it likely is not for very for long so even if the share price is not moving your favor. You can always retrieve your money and know that there is some left. 

👉There is more data released about the company that could be influencing Price action. Helps guide you on if it will pop or dump. News releases, earnings, politics, sector changes, federal decisions.   Whereas trading penny stocks you’re usually going in blind and just guessing.

👉 please consider this as a safe way to play earnings. Just put money in at the dip and then ride the wave to whenever you feel comfortable.

Anyhow. I don’t think Tesla will dump much today. 

You can always set a stop loss the day after and just ride the pump until it drops below a certain level. Remember setting a stop loss on the same day may trigger a PDT flag as well. 

I included pics of how my swing plays doing.

🥰10% gain is looking pretty sweet. But it seems a lot of people like a 20 or 30% gain for Plays. Tesla is pretty volatile and it might get there. I will signal an exit. But feel free to bail out on Tesla whenever you want.

But lots of mag seven stocks may only get you 5 to 10% pop on their best day. Still I’m hopeful😇

⭐️1. Raw Material Sourcing
* Silicone/TPU: Sourced from chemical manufacturers (e.g., in China, Germany, or the U.S.) for body-safe, hypoallergenic external materials.
* Lithium-ion Battery: From battery suppliers (e.g., Panasonic, BYD) often in China or South Korea.
* PCB & Microchips: Designed by electronics engineers, manufactured by fabs like TSMC or Foxconn, often in Taiwan or China.
* Electric Motors: Micro-motors from manufacturers like Mabuchi Motor (Japan) or OEM factories in Shenzhen.

⭐️2. Component Manufacturing
* Injection Molding: Silicone or plastic casings are shaped using molds, typically in Chinese or Vietnamese factories.
* Circuit Board Assembly: SMT (surface-mount technology) factories assemble the control board with microcontrollers and Bluetooth chips.
* Battery Packs: Assembled separately and tested for safety compliance (with USB-C or magnetic charging interfaces).

⭐️3. Product Assembly
* Final Assembly Plant: Components are sent to an assembly facility (often in China, Malaysia, or Mexico), where:
    * The motor is embedded into the molded casing.
    * The circuit board is installed and connected to the power system.
    * The product is sealed to meet waterproof or hygienic standards (IPX7 or higher).

 ⭐️4. Quality Control & Testing
* Units go through vibration testing, waterproofing checks, battery safety protocols, and software QA if app-controlled.

⭐️5. Packaging & Branding
* Packaging designed in U.S./Europe, manufactured in China or India.
* Manuals printed, devices branded (with logos or engravings), and boxed.

⭐️6. Global Shipping & Distribution
* Products are shipped via ocean freight to distribution centers (e.g., in Los Angeles, Rotterdam, or Hamburg).
* Distributed through:
    * Online retailers (Amazon, Lovehoney, etc.)
    * Adult boutiques or specialty stores
    * Direct-to-consumer via brand websites

⭐️7. Retail & Customer Support
* End user receives product.
* Support for charging, warranty claims, and app integration managed via service teams (often outsourced to Philippines or India)

title: BTC CC on $IAG: Advice from The gambler.
body:
So here is a real life example of when I like to to buy. back my covered calls.

💰I use covered calls as babysitting money on shares I don’t ever want to sell. They gave me premium and I put that premium to work buying more shares. That way I can grow my portfolio without adding money.

🥳So when my covered calls get cheap. As in 87% off or in the green on Robin Hood. I go ahead and buy them back. 

👉 this will make you more money over the life of your share ownership overtime instead of just waiting till expiration.


🤑And then I replace them for more premium. 

👉This usually happens when the underlying stock drops in share price. 

👉The drop and share price does not bother me at all. Because I own things I know will rise again. It’s just Mr. market being silly as WTF would say , so you might as well just make money on it. 

👀If this holds through the night. I will probably buy back this cc in the morning. And wait a day or so before placing another covered. Call on it. Likely for the same date, but maybe a different strike price. Just to continue to get premium.


👉Gambling advice is very good advice for investments even if you’re not a gambler like me.. Just ask 😎Kenny Rogers.

Covered call TLDR: KNOW when to hold them , KNOW when to roll them

🚫 no tippy tippy!! 🚫

🚩8 red flags that indicate a meme coin rug pull🚩

 1. No Lock on Liquidity✅

👉 Red Flag: If the token’s liquidity is not locked, the developers can remove all funds at any time.

👉 How to Check: Use tools like Unicrypt or Team Finance to verify if liquidity is locked.

2. Anonymous or Unverifiable Team✅

👉 Red Flag: No public faces, fake names, or team members with no verifiable history.

👉 How to Check: Look for LinkedIn profiles or track past projects; be cautious with teams that use only Telegram or Discord.

3. Suspicious Tokenomics ✅

👉 Red Flag: The devs or insiders hold a large % of the total supply (e.g., 50%+).

👉 How to Check: Use Etherscan, BSCScan, or DexTools to check the top wallet holders.. Meteora wallet holders-32%


4. Hardcoded or Disabling Functions❓

👉 Red Flag: Smart contracts allow for minting more tokens, disabling trading, or blacklisting wallets.

👉 How to Check: Use TokenSniffer, GoPlus Security, or Coinscope to scan the contract for risky functions.

5. Overhyped Marketing & Lack of Utility❓

👉 Red Flag: Flashy promises, aggressive Telegram shilling, no real product or roadmap.

👉 How to Spot: Evaluate whether there's a real-world use case or if it's just meme-driven hype.


6. Unverified or Suspicious Contract ❓

👉 Red Flag: The smart contract is not verified on the blockchain explorer.

👉 How to Check: Verified contracts have readable code on Etherscan or BSCScan. Unverified = risk

7. Price Behavior ❓

👉 Red Flag: Huge pump with no retrace, then flatlining. It’s usually artificial or dev-controlled.

👉 Tool to Use: Check trading volume on DexTools. Look out for one-sided trades and no real buyer activity

8. Limited or Disabled Sell Function❓

👉Red Flag: You can buy, but you can’t sell — or selling has massive slippage or tax (like 50%+).

👉How to Test: Try a small sell. If it's blocked or results in a tiny return, it’s likely a honeypot.

Boomer definitions here👇

🚓“To pop a cap in someone” is a slang term made popular in action movies and hip-hop, meaning to shoot someone with a firearm—usually with dramatic flair. 

📈In investing, a stock “popping its cap” isn’t quite as lethal, but it’s just as explosive: when we say a stock “broke its market cap,” we’re talking about a massive surge in value that pushes the total worth of the company to a record high. It's the corporate equivalent of blowing the roof off.


What Does It Mean When a Stock Breaks Its Market Cap?

🤓A stock "breaking its market cap" typically means the company’s total market value (share price x number of shares) has hit a historic or unexpected high. It's usually fueled by:

* A revolutionary product launch
* Explosive earnings
* Market hype (hello, meme stocks!)
* Strategic deals or acquisitions

🤪It signals confidence, momentum, and sometimes a bit of madness from investors.

🍿Now, let’s bring together three infamous market-cap-busting stocks and three revolutionary movie gunfights that left a similar blast on cinema history.



🔫STOCKS THAT POPPED THEIR CAPS🔫

1. Tesla ($TSLA)

🚙Market Cap Break Moment: In 2020–2021, Tesla shot past a $1 trillion market cap, becoming the first automaker to do so, despite selling far fewer vehicles than competitors. Investors were betting not just on cars, but on Elon Musk’s vision for the future—energy, AI, space... maybe Mars parking lots?

Why It Mattered: It turned the idea of traditional valuation on its head. Tesla wasn't just a car company—it was a cultural icon.

2. Nvidia ($NVDA)

🖥️Market Cap Break Moment: In 2023 and again in 2024, Nvidia broke market cap records by riding the AI boom. With its GPUs powering ChatGPT and every chatbot under the sun, Nvidia’s shares skyrocketed.

Why It Mattered: It cemented the company as the beating heart of the AI revolution, making chips the new oil of the digital age.

3. GameStop ($GME)

🕹️Market Cap Break Moment: 2021’s infamous meme stock frenzy. A wave of Reddit retail traders launched $GME to insane heights, breaking all rational ceilings.

Why It Mattered: It was less about fundamentals and more about rebellion. Wall Street got a slap, and finance met internet culture in a full-blown cinematic moment of its own.


🎬GUNFIGHTS THAT REWROTE THE SCRIPT🎬

1. The Lobby Scene – The Matrix (1999)
🪪Slow motion. Sunglasses. Wall flips. This scene turned bullet time into cinema gold. Neo and Trinity’s shootout redefined action choreography and digital effects for decades to come.


Stock Equivalent: Nvidia. Both made the future look cool—and made everyone else scramble to catch up.

2. The Bank Robbery – Heat (1995)
🏦When Robert De Niro’s crew exits the bank and all hell breaks loose in the streets of L.A., the gunfight feels real, raw, and terrifying. It's studied by real-life tactical teams for its realism.

Stock Equivalent: Tesla. Nobody expected an electric car company to dominate so hard—just like no one expected that level of realism in a Hollywood gunfight.

3. The Saloon Shootout – The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)

🤠This classic standoff scene gave us close-ups, tension, and the quiet-before-the-bang pacing that every Western has tried to copy since.

Stock Equivalent: GameStop. It was all about the stare-down between Reddit and Wall Street, ending in a bang that echoed through time.

Wrapping It Up
🙌Stocks and film have a lot in common. 

🏛️Both deliver spectacle, tension, and a storyline worth watching. 

TLDR: just remember: when a stock “pops its cap,” it’s not about violence—it’s about volume, vision, and a whole lot of investor driven momentum.

title: For @theirn : Back taxes🤣
body:
The Boston Tea Party — Quick Overview

On December 16, 1773, American colonists (the Sons of Liberty) dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor in protest of the British Tea Act. This event involved tea owned by the British East India Company.

Step 1: Value of the Tea in 1773

Estimates vary, but historians generally agree that the destroyed tea was worth about:

£9,659 sterling in 1773

Equivalent to $1.7 to $2 million in today’s U.S. dollars when adjusted for commodity value and inflation

Step 2: Tea Tax Rate
Under the Tea Act of 1773, the tax was 3 pence per pound of tea.

Let’s estimate:

Each chest had ~90 lbs of tea → 342 chests × 90 lbs = 30,780 lbs

Tax at 3 pence per pound = 92,340 pence = 3,847.5 pounds sterling in 1773

Step 3: Convert to Present-Day USD

To convert £3,847.50 (tax loss) in 1773 into 2025 U.S. dollars:

Using historical economic multipliers like inflation, wage value, and GDP share, we get a wide range.

The most relevant estimate (commodity-based or income value): ~$1.2 to $1.5 million USD in back taxes owed in today’s money.

title: Tip 👉 @whataremyoptions : reverse head and shoulders
body:
So in response to a post from @whataremyoptions  

I used a picture and inserted it into ChatGPT and asked if it was a reverse head and shoulders. 

Because I was a little doubtful chat, GPT would be able to determine that the  red crayons are not part of the original picture. I went to Robin Hood to search for a fresh one.

Obviously, the stock had changed. I inserted that picture as well into ChatGPT and asked the question.

Here are the answers for the original picture. 
As well as the refreshed Robin Hood picture that I took. 

👉Picture one:

Looking at the price chart of $NVR from the screenshot over the 5-year period, the portion you've circled shows a rounded top formation—not a reverse head and shoulders.

Here’s why this does not resemble a reverse head and shoulders:

What a Reverse Head and Shoulders Looks Like:
Left shoulder: A drop, followed by a short-term rally.
Head: A deeper drop, followed by a rally.
Right shoulder: A smaller drop (similar in depth to the left shoulder), followed by a breakout.
What This Chart Shows:
The circled area displays a sharp uptrend followed by a clear peak and then a decline—more characteristic of:
A blow-off top, or
A rounded top / distribution phase, which often precedes a bearish trend.

Conclusion:
This is not a reverse head and shoulders.
It looks more like a top-heavy formation, suggesting potential for further downside or consolidation rather than a bullish reversal.

👉Picture two:

Thanks for sharing the updated image. This chart shows the 1-day price action for NVR.

Quick Analysis:
This is intraday movement, and from what’s shown:

There's a sharp rise early in the day, followed by a steep drop.
There's no pattern here resembling a reverse head and shoulders.
Instead, this shape is more indicative of a bull trap or failed rally—often seen when buyers push prices up early, only for it to be sold off quickly.

Conclusion:
No, this is not a reverse head and shoulders. It's just one day of volatile movement, likely reacting to broader market sentiment, earnings, or macro news.

body:
Clint Mansell’s 5:45 length composition of the title sets the mood for me this week.  

🩰The film a personal favorite and very appropriate for those who succumb to a life of options. 

Tips go to: @smartguyac

Poor user is wrestling with the conspiracy that am I bot 

🤔NGL some work days i wrestle with that question too. 

🤗But I appreciate the inspiration to become more concise and mathematical in my posts


🩰Definition of Perfection 👇

Perfect numbers are positive integers that are equal to the sum of their proper divisors (excluding the number itself).

A number n is perfect if:

The sum of its proper divisors = n

Examples:
* 6: Divisors are 1, 2, 3 → 1 + 2 + 3 = 6
* 28: Divisors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 → 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28
* 496, 8128 are the next few perfect numbers

They are rare and get large quickly.😎

👀666 not a perfect number but a humbling following nonetheless. 😉

Did you know ? 

There are no known examples of perfect numbers directly occurring in nature in the same way that, say, Fibonacci numbers or the golden ratio do.

💡So 👉Perfection takes work and sacrifice.

body:
TLDR : Scared of losing money? Swing whole shares on larger companies.  less risk of big losses.

For the broke folks 
This demonstrates why fractional shares can be limiting on RH.

Luckily, this is not a penny stock. Today looks like it may open pretty green. So I’m hoping this will recover by the end of the day. 

Obviously, not losing much money here ($20 fractional shares ) . But the idea of of course, is to gain not to lose. 

As this JKatniss earnings challenge comes to an end .￼

Do your best to trade or swing whole shares not fractional.

￼ anyhow if you’re doing this with stocks on larger market caps. You don’t have to necessarily worry about the stock going to zero like a penny stock. These are bigger companies that have staying power. ￼

title: Hey AH ! : Are side pieces okay? 🤔
body:
🙏Please don’t read too much into this post. 
It’s a gender neutral question. 😎

It’s just- The longer I hang out on AH the more I get curious 🧐.

Who here utlizes inverse shares as a side piece in their financial relationship? 👋 

I know. I know. 

💯Longterm commitment to whole shares is the key to happiness. 

👉Find the right company with a solid background, strengthen your positions during market dips and you will live in bliss when good times come. 👰‍♀️🤵💍💒

😈But what if your shares just aren’t ‘doing it for you’?

🙄Maybe its a red day. Maybe it’s a ridiculous post on X thats got your portfolio all bent out of shape.  Maybe you can’t figure it out,  but the company can’t get its  share price up. Or Maybe you are seeing just one missed earnings after another.

👀Why not slip into an inverse play when things are scary and come back out refreshed on the other side ?


Too risky? Too pricey? 
What could go wrong? 😎

😳 Welp, I have learned Decay is one downside.

Compounding decay (also called volatility drag or daily compounding effect) refers to how leveraged ETFs — especially inverse or 2x/3x funds — can lose value over time even if the underlying index is flat.

Here’s how it works:

Leveraged ETFs reset daily, meaning they aim to match their target return only for one day. Over time, the compounding of daily percentage changes — especially during volatility — can lead to a decay in value, even if the underlying asset hasn’t moved much overall.

Example (Using a -3x ETF like $SQQQ):
Let’s say the Nasdaq-100 moves like this over 2 days:

Day 	Nasdaq-100 Move	SQQQ (-3x) Move
1	            +2%                                 -6%
2	             -2%	                             +6%

If you start with $100 in $SQQQ:

💚After Day 1: $100 → $94
❤️After Day 2: $94 × 1.06 = $99.64

Even though the Nasdaq-100 is back to where it started (net 0%), SQQQ lost money due to compounding.

Key Points:

⚠️The effect worsens with volatility and longer holding periods.
⚠️Works against you in choppy markets — even if your directional bet is correct.
⚠️Best used for short-term trades, not long-term investments.

Well what do you think? 

If you are brave enough to admit to it. Idk Maybe you have an open trading relationship with the market. Post your advice here 👇

Don’t worry! Its AH your secret is safe with us 🤗

title: Yes ! You can get her back 🤗 Wholesome Sat
body:
🥰How to Win Her (or Them) Back: 

Aka - What Rebuilding Love 📈and Brand Loyalty📉 Have in Common

Everyone loves a second chance.

No ! You  don’t need money or the best market indicator. 😇

Let’s take a look at 5 companies that pulled off redemption arcs — and what their journey has in common with famous couples who found their way back to love.😍

💚1. Admit What Went Wrong - Publicly Johnson & Johnson | Justin Timberlake + Jessica Biel

‼️ The Crisis: J&J’s Tylenol scare in 1982 — tampered capsules caused 7 deaths. Trust shattered.

👀The Response: Immediate product recall. Transparent communication. Industry-changing safety reforms.

🥰The Lesson in Love: Justin and Jessica split in 2011 amid rumors and career clashes. Like J&J, he took accountability, adjusted, and re-committed. They married in 2012 and built a strong foundation as parents.

👉Redemption Rule #1: You can’t fix what you don’t acknowledge.

💚2. Do the Work — Not Just the Talk Nike | Pink + Carey Hart

‼️The Crisis: 1990s sweatshop scandals nearly crushed Nike’s reputation.

👀The Response: They invested in ethical practices, opened up their supply chain, and rebuilt trust over time.

🥰The Relationship Parallel: Pink and Carey separated in 2008. Instead of walking away, they both did the work — including therapy — and came back stronger in 2010.

👉Redemption Rule #2: Real change means effort. Words are empty without action.

💚3. Offer a Real Solution — Not Just an Apology Apple | Dwyane Wade + Gabrielle Union

‼️The Crisis: iPhone 4’s “Antennagate” dropped calls and customer confidence.

👀The Response: Apple gave out free bumper cases and addressed the problem publicly — owning the narrative.

🥰Relationship Parallel: Dwyane had a child outside the relationship. Instead of hiding, he faced it. Gabrielle forgave, they married in 2014, and became a symbol of mature, honest love.

👉 Redemption Rule #3: Don’t just say “I’m sorry” — show you’ve solved the problem

💚4. Give It Time — and Show You’ve Grown Toyota | Miley Cyrus + Liam Hemsworth

‼️The Crisis: A massive 9-million car recall due to unintended acceleration.

👀The Response: Toyota revamped its entire safety system and weathered the storm.

🥰The Love Story: Miley and Liam first fell in love in 2009, broke up multiple times, and spent years apart. After personal growth and reflection, they reunited and married in 2018. Though the marriage didn’t last, their reconnection showed maturity and healing.

👉Redemption Rule #4: Sometimes the only fix is time, self-work, and evolution — even if the final outcome isn’t forever.

💚5. Win Back Trust, One Small Step at a Time Chipotle | Chrissy Teigen + John Legend

‼️The Crisis: E. coli outbreaks in 2015 wrecked Chipotle’s reputation and sales.

👀The Response: New food safety protocols, digital ordering upgrades, and consistent transparency brought customers back.

🥰The Relationship Parallel: Chrissy and John had an early breakup. But they reconnected quickly, built something real, and became everyone's #RelationshipGoals.

👉Redemption Rule #5: Rebuilding trust isn’t one big moment — it’s many small ones done right.

🤙The Bottom Line: Redemption is Earned, Not Given

So AH Fellas 📣

Whether  it is a misplaced  W instead of an L,  

you forgotten who actually had the gag reflex and who didn’t 

or you have let the side piece stay overnight one to many times bringing the entire port down . 

You have to have 👇 Accountability. 
Transparency. 
Effort. 
Consistency.
 Yep That’s the blueprint. 
That’s how you get another chance — and make it count.💪🏻

Tips to @mphinance  for trying to ask the hard questions about how to get more women-  easily 

Yeah Good Luck with that🍀😉

Now, of course, you risk missing on any additional upside. But for me, I’m OK with this because I plan on leaving some shares in the bucket to continue to ride along four years to come.

I also plan on adding more to this position on future dips 


At $17 I would’ve gained a good bit of profit. And I would be happy with that. So I set a limit order for selling my 110 shares and will move this cash back into my checking account if this order execute.  Yes. This is my rent money. I’m out here playing with.🤣🤣

Most of these sell limit orders do close out at the end of the day. But Robin Hood does have a version where you could set it for a 90 day time length.

title: It’s Friday! : Ease on down the road!
body:
Just some Fun For my followers : 

Can’t have a Wizard of Oz themed week without finishing on the Wiz😎

Here are some fun and surprising facts about The Wiz — the 1975 Broadway musical and 1978 film — with a business and numbers twist:

💵 1. Budget Blowout: The Film Nearly Got Canceled
Original Budget: $20 million (huge for the time).
Final Cost: Over $24 million.
Studio Risk: Universal Pictures nearly pulled the plug because the projected costs were too high for a musical with a predominantly Black cast — rare for major studios in the '70s.


🎭 2. Broadway Success: From Underdog to Million-Dollar Hit
Opening Night: January 5, 1975.
Initial Struggles: Poor ticket sales almost killed the show within weeks.
Turnaround: A bold radio advertising campaign helped generate buzz.
Result: Over $17 million in box office revenue and 1,672 performances later, it became a Broadway classic.



👟 3. Michael Jackson’s Paycheck for the Film
MJ was paid $100,000 to play the Scarecrow — a modest sum by today’s standards.
The film was one of his first steps into acting and business independence.



👩🏾‍💼 4. Diana Ross Negotiated Her Way In
Diana Ross was not originally considered for Dorothy — producers wanted someone in their late teens.
She lobbied hard and personally convinced studio heads. Lesson: Personal branding and persistence matter in business.



📈 5. The Wiz Was a Pioneer in Black Venture Investment
The show’s Broadway success opened the door for more Black-led productions.
It was a rare case in the 1970s where a Black creative team and cast helped generate multi-million dollar revenue and critical acclaim — proving investor assumptions wrong.


💿 6. Soundtrack Goldmine
Quincy Jones produced the soundtrack.
Though the film bombed, the music — including Jackson’s “You Can’t Win” and Lena Horne’s “Believe in Yourself” — became iconic.
Soundtrack sales and licensing rights brought in millions post-release.



🧙🏽‍♂️ 7. Merchandising and Legacy
The Wiz didn't have a major merch rollout like Star Wars, but it sparked a wave of Black theatrical productions and Afrofuturistic reinterpretations in pop culture.
Its cultural capital far exceeded its box office — and its long-tail value is still monetized through revivals, licensing, and musical influence.

That was a week whew! 

🎶

Ease  on down , Ease  on down the road 🎶

title: Just for the new ladies AH: 🍆 ￼Market Indicators
body:
Yes 🙌. This week its back to skanky subject matter 

(Well OK fine I will allow the men to participate only if they know how to behave themselves.)

📉 Market Indicators: A Surprisingly Accurate Comparison

😈
I will be honest… Before AH, I had no idea how market indicators worked. Now? I see the signals, the cycles, the sensitivity — and yes, sometimes the false alarms.

Here are the 3 🍆 indicators I use regularly. 

(Well, really 4 if you count at longwashere. But Longs market indicator I have never met in person so I don’t know how that works. I just follow it.😇)

Yes! And before you ask,   I am always looking for more. So don’t be shy and put your recommendations below.👇

1️⃣ Moving Averages (MA)

Hey, how’s it going?: Like me checking how things have been going the last few days — MA is all about trends. 🔹 Use: Detects upward/downward momentum. 🔹 Function: When my 50-day MA crosses above the 200-day, it's a Golden Cross — a bullish signal (aka time for the stock to rise 🌞). 🔹 Death Cross Definition: When the 50-day drops below the 200-day — that's the Death Cross. Translation: momentum’s dying, and things might go soft for a while 🪦🍆. 🔹 Bullish Level: Golden Cross = Uptrend potential. 🔹 Bearish Level: Death Cross = Possible downturn. 💥 Swing Trade Role: Great for spotting trend continuations or reversals — perfect for entries & exits. It can be a good one to determine if it’s time to join the party or it’s time to leave. I am the lady who never “wants to overstay my welcome”🍍.


2️⃣ Relative Strength Index (RSI)

How ready are you?: Measures excitement. Is the market overstimulated (overbought)? Or struggling to get going (oversold)? 🔹 Use: Momentum gauge (0–100 scale). 🔹 Function:
* RSI > 70 = Market might be too hot, time to cool off 😓
* RSI < 30 = Things could be ready to rise again 😉 🔹 Bullish: RSI rebounding from below 30 🔹 Bearish: RSI falling from above 70 🔥 Swing Trade Role: Catch those reversal plays like a pro. Sometimes with swinging entries and exits are all about timing.😅 enough said about that one. 

3️⃣ Volume

How many are in on this ?: : Without volume? It’s just wishful thinking, baby. 🔹 Use: Confirms if the price action is the real deal. 🔹 Function:
* Big move + Low volume = Meh 😒
* Big move + Big volume = Now we’re talkin' 💪 🔹 Bullish: High volume supporting upward price 🔹 Bearish: High volume on sell-offs ⚡ Swing Trade Role: Confirms breakouts, fake-outs, and strength of moves. Premiums are higher , share prices price quicker if everybody is trying to get in on the fun.🙂☺️

📈 TLDR: These indicators don’t just read the market — they read the room. Trading is about timing, signals, and knowing when the momentum is really there. 😉

🥹Don’t have too much fun without me. I love open invitations, if you see several indicators are ready. It’s OK to tag me on a post. I do like to do my own research and can be a little slow to join. Don’t be shy,, . It’s OK even if things don’t work out.

💚Don’t be silly! Of course I brought pics. Just swipe to the left and take a look😊.

👉you can get to a similar chart on Robin Hood by pressing the double arrows in the upper right hand corner of your favorite stock

👉Note I made a watchlist for myself of the favorite stock and index I use to determine the market.

title: KNOW labs:  I did not buy into this one. From chat. $KNW.
body:
KNW Stock Is Going Crypto? Here’s What You Need to Know

There’s a surprising shift happening in the world of medical tech—Know Labs (ticker: KNW), a company best known for its non-invasive health monitoring technologies, is diving into Bitcoin in a big way.

So, what’s happening?

On June 6, 2025, Know Labs announced a major strategic move: Greg Kidd, a former Chief Risk Officer at Ripple and early investor in companies like Twitter and Coinbase, is set to acquire a controlling interest in KNW through his firm, Goldeneye 1995 LLC.

Here’s what makes this unique:

The deal includes 1,000 Bitcoins, used to purchase shares and retire existing debt.
Kidd will also provide additional cash to fund operations and take over as both CEO and Chairman of the Board.
Most notably, KNW plans to adopt a Bitcoin treasury strategy, meaning Bitcoin will become a major component of the company’s balance sheet.
This move puts Know Labs in rare company—alongside firms like MicroStrategy—as it aims to give shareholders direct exposure to Bitcoin via the public stock market.

But is KNW becoming a crypto company?

Not exactly. Know Labs is still focused on medical diagnostics and non-invasive biosensors. However, this pivot introduces a financial layer that reflects a growing trend: using Bitcoin as a corporate reserve asset to hedge against inflation and offer unique investor upside.

How does this compare to Trias (TRIAS)?

While some may confuse the two, Trias is an entirely separate blockchain project with its own token and mission. KNW is not becoming Trias, but it is aligning itself more closely with Bitcoin’s financial ecosystem.

Sources:

BusinessWire. “Greg Kidd to Acquire Controlling Interest in Know Labs and Introduce Bitcoin Treasury Strategy.” June 6, 2025. Link
CoinGecko. “Trias Token (TRIAS) Overview.” Link

title: About me: @883Ismygovtname
body:
A lot of new followers here. 😅

As a divorced mother, who is taking a break from dating, and who has split custody of her kids-The thought of being followed is a bit scary.

But  heck , we’re at the point in my lifetime movie -I figured I might as well introduce myself.

Playful, cheeky , approachable, open minded and positive I hope would be my descriptors.

Pamela Anderson once said what motivates her to stay in shape is she puts a bikini on every day and takes a picture.

Me posting my trades and linking my Robin Hood portfolio. Is my financial bikini. 

🧭 My Core Strategy: Long-Term Growth With an Edge

At the heart of my trading style is a belief in long-term equity ownership. I like to hold 100-share positions in high-growth companies, not just for the appreciation, but because it allows me to sell covered calls for extra income. It’s a simple way to add money to my port without adding money. 

Selling covered calls is the name of my game. I’m pretty much a “one-trick pony.”🐴. Each of my 100 share blocks I call a workhorse and and I’m out here on Robin Hood just learning to farm money.

I don’t keep much lazy cash in my portfolio, so you won’t see me doing many cash-secured puts. The wheel strategy (selling puts then covered calls) isn’t ideal at my capital level — I think it works better at higher price points and with more stable, higher-quality companies. That’s just not the place I’m in… yet.


💻 Where My Money Lives

I have three main investment accounts:

💰 Fidelity account: This is for traditional, long-term investing. I do have a larger account that is privately manage here. There is a leftover joint savings account that I recently made active. No fancy trades. No covered calls. Just buy and hold. ($MTPLF, $ONDS, $KWM).
🐴Robinhood personal + IRA accounts: These are my more active portfolios. This is what I have linked here. I use them to test strategies, experiment with growth ideas, and execute options or leverage plays when I have high conviction.
🪙BLOFIN is where I trade crypto.  
👉If I’m aiming for a huge gain, I usually put that trade inside my IRA to keep the tax situation clean. 
👉If it’s more of a slow grower or an “experiment,” it goes into my personal account. 
👉I don’t add money to cover losses.
👉I don’t withdraw from my account — I’m fortunate that I don’t need this capital for bills.


💰 Options, Crypto, and Conviction Plays
I’m not big on buying lots of options, but when I do, it’s usually long-dated calls or LEAPS. If something is in budget and feels worth it, I’ll fund it directly.

I do have a $20 DCA that goes into BTC.. Every time I get a 20% gain, I will pull the capital and profits and move them into MSTY, a more grounded position. That’s my way of stabilizing the volatility and allowing my money to work harder for me.

🔄 Fractionals, Pineapple Pizza, and My Investing Language
I don’t hold onto fractional shares long term. I might use them for quick swing trades (JKATNISS ) targeting 10–30% gains, but that’s it.

There are also some stocks/sectors I jokingly refer to as “pineapple pizza” positions. If it’s pineapple pizza, it means I have an irrational distaste that cannot be explained. These tend to be healthcare and weaponry. There are some exceptions to this rule PFE, ONDS, or PLTR. Yes I love pineapples.🍍😎. And I do like 🍕 😋 but if you put them together 🤢. Don’t ask me to explain why.

Bringing me to my next point. ✍️

I’m big on metaphors. I believe in making the stock market simple and intuitive — partly because I’m a mom, and I’m trying to introduce these lifelong (hopefully generational) concepts to my kids in a way that sticks.

📈 Goals and Vision
Long-term? My dream portfolio would grow to $10 million — I’ll admit, that goal was inspired by Reddit and Sir Jack challenge. But as I’ve learned more about myself, I’ve also realized I’m probably not the type to aggressively scale through risk. I prefer buying good companies and letting them work for me.

Short-term? My next real milestone is $100K. After that, I may begin scaling up to $300K to $600K, by pulling in more capital. At that point, I’d love to leave full-time employment and focus on traveling, writing, and trading with purpose.


🗓️ Weekly Rhythm & Community
⭐️Sundays/Mondays: I post my weekly strategy, including new goals, any major changes, lessons learned, and concepts I’m exploring.
⭐️ Fridays/Saturdays: I like to keep things lighter. I post market metaphors, creative analogies, or just fun takeson the week in trading.
🎊🎁
This isn’t just about money — I genuinely enjoy the social side of AfterHour. Writing is  a stress-relieving hobby, and I find inspiration in the markets, in life, and in the people who show up every day — whales, minnows, and everyone in between.
😇
I’m spiritual. I believe God places people in your life for a reason, and when you’re paying attention to the signs, good things follow.

Follow or Unfollow as you please. 
I follow back. 
I try to comment on the ignored posts as much as I can as time permits.
No tips needed for me. Because the next week I might say something that will make you wanna take them back.🤣

I have nothing to sell or to preach really. I would be the same person with one follower as I Would be with 1 million followers. So I will apologize in advance for that.🤣🤣

For now, no social media links, no discord, I really don’t post on Reddit anymore, no YouTube, no courses or investments.
Hopefully there are no bots or scammers out there

Best wishes to us all🤗 🐴🌱💚🤗

title: Using Chat  for complex decisions: $OKLO
body:
No need to comment. This is just forfun . If you’re bored and late night degeneracy 🤪.

Asked to chat for some advice on what to do with my deeply in the money covered call on $OKLO 

Just wanted to offer a peek into how this feature works. It’s a great tool to use, but I don’t rely on. 

I asked it to run through the scenario for my $OKLO 

📈 Your Net Profit If Assigned
Buy price: $23.93 × 100 = $2,393
Sell price (assigned): $27 × 100 = $2,700
Premium received: $1,168
Total proceeds if assigned = $2,700 + $1,168 = $3,868
🧾 Total Profit = $3,868 – $2,393 = $1,475
✅ Return = ~61.6%

Compare this to holding and selling today at $54.31 — which would be a $3,038 profit (~127% gain).
🔁 Should You Roll?
To roll up (say to $55 strike expiring later), you'd:

Buy to close the current call for ~$27.58
Sell a higher strike call, hopefully getting some premium back
🔍 You would need a new option to offset that $27.58 debit, which is very steep right now — meaning the stock has run up way past your original covered call.

🧠 Your Options Now
✅ Option 1: Let it Assign

Locks in $1,475 gain
Simple, no further risk
Lets you redeploy capital (especially with such a large percent of your portfolio in this stock)
🔄 Option 2: Roll Up & Out

If you believe OKLO will go even higher, you could roll to a higher strike, further expiration (e.g., $60 for August or September)
This would recapture some upside, but you'll pay heavily upfront due to the massive intrinsic value in your current $27 call
🧨 Option 3: Buy to Close & Hold

Close the short call and just hold the stock
This re-opens you to full upside — but costs ~$2,758 to close, which subtracts from your total return


📌 Final Thought:
Since this is in a Traditional IRA, you avoid capital gains tax either way. That makes allowing assignment more appealing if you're satisfied with the return and want to reduce risk or rebalance.

title: $NOVA becomes $NOVAQ :What does it mean?
body:
Dammmit Chat 🙄🤬

ChatGPT said:

When a company changes its ticker symbol — like NOVA becoming nOVAQ — it typically signals a major corporate action. In this case, the change from NOVA (Sunnova Energy International Inc.) to nOVAQ suggests one of the following possibilities:

🚨 Likely Explanation: Bankruptcy or OTC Delisting
The lowercase "n" and the "Q" at the end often indicate that:
The company filed for bankruptcy (Chapter 11).
Or it's now trading over-the-counter (OTC) instead of on a major exchange like NYSE or NASDAQ.
🔍 Ticker Breakdown:
nOVAQ:
The "n" prefix often denotes an OTC (over-the-counter) market designation.
The "Q" at the end is used by NASDAQ to indicate the company is in bankruptcy proceedings.
🧾 Real-World Example:
If Sunnova Energy ($NOVA) is now nOVAQ, this could mean:

The company entered bankruptcy.
Its stock was delisted

 You know what?

Take a peek down below👀.

to a stock.

and oh oh oh baby !

👉with just enough volatility to keep things interesting

 🙀 Is that TMI. ￼ well don’t you? Wanna know how I choose between so many?

*giggles*

😏Here’s what gets me turned on to a stock.
(No, I clearly said “ST”)

1️⃣ Long-Term History (Price Action & Trend 📉)
 I hate to be Debbie Downer, but yes, I do look at a past.
 📆 I’m checking:

✨ 1 Week ✅ (Are you available?)
✨ 3 Month ✅ (how’s the chemistry?)
✨YTD ✅ (Are we trending upward?)
✨ 5 Year ✅ (how do you handle life’s stresses?)

It doesn’t need to be perfect — I just need to know what to expect if we make it official.
 📉 No ghosting. 📈 No pump-n-dumps. 
Loooonng term stocks just don’t do that. I need good company, not chaos.

🍆Market Indicator: Use Moving Averages (50-day & 200-day) 💡 Look for a golden cross = long-term trend confirmation

2️⃣ Momentum, Baby (RSI + MACD 🚀)
 Upward trend? I’m all in. Ambition looks good on you. You’re not just moving — you’re going somewhere. 
you know that big stock energy🥰

And no, I’m not a gold digger. 🙄 🤩I just want and feel I deserve something bigger...
 giggles …

for both of us, of course.

🍆Market Indicator: 🔍 RSI between 50–70 = trending strong 🧠 MACD crossover = bullish vibes, baby

3️⃣ Volatility Has Its Benefits (Implied Volatility 🌀)
 I like it spicy — just enough to sell some juicy covered calls 😏 But not so wild I can’t sleep at night. Surprise me… just be there in the morning, okay?

🍆Market Indicator: 🎯 IV Rank 60–80% = premium-worthy but manageable 💸 That’s the sweet spot for writing calls while still holding tight.

4️⃣ Liquidity is a Love Language (Volume & Open Interest 💧)
 Low volume? 🚩 Immediate turn-off. If all eyes are on you, I know all eyes are on us 😎 I want: ✔️ Options volume ✔️ Tight bid-ask spreads ✔️ Easy exits & sexy entries I don’t do messy breakups or slow fades.

Market Indicator: 🔄 Daily trading volume > 1M shares 📈 Open interest > 500 contracts per strike

💋 Bottom Line: 📈 Turn me on with stability and a bright future 💸 Tease me with premiums 💚 Stay long enough to build wealth together
