🍕🍕🍕🍕🍕🍍🍍🍍🍍🍍🍍

📄 Your Position Summary:

Contract: KULR $1 Call expiring 1/16/2026
Premium Paid: $0.85 (or $85 total)

Post-split status: KULR did a 1-for-25 reverse split, so your contract is now a non-standard adjusted option.

🧮 What You Actually Hold Now (post-split):
Your contract now represents:
✅ 4 shares of KULR
✅ Effective strike price: $25
✅ You paid $85 = $21.25/share cost basis if exercised
🚨 Should You Exercise?

🚫 No — Not Right Now
Here’s why:

Current KULR price (as of June 2025): ~$0.90–$1.10 per share pre-split

Post-split price: ~$22–$28 range depending on volatility
Your strike price is $25, so KULR would need to trade above $25 for it to make sense to exercise.

You’d get 4 shares at $25/share, costing you $100 total — but you already paid $85, so your true break-even is $28.75/share

📉 Unless KULR climbs above $28.75, you’d lose money by exercising.

✅ What Are Your Best Options Now?

1️⃣ Sell the LEAP if you want out
Even if it’s a small loss, you clean up your portfolio
Avoids the liquidity trap of non-standard contracts
2️⃣ Hold if you believe in a KULR moonshot
You have until Jan 2026
If it spikes well above $28, your LEAP becomes valuable again
3️⃣ Avoid exercising — or rolling until price improves
Rolling into a new, standard contract (on 100-share basis) might simplify your position, but it could cost you premium


🧠 Recommendation:

If your conviction is low, sell now and use that $85 toward KULR shares directly — clean ownership, easier to manage.

If you’re still bullish long-term, hold it, but don’t exercise unless KULR rallies past $30+ before expiration. ￼

Medium: Installation (oil painting, corporate signage)
Estimated Value: ~$1 million+ (museum-grade political art rarely hits the open market)

📍 Where to See It:
🖼️ Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
Part of their permanent collection — often exhibited in rooms focused on political critique and institutional power.

🧠 Why This Still Matters in Today’s Market:
This isn’t decorative — it’s a direct corporate call-out.

🔍 In the heart of the piece is the Mobil oil logo, embedded not as branding — but as blame.
Haacke exposes how multinational oil money quietly funds the very institutions that shape public opinion.

📈 Market Connections:
Haacke painted this during the rise of Reaganomics and oil-backed influence. His message?

Museums aren’t neutral.
Corporate sponsorship = cultural manipulation
Art isn’t just creative — it can be a political and financial weapon

🧨 Why So Controversial?

Spectacle vs. Substance – Critics called it “bling gone berserk.” Is it art, or a stunt?

Price Tag Politics – Debuted during the 2000s boom, weaponizing auction-house hype to prove art could be as bankable as a blue-chip stock.

Death Commodified – A literal human skull turned luxury object: confronting our fear of mortality while flexing obscene wealth.

🎶 Music Match:

“金钱 (Money)” – Faye Wong
Dream-pop vocals float over minimalist beats, asking whether endless riches = emptiness. 

The perfect soundtrack for a diamond skull that whispers: Is this excess… or is this the end?

title: $APLD : @brayflex we are both correct
body:
Had some pillow talk with chat last night.


for any lurkers -I’ve included the links to the original post to what this is referencing.

🌟Basically, I have a $APLD call that is in the money. 

I had some wonderful suggestions. 

I will not be selling poor man’s covered calls against it, but I may try that in the future with a higher value option 

Brayflex had  an interesting suggestion about just exercising it for cash instead of taking the shares because of an intrinsic value

😇But the TLDR is that I will just go ahead and exercise it. I do not have $1000 of cash in my account.🤪🤣

Here is chat response 👇

Here’s the breakdown of your APLD $5 call option priced at $5.90:

👉 $5.59 of the value is intrinsic — directly from how far the stock price is above the strike.

👉 $0.31 is time value — the extra premium priced in for volatility and time until expiration.

This confirms that the majority of the option's value is intrinsic, meaning it’s deep in-the-money. If you’re considering exercising vs. selling, you’re essentially deciding whether you want to:
💚💚💚
👉 Lock in more liquidity now (by selling the option for its full value), or

👉 Take ownership of 200 shares at a lower cost basis (and potentially hold for more upside or income).


You own 2 call contracts for APLD $5 strike, expiring 1/16/26, and APLD is currently trading at $10.59.

Option 1: Exercising the call
Each call gives you the right to buy 100 shares at $5/share.
 So for 1 contract (100 shares):

👉 Exercise cost = 100 × $5 = $500
You have 2 contracts, so:
👉 Total exercise cost = 2 × $500 = $1,000
👉This gives you 200 shares of APLD for $1,000
Effective cost per share = $5
 (You could include the premium if you want true cost basis: $3 × 100 = $300 per contract, or $600 total → effective cost basis = $8.00/share)

Option 2: Buying shares outright
Current market price = $10.59/share So 200 shares would cost you: 200 × $10.59 = $2,118

✅ Conclusion:
👉 Exercising the call = $1,000
👉 Buying on market = $2,118
➡️ Exercising is $1,118 cheaper (though you give up the flexibility and time value of the options)

🧠 First, some definitions:
👉 Intrinsic Value = Current Share Price – Strike Price
👉 Time Value = Option Price – Intrinsic Value
You have:
👉 Current APLD share price: $10.59
👉 Strike price: $5
👉 Current option price: $5.90

🔢 Step-by-step:
1. Intrinsic Value (per contract): $10.59 – $5 = $5.59
2. Time Value (per contract): $5.90 – $5.59 = $0.31

💰 Result:
👉 Time value per share = $0.31
👉 Each contract controls 100 shares → $0.31 × 100 = $31 of time value per contract
👉 You have 2 contracts → $62 total time value

🧾 Summary:
Metric	Value
Intrinsic Value	$5.59/share
Time Value	$0.31/share
Time Value per Contract	$31
Total Time Value (2 contracts)	$62
This means that out of the $5.90 current premium, only $0.31 is due to time value — the rest is pure intrinsic value.

🎵 Song Sidebar: UGK’s International Players Anthem

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=awMIbA34MT8

A few quick facts:

* Sampled from Willie Hutch’s “I Choose You.”
* Video features a wedding scene with fighting bridesmaids, minor colorism, and cameos galore (no nudity or guns).

 🧬Origins & Sampling
* The beat is built around Willie Hutch’s 1973 soul song “I Choose You.”
    * That original is a romantic, lush ballad from the “The Mack” soundtrack — a blaxploitation classic.
    * Producer Mr. Lee and Three 6 Mafia’s DJ Paul & Juicy J flipped the sample into a slow, triumphant Southern anthem.

👑 UGK x OutKast Collab
* This track brought UGK (Pimp C & Bun B) and OutKast (André 3000 & Big Boi) together — a Southern dream team.
* Despite their stylistic differences, the chemistry was off the charts.
* Pimp C originally didn’t want the beat to be used if Three 6 Mafia touched it — that tension only added to the song’s legend.

🗣️ That André 3000 Verse...
* André’s verse opens the song a cappella, and it’s iconic: “So I typed a text to a girl I used to see...” me saying goodbye to some equities.  
* The verse tells a full story — love, loyalty, maturity — in under a minute.
* Fun fact: André reportedly recorded it separately without knowing how the rest of the beat would drop.


💿 Album & Awards
* Featured on UGK’s final studio album, Underground Kingz (2007).
* The song was nominated for a Grammy (Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group).
* Ranked by Rolling Stone, Pitchfork, and Complex as one of the greatest rap songs of all time.

💔 Bittersweet Legacy
* Tragically, Pimp C died just months after the release of the album.


👀 The Music Video
* The video is a wedding-themed comedy, with Bun B as the groom and André as the wild, interrupting groomsman.
* Cameos include:
    * Bishop Don Magic Juan
    * Nick Cannon
    * T-Pain
    * Project Pat

The song’s about choosing  in a world of options — just like trading.

title: 🎺🇺🇸 Instruments of Pleasure: 🎆🍦
body:
Happy Birthday to America 🇺🇸🤗

Yes Apologies  I truly DO like it all

So

🎧John Phillip Sousa”s orchestrated march is on blast today and it is my absolute fav soundtrack for the fourth 🎧

From Crispus Attucks, personal roots in slavery and relatives in the military  , the idea that certain ethnicities are “unAmerican” I find humorous at best. 

This holiday is HUUGE in our family so forgive my slow response time. Im out celebrating 🇺🇸
For me growing up, Singing Happy Birthday America brings back memories of sitting on the hood of MG convertible.  Hood hot still from the blazing sun. Stars stripes from a live Orchestra piped over speakers, orgasmic fireworks and lots of sticky dripping ice cream. 

So what do you think ? 

Was my July 4 th American or unAmerican ?

Lets take a look at the market 👀

🥁 “The Stars and Stripes Forever”
John Philip Sousa composed The Stars and Stripes Forever in 1896, and it remains the official national march of the United States. 

But the instruments used in this patriotic powerhouse? Not as American as apple pie (which, for the record, is also European).

Key Instruments:
* Piccolo – European roots, but vital to the sound.
* Snare Drum – Although the drum set is uniquely American, the drum has orgins in china, used for communication in Africa, the. Snare drum is European version 
* Sousaphone – American-made innovation by Sousa himself!
* 
Market Fact: The U.S. band instrument market is valued at over $800 million annually, with schools and military bands driving demand.

Stock to Watch for funsies, but I don’t own.:
 🎷 Yamaha Corporation (OTC: $YAMCY ) – A global leader in musical instruments, including marching band gear. While Japanese, it plays a major role in American bandrooms.

🎇 CHYYYNA
Fireworks and the Fourth are inseparable—but almost all consumer fireworks in the U.S. are made in China.

Today: Over 90% of U.S. consumer fireworks are imported from China.
Stocks to Watch:
* 💥 Phantom Fireworks – Privately held, but...
* 🎯 Walmart (NYSE: $WMT ) and Costco (NASDAQ: $COST ) – Major retailers selling fireworks in legal states.
* 📦 Amazon (NASDAQ: $AMZN ) – An increasingly popular place for ordering party supplies (though not fireworks themselves).

Market Boom: Fireworks imports exceeded $400 million in 2024, despite tighter state regulations.

🍦 Ice Cream – You scream 

That scoop of vanilla? Global roots, big U.S. market.
Market Size: Over $11 billion in U.S. annual sales.

Stocks to Watch:
* 🍨 Unilever (NYSE: $UL ) – Parent of Ben & Jerry’s, Magnum, Breyers.
* 🐄 Conagra Brands (NYSE: $CAG ) – Owns brands like Healthy Choice and has a frozen treat portfolio.
* 🛒 Walmart (NYSE: $WMT ) and Kroger (NYSE: KR) – Major grocery chains that dominate domestic ice cream sales.
* 
Fun Fact: The U.S. consumes more ice cream per capita than any other country. Vanilla remains the top flavor, and most flavor extracts like vanilla come from Madagascar🌍

🇺🇸 Flags and Fabric – American Pride, International Threads
Yes, even your American flag is part of the global supply chain.

Stocks to Watch:
* 🧵 Hanesbrands Inc. (NYSE: $HBI ) – Known for textiles, with facilities globally that could include flag fabric production.
* 🇺🇸 Joann Inc. (NASDAQ: $JOANQ ) – Fabric and craft retailer offering flag kits and materials.
* 📦 Amazon (NASDAQ: $AMZN ) – One of the largest marketplaces for flags, including many made overseas.

The American experience is proudly assembled from everywhere.

🇺🇸 Featured Tickers Recap:
* 🎯 $WMT  – Walmart
* 📦 $AMZN  – Amazon
* 🛒 $COST   – Costco
* 🍨 $UL  – Unilever
* 🐄 $CAG  – Conagra
* 🧵 $HBI  – Hanesbrands
* 🇺🇸 $JOANQ  – Joann Inc.
* 🎷 $YAMCY  – Yamaha Corp. (for band instruments)

Now matter the origin- I say learn to enjoy your instruments of pleasure. Its the American tradition . 🇺🇸🎆🍦

Afterhour,  Lets talk about How to get ready for your 👇

💦 Money Shot in Options Trading💦

(Short-dated call buying edition)

Setup: Buying a weekly call on a fast-moving stock like $NVDA, $TSLA $HOOD

🔺 Delta: Your Main Performer (Direction + Power)

🌟Ideal Delta Range: 0.30–0.60
🌟Think of Delta as your star performer. If it’s too low (0.10), you’re just teasing — too far out-the-money, no real movement. If it’s too high (0.80+), you’re already “there” — expensive and little reward left. Sweet spot? 0.40–0.60 — enough leverage, but still room to explode.
🎥 “You want enough action to build tension — but still leave room for the climax.”

⏳ Theta: Your Buzzkill Clock

 🌟Theta Burn: > –0.10/day is dangerous (the higher in magnitude, the faster the burn)
🌟In short-dated calls, Theta is like the countdown before the money shot — once it's ticking, you're racing against time. Every hour you wait, your premium gets soft— even if the stock’s moving.
🎬 “Wait too long, and it’s over before you even hit record.”

📈 Gamma: Your Plot Twist (Volatility Sensitivity)

🌟High Gamma: > 0.05 can be explosive
🌟Gamma makes Delta go wild. When Gamma’s high, even a small move in the stock pumps up Delta and gives your call option a surge of life. Great for short-dated setups — the moves are sharp and sudden. But risky too. Gamma cuts both ways.

🎞️ “Gamma’s that camera shake right before everything explodes — messy but magical.”

🌪 Vega: The Lighting Crew (Volatility Impact)

title: This post for @AimUsurper 🤗💚🤗
body:
Here is a little overnight homework for you ( or any lurkers ) before market opens.

😎A quick reminder. I’m not someone who’s necessarily looking for followers or even tips. I just learn out loud. So please do not feel compelled to follow me. 

⏰Right now, it is 1 AM Eastern standard time. So the market is not open. This current options chain is not accurate. But it can be a good platform for me to illustrate some things before market open.

💚Again. The first thing you should do is decide in your mind mentally what is the share price you’re willing to have your shares assigned. 

🙏I know you do not want assignment. But to help you make decisions going forward. It’s nice to know what’s your current cost basis. And how much you would be willing to sacrifice. 

Note I provided you three examples of options. 
👉A $3 dollar strike 
👉A $3.5 strike 
👉A$4  strike 

￼￼ You do not have to be an expert to see that $BTBT has been on a little bit of a down trend this week. This is reflected in the options premium.

Note that a three dollar strike, carries a Delta of 0.75. If you select that Delta as a covered call. You get a nice premium, but you also get a 75% chance your shares will be called away. 


On the opposite end of the spectrum look at the four dollar strike. Again $BTBT has been trending a little bit lower. So at this current moment. In this current macro environment. It is highly unlikely that $BTBT will hit four dollars at the end of the week . look at the Delta. Because this is so unlikely look at the premium that is offered. It is zero dollars. Not many people in the market will pay for a 0% chance.


Understandably the $3.50 strike is somewhere in between. 


🤔Now let’s take a look at the IV ratio. It’s in the upper right hand corner. 

👀All of the IV ratios are greater than 100%. This means the stock is pretty volatile right now. Maybe like having a cranky unstable (girlfriend, or boyfriend )date. But again. Don’t blame the options chain on this. You selected this dating partner for a reason. You thought this dating partner ￼ was hot and y’all could grow together.🤷

😧At any point even though the evening with your dating partner is going well, this dating partner
 may get up and leave the restaurant. It has nothing to do with you. OR The restaurant you selected ( the delta) It’s just how your dating partner (stock )is behaving today. Keep in mind in the future your dating partner ￼ may calm down and be totally reasonable or even be marriage material.

🤪Anyhow, -Keep this in mind when selecting your Delta. What is the IV ratio or instability of your underlying date.


😬So a Delta less than 0.3 technically should leave your shares in your hands by the end of the week. But with this high IV ratio. If you really wanted to play it safe. You might want to consider accepting less premium and a Delta of 0.2 or 0.1.  


🤓Another more labor intensive option is just watching the price movement of your stock. 

🔮For instance. You can chance selecting a higher Delta if you’re familiar with how the stock moves, let’s say $BTBT has an audit coming up at the end of the week 
OR there are some news in the media that you think will negatively impact the stock. Maybe the CPI report, 

🔭You can take a chance with a higher Delta , feeling confident that the share price will go down because of your knowledge of the macro economic environment.

🗞️Likewise. If you know your stock is coming up on some news that will likely make it grow. Let’s say the president plans on visiting $BTBT headquarters on Friday. That is a situation where you might want to select a very low Delta. 0.1 or do not place a covered call at all. Why? Because at the end of the week once this news event occurs. The stock may grow exponentially And your shares might be exercised. Or taken away.


👽That’s a lot of information. I’ll let you look over it. And then tomorrow morning I will make a post about which Delta I think maybe best. 

🎗️Don’t forget your homework. What is your underlying cost basis for your $BTBT shares. And also at what price if exercised would you be at least a little bit profitable?

Options on U.S. equities (including those traded on platforms like Robinhood) typically expire at market close on the expiration date, which is 4:00 PM ET on that Friday — July 18, 2025 , in this case.

$IWM ghosted hard — slipped below $219 and left the user  hanging. No lift, no spark… just a slow fade into zero.

Let’s pause the video here sugar:👇
these contracts expired
😮Deep Out of the Money (OTM)
😯 Worth close to $0.00
😯 No time value remaining
🔻 Estimated Loss: If they expired worthless, the full cost is lost:
Loss = $1,961.47 (100% loss) 😢



🤨 These calls were bought as a lottery ticket for a last-minute move in IWM (Russell 2000).

 🤨 the user  had ultra-short-term, OTM exposure on a major index — basically a YOLO bet that it would spike above $224 .

👀 Because the breakeven would be $224 + $0.28 = $224.28, and IWM was nowhere near that, these were extremely low probability plays.

🔮 Going Forward
This was:
🤫 A high-risk, high-reward day trade or volatility spike bet.
🤫 Likely bought hoping for a Fed decision, CPI print, earnings, or geopolitical event to shock IWM upward intraday.

🌊 “When Gamma Hits Like Ocean Waves” 🌊
I too used to  wonder how stocks suddenly rocket out of nowhere? That’s the power of a gamma squeeze — and it works like the ocean. Here’s the analogy:

🌬️ 1. Wind Starts the Wave
✨In the ocean, wind = call option buying
✨Traders buy OTM (out-of-the-money) calls
✨This creates ripples… but the real action starts underneath

🌊 2. Energy Builds Below the Surface
✨Market Makers (brokers/RH) sell those calls → now they’re short gamma
✨To hedge, they must buy shares of the stock
✨Buying shares = adding energy under the wave

🌪️ 3. The Swell Grows
✨Stock price rises → delta of those calls increases
✨Market Makers must buy even more shares
✨This is like wind blowing harder, making waves grow taller

🌊💥 4. The Big Wave (Gamma Squeeze)
✨As calls move ITM, hedging accelerates
✨Massive share buying hits the market
✨Price surges like a tsunami, crushing shorts along the way

🔥 Short Squeeze Combo

💫 If shorts (sells) are trapped, they cover positions → more buying
💫Now the wave becomes a tidal wave 🌊🌊
💫Momentum feeds itself

📈 Result: Stock price skyrockets in hours or days.
 💡 Tip: Watch for high call volume, rising IV, and heavy OTM bets — that’s wind before the storm.

⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️
Warning: searching for the next GME is probably not a safe or realistic way to gain money in the market.👈

Just like real surfing. It’s unpredictable which side of the wave your portfolio might land.😬

Yes, you could ride the wave, barrel roll and end up in money shot fame on IG 

OR

Your portfolio can crash and burn on the Rocky reef as the stock falls. Not even enough for a rescue back to the beach.

Even the aptly named experts on AfterHour👀 have trouble getting it right . You can just scroll their feed and see all the angry comments they get from their followers because it is so difficult to predict.😅

But if you had a taste of the waves. And you want to become a surfer, then here are a few things that you would look for.👇


🚀 Want to Spot a Short Squeeze Before It Pops?
Watch these 5 indicators with actual numbers:

✅ 1. Short Interest (SI%)
20%+ of float shorted = high squeeze potential 30%+ = 🔥 prime danger zone


✅ 2. Cost to Borrow (CTB)
Above 10% = shorts feeling pain Above 50% = extreme stress


✅ 3. Float Size & Volume
Float under 50M shares + Daily volume ≥ float ÷ 3 = supply crunch


✅ 4. Options Activity (Gamma Fuel)
OTM call volume 3x normal daily avg IV spiking 20%+ in 24 hrs



✅ 5. Sentiment Spike
Trending tickers on Reddit (r/WallStreetBets) or X Rapid Google Trends rise

🔥 When 3 or more of these hit together → Surf season begins.

body:

The TLDR is that this will lock in my games. I get to take a little bit of profit off of this leap. Rolling it up to a higher strike. But I think it will likely hit in the near future. 


Here is the information and some pics to go with it. 


Thanks for sharing the screenshots! Here’s what I see:

Underlying stock (BULL): $16.08
Current Call: $12.50 strike, exp. 07/17/2026
Your Cost: $4.30
Current Option Value: $6.40
Current Gain: +$210 (≈49%)
Delta: 0.7774 (very ITM)
Breakeven: $16.80
So, you’re deep ITM and already sitting on a good gain. Rolling up makes sense if you want:
✔ Lock in gains
✔ Open more upside room
✔ Possibly reduce risk

✅ Step 1: Lock in Profit Calculation
Current option = $6.40
Your cost = $4.30
Profit = $2.10 per share ($210 total)

If you sell now, you lock in $210 profit.

✅ Step 2: Rolling Up Strategy
You’ll sell this $12.50 call and buy a higher strike (likely $17.5, $20, $22.5, or $25). All still 07/17/2026.

➡ The higher you go, the cheaper the new call, but you pay more net debit because you’re giving up intrinsic value.

✅ Best Play?
Moderate Aggressive: Roll to $20 strike (pay ~$2.90 debit).
Keeps you in for 2 more years of upside.
Stock has to go beyond $22.90 for your new position to profit from here.
Conservative Aggressive: Roll to $17.50 strike (pay ~$1.90 debit).
Easier breakeven, still $5 room.

🔥 Alternative: Sell half of your position (take profit) and roll the other half up for max upside. But since you have 1 contract, that’s not possible unless you open a second call.

body:
😈A Madame 8 loss porn production😈

🎧🎤 Unravel me – Sabrina Claudio 🎧🎤

Gentlemen, I get it. 

It’s an awkward question.

How do you know when she’s done having fun?
 Same with stocks—you need to know when to pull out before things get messy.

Today, we’re diving into Loss Porn with some anatomy lessons for traders:

👉 For each stock, check: ✅ Support & Resistance Levels ✅ RSI (Relative Strength Index) ✅ 20-Day EMA ✅ Trading Volume

Every stock is shaped a little different. But the anatomy? Same rules apply. If you don’t know how, take a screenshot and feed it to ChatGPT. She won’t mind.

🍑 Lesson 1: The First Moan – Reading the Signals Before the Climax

Just like you don’t assume the first moan means “game over,” the first green candle doesn’t guarantee a breakout.
Key Points:

🔍 RSI rising above 70 = She’s getting hot, but might be peaking.

⏳ Don’t exit too early—wait for 2-3 candles above breakout line for confirmation.

🕯️ Patience matters: unfinished candles = unfinished business.

🍓 Lesson 2: The Fake-Out – False Breakouts & Pillow Talk
Ever thought she was close, but she was just… adjusting the sheets? That’s a false breakout.

Key Points:
❌ Happens near resistance levels—stocks love to tease.
📊 Volume is your tell: Big moans = big moves. Silence? Probably nothing.

✅ Rule: Wait for the candle to close before acting.

🍒 Lesson 3: The Climax Indicator – When She (or the Market) is Done

How do you know she’s had the big O? Body language changes—so does your chart.

Key Points:
⭐ Reversal candles (shooting star, doji) = the mood shifted.

📉 Volume spike → fade = after the storm, silence.

🔻 RSI dropping after peak = trend exhausted.

💋 Lesson 4: Afterglow or Ghosting – Hold, Exit, or Round Two?

Sometimes she cuddles, sometimes she ghosts. Same with stocks.
Key Points:

➖ Sideways trading = afterglow (trend taking a breather).

 🏃 Sharp reversal = ghosting (pack your bags).

✅ If price stays above 20-day EMA, round two is possible.

🍷 Lesson 5: The Walk of Shame – When You Stayed Too Long
You ignored the signs—she’s already dressed, phone in hand, and you’re still lying there.

Key Points:
🚨 Support broken = She’s leaving.

⚠️ Volume flatlines = No excitement left.

🚕 Trailing stop = your Uber ride—set it before things get awkward.

📉 Where Does MTPLF Fit In?

Being impatient cost 40% or $689 and that’s not including the $100 international fee round-trip for the visit.

For now, I’m chasing partners who break me off weekly or show faster, long-term growth.

title: 1️⃣ of 2️⃣Crypto Basics in 5 Min: From Bitcoin to Leverage Trading
body:
⭐️Cryptocurrency is digital money built on blockchain technology—a decentralized system that records transactions on a public ledger without banks or middlemen. 

It’s borderless, secure, and transparent, making it one of the most revolutionary financial innovations of our time.


⭐️So, how does it actually work? Every crypto transaction is stored in “blocks” and verified by miners or validators, not traditional institutions. 

Once confirmed, it’s permanent and tamper-proof. No single entity controls the network, which makes it resistant to censorship and centralized failure 


⭐️There are different types of crypto assets you should know about:
* Coins – These are native to their blockchains, like Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH).
* Utility Tokens – Provide access to services, such as paying for gas fees on Ethereum.
* Security Tokens – Digital versions of traditional assets, like stocks or bonds.
* Stablecoins – Pegged to real-world currencies like USD for stability (e.g., USDT, USDC).

🤓Where Do Meme Coins Fit In?

Meme coins, such as Dogecoin (DOGE) or Shiba Inu (SHIB), are tokens often created as jokes or based on internet memes, but many have grown into massive communities with billions in market cap. 

They usually fall under the altcoincategory and don’t always have strong utility, but thrive on community hype, social media influence, and speculative trading. While fun, they’re highly volatile and risky compared to mainstream crypto assets.


⭐️Among all these, Bitcoin remains unique. Created in 2009, it’s the original cryptocurrency and has a fixed supply of 21 million coins, making it scarce like digital gold. 

Unlike most altcoins, Bitcoin doesn’t aim to power apps or smart contracts; its main role is as a store of value and inflation hedge.

⭐️But what about leverage trading in crypto? Here’s where things get interesting—and risky. Trading crypto with leverage means borrowing capital to amplify your exposure. 


For example, if you use 5x leverage on $100, you control $500 worth of crypto. A 10% price move in your favor equals a 50% gain—but the reverse is also true. 


A small unfavorable move can wipe out your position quickly. This is why leverage is often called a “double-edged sword.” Always use stop-loss orders and never risk more than you can afford to lose.

Why It Lost Money

⭐️ Expired Direction: A weekly call with a $215 strike requires AAPL to climb above that before expiry on August 1 or 15 (depending). At ~$209, it had no intrinsic value.

⭐️ Time Decay: Weekly options decay fast. Ironically, even if AAPL held steady at the strike, decay would eat into the premium rapidly.

⭐️ Bid/Ask Spread & Liquidity: The mid‑price was ~$2.60 with a bid at $2.58 and ask at $2.61. Even that was a marked-down mark-to-market value from the average entry at $4.13—noticeable slippage occurred.

On April 2–10, global markets plunged due to sweeping Trump‑administration tariffs (on China, EU, India, etc.), creating panic selling across major indexes including AAPL-heavy Nasdaq While markets recovered by June, mounting fears about macro volatility persisted in late July.


2. Apple-Wide Weakness in Big Tech
In 2025, Apple was the worst-performing “Magnificent Seven” tech stock (down ~16–20% YTD), dragged by trade-war tariff threats and slow AI

On July 31 (after market), Apple posted solid Q3 results: $94 b revenue (+10% YoY), iPhone up 13%, services up — beating expectations Yet investors weren’t convinced—stock only rallied briefly then fell ~2.5%, signaling skepticism despite beat

⭐️Advice number one: try not to sell your shares on a red day. Try to sell them when the market is generally green. 

Squeeze all the money you can out of your shares. Try to be patient. 

With that being said 

⭐️TLDR:  I would sell a covered call ITM with a strike of $7.50. This expires August 15. It looks like the premiums are pretty high you can get 400 or $500 instantly. And your shares would be sold by the end of the next week.

Your shares are probably going to be exercised and taken away and you’ll get about 7K in cash

But it is generally better to exit your losers early. 

🤔Why not just sell your shares today?
You could do that. But either way you’re gonna be taking a loss. But you could watch the market and wait for a higher price than seven dollars. Taking a chance that it might get higher and you can sell your shares there.

🤔You could set a sell limit order. And just decide to sell your shares at a certain price. But again the likelihood of it being $12 at the end of two weeks is not good..


🤔Why sell now? 

The likelihood of $PEW going to $12 and beyond to recoup your losses over the next 2 to 3 months is very low 

You sound like someone who needs your money quickly. 

If you did not need your money quickly, you could always just wait and see what happens.

If you’re always worried about what another man does, I call it riding their dick. Big turn off. 

And if you get thrown off by one big loss, what you’re telling me is you don’t believe you can win again.

Sure, I am madam 8,  I can stroke a bruised ego back upright — but there are only so many times a gentleman can ask me to do this. before I start to wonder if you should learn, to do it by himself.

Shout-out to the shorter guys, because they tend to carry this “🍆” energy I enjoy so much.    Yep .  Even more than the ones who have everything going for them.🤷‍♀️


So let me share one of my biggest trading losses — because I recently asked that of my followers . Congrats to @CYNCE  who walked away the winner and got 6,969 coins for it. 

👇So here’s mine: a time I had big energy… and got humbled.

The Trade: NVDL $52 Call — From Ego to Lesson Learned
✨ Buy: 2/24 at $19.86 ($1,986 total cost) — feeling unstoppable.

✨ Sell: 4/17 at $0.69 ($68.96 credit) — took a $1,917 loss.
✨ Why? I closed right in the middle of tariff chaos. On April 2, the “Liberation Day” tariffs hit the market. Tech stocks — especially NVDA — stumbled, and a leveraged ETF like NVDL doesn’t just wobble, it faceplants.

What If I’d Held the Call?
✨ By August, NVDA was up roughly 40% from my entry. That $52 call could’ve been sitting in VIP territory — easily deep in the money, and worth several multiples of my entry.
✨Instead, I closed early, let the macro noise push me out, and missed the full summer rally.

What If I’d Rolled Out to August?
✨ Rolling the call forward could’ve let the thesis play out.
✨ I’d have sidestepped the April panic, kept exposure through the rebound, and walked away with orgasmic level, profit instead of quiet night.
✨ This was a textbook example of not letting short-term ego bruises make me bail on a valid long-term setup.

• Resets daily — not built for long-term.

• News/events can spark big Monday gaps.

• Strong conviction on Monday’s move.
• Low weekend catalyst risk.
• Ready to exit quickly if wrong.

🚫 When Selling is Smarter
• Target move already hit.
• Choppy market ahead.
• Lock in profits before decay eats them.

💡 Rule of thumb: Leveraged ETFs are for tactical, short-term plays — not weekend buy & forget.

title: Rolled my $SOFI $20 strike, $230 gain
body:
I will let chat. GPT explain this move to you. 


But this original tactic, I learned from invest with Henry YouTube videos . Very interesting and it’s becoming a new favorite trick for this one trick pony.


Basically you get to lock in the gains on your leaps , without closing the call out completely and maintaining a bullish view on the stock.

Anyhow, this adds $250 to the pot here.
Will use it to buy my weekly $SCHD 

💚💚💚🤗chat
I see your position: you hold 2 SOFI $18 Calls expiring 5/15/26, bought at $6.35, currently worth $9.35 each. 


You’re up about +47% total ($600 gain). Your goal is to lock in some profit but stay near the $18 strike (similar directional bet).
Here’s how you could think about rolling:


🔄 Rolling Approach
Sell to close your current $18 calls (bank the ~47% gain).
Buy a new call with a similar strike ($18 or nearby) but a later expiration or cheaper premium, depending on what’s available.


📊 Based on Your Screenshots
Current contract: SOFI $18 Call – exp. 5/15/26
Bid/Ask: $9.30 × $9.40 (tight spread).
Greeks: Delta ≈ 0.82 (very sensitive to price changes), Theta ≈ -0.008 (low time decay due to long expiry).
Because this contract is already long-dated (2026), “rolling” usually means:
Same strike, further out in time → But you’re already out to 2026, so there may not be later expirations yet.
Higher strike, same expiration → Lock in profit while staying bullish (e.g., roll up to the $20 or $22.5 call).


⚖️ Example Roll Ideas
Close $18 Calls → Open $20 Calls (5/15/26)
You take profit on the $18s.
Buy cheaper $20s, freeing up capital while still participating in upside.
Close $18 Calls → Spread ($18/$25 Call Spread, 5/15/26)
Lock in gains on the $18s.
Use some proceeds to buy the $25s.
Caps upside but significantly reduces cost risk.


✅ Key Takeaway
Since your $18 calls already have deep time value (delta 0.82), rolling up to a slightly higher strike with the same expiration is the cleanest way to:
Lock in gains (sell expensive $18s)
Maintain bullish exposure (buy cheaper $20s or $22.5s).

🕳️ 1. The Support Hole

- Look for strong support levels where the stock price has bounced multiple times.
- Example: If SOFI keeps bouncing off $20, that’s your indoor swingset. Entering calls there gives you more cushion if things dip.

🕳️ 2. The Breakout Hole

- Watch volume spikes + resistance breaks.
- Example: Tesla hovering at $200 and suddenly surging on big green candles — that’s entry  time. Calls entered here ride the momentum.

🕳️ 3. The Sentiment Hole

- Track market indicators like:
    - VIX cooling off (fear subsiding 😅)
    - RSI around 30 (oversold = bargain bin)
    - MACD crossing bullish.
- Example: Nvidia RSI dipping into oversold, VIX calm, and a MACD cross? That’s a glory tunnel worth sliding into.

🕳️ 4. The Earnings Hole 

- Risky but juicy: entering right before earnings if you expect a blowout.
- Example: Amazon showing strong retail data + cloud growth → buying calls before earnings can feel like Vegas… but just like Vegas your money go there and not come home with you


🕳️  5.  The 20% Discount Hole ( my favorite😈)

- A 20% decline often signals major support forming, especially if the stock had a strong trend before.
- Many investors (and algos) see this as a “buy the dip” opportunity.
- Example: A stock goes from $100 ➝ $80. That $80 level could become psychological support, where value buyers step in.

🕳️ 6. The Capitulation Hole

- If volume spikes and RSI plunges when the 20% drop hits, that’s often capitulation — the removing a bra before a bounce.
- Example: Nvidia or Tesla in past sell-offs — they tank hard, then bounce like a silicone when weak hands are gone.

body:
A safe drama free space to discuss these two plays
if you wish. 


Analyzing the data beginning, October 2024 

📉📈 UPS vs RXRX: A Tale of Two Very Different Declines

When you compare a global shipping giant like United Parcel Service (UPS) with an AI-driven biotech innovator like Recursion Pharmaceuticals (RXRX), you wouldn’t expect their stock charts to rhyme. Yet, since October 2024, both names have trended downward—albeit for very different reasons and with very different volatility.


🚚 UPS: The Steady Slide
October 2024 Price: Around $126

Current Price (Aug 2025): Around $87–88

Change: Roughly –30% decline in less than a year

UPS has been weighed down by slowing global shipping demand, rising labor and fuel costs, and macroeconomic uncertainty. Unlike a biotech, the company doesn’t see wild price spikes—but the steady erosion has hurt long-term holders.

12-month total return: About –25% to –28% even when factoring in dividends.

Trend: Both the primary (long-term) and secondary (shorter-term) trend remain negative, showing no sign yet of a major reversal.



🧬 RXRX: The Volatile Biotech Ride

October 2024 Price: $6–7

Recent Price: Around $4.8–5

Change: –28% to –30% YTD

RXRX’s story is much more volatile. Shares briefly spiked to $12+ in early 2025, fueled by biotech enthusiasm and speculation around its AI-driven drug discovery platform. But the rally fizzled, and the stock has drifted back to the mid-$4s.


2024 Performance: Ended the year down ~31%.
2025 YTD: Roughly –28%, despite temporary rebounds of 15–20% in short bursts.

Volatility: RXRX carries a beta near 3.5—about three times the volatility of the broader market.

title: 🔮I can predict the future: @RallyVirtue817 🔮
body:
￼ so this post is for @RallyVirtue817 

This user is interested in future’s trading. That is something I don’t do. 

But here is an answer from chat that I thought lurkers would be interested in 

Anybody who is well-versed in futures, can below and make a comment . 

Excellent question 👍 — both options trading and futures trading involve derivatives, but they work differently in terms of rights, obligations, margin, and how profits/losses play out. Here’s a clear breakdown:


📊 1. Underlying Asset
Options Chain: Contracts on stocks, ETFs, or indexes. Each option typically represents 100 shares of the underlying stock.


Futures: Contracts on commodities (oil, gold, wheat), financials (Treasuries, currencies), or stock indexes (S&P 500 futures). One futures contract size is standardized (e.g., 1 crude oil contract = 1,000 barrels).


🔑 2. Rights vs. Obligations

Options:
Call Option Buyer → Right (not obligation) to buy stock at strike price.
Put Option Buyer → Right (not obligation) to sell stock at strike price.
Options can expire worthless if not exercised.


Futures:
Obligation for both parties. Buyer must purchase, seller must deliver, at the agreed future price/date (though most close/roll positions before delivery).

No “optional” aspect like with options — both sides are locked in.


💵 3. Premiums & Cost
Options: You pay or collect a premium upfront. Premium = the most you can lose as a buyer.
Futures: No upfront premium. Instead, both sides post margin collateral and settle daily profits/losses (mark-to-market).


⚖️ 4. Risk Profile
Options:
Risk for buyers = limited (premium paid).
Risk for sellers (writers) = unlimited for calls, large but defined for puts (if assigned).


Futures:
Risk = unlimited in both directions. If crude oil falls $10/barrel, and you’re long 1 contract, that’s a $10,000 loss instantly.


📈 5. Expiration & Settlement
Options: Expire weekly, monthly, or LEAPS (up to 2–3 years). Most are American-style (can exercise any time).
Futures: Expire quarterly/monthly. Some settle in cash (e.g., index futures), others by physical delivery (e.g., oil, corn).


💡 6. How They’re Used
Options:
Hedging (protect stock positions).
Income (covered calls, cash-secured puts, wheels).
Speculation with defined risk.


Futures:
Hedging commodities/currencies (airlines hedge jet fuel, farmers hedge crops).
Speculating on macro trends (S&P 500, interest rates, gold).

Access to leverage with smaller capital upfront.


🏆 Key Takeaway
Options Chain = “rights + flexibility” → you choose if you exercise. Lower upfront cost, risk capped if buying.
Futures = “obligations + leverage” → locked contract, high leverage, daily mark-to-market. Bigger potential profits, but also much bigger risks.


👉 If you’re coming from stock options trading (like wheels, covered calls), futures will feel way more leveraged and less forgiving — but they’re powerful for hedging or speculating on indexes, commodities, or rates.

From chat

  1. Trend Confirmation
Look for a downtrend already in motion (lower highs, lower lows).
Use the 200-day moving average — if price is trading below, puts have stronger backing.
Shorter MAs (20- or 50-day) crossing below long-term averages = bearish crossover.

2. Breakout Signals
Support Breakdowns: Key levels of support failing (previous lows, major round numbers).
Bear Flag / Rising Wedge: Temporary bounce within a downtrend that’s about to roll over.
Head & Shoulders: Neckline break signals continuation lower.
Volume Spike on a Red Day: Heavy sell volume suggests institutional unloading.

3. Momentum Indicators
RSI > 70 and rolling down = overbought turning bearish.
MACD Bearish Cross: Signal line crossing under MACD line.
VWAP rejection: Price can’t sustain above VWAP intraday.

4. Volatility Context
Rising IV (Implied Volatility) boosts put premiums.
Best to enter before IV spikes (earnings, bad news catalysts).

title: 🦊💚 Keep it FOXEY: How to Grow Your Followers field trip 💚 🦊
body:
🎧🎶 “ Foxey Lady” – Jimi Hendrix 🎶🎧
 

💚💚💚💚💚😙😚


Back-to-Basics September.

Lesson 1: Be a confident cat !
 Lesson 2: The Anaconda says K I S S.

Lesson 3: 

This is AH ￼

We all know what sells: 😈

Money sells.
 And yes… that’s sexy.

So keep it foxy, like Jimi says

Don’t Just Post Gains 💰

Yes, show your wins. 

But don’t waste the chance to gain new followers.


Think of it like foreplay — tell the story before the climax.
ESPN doesn’t just say “They won the championship.”

 They show the missed field goals, the snowy day, the family in the hospital.
 They unravel the drama. That’s what hooks people.

Market about to close. You were stepping into a meeting. The pressure is from margin. A looming red candle was beginning to form.

Add the Details ✍️

Did your gains pay off a mortgage?
 Did you write the check, kiss the envelope, and slap it in the mailbox?
 Or did you just click a box online and watch your balance melt to zero?

How did it feel? That’s the story your followers want.

Why It Works 🔥

Posting gains with emotion makes people fantasize about you.
 They want to feel it too.

 And one day — with your leadership , they will. 

So keep it foxy. 🦊 

Don’t just post numbers, post the story.

Tell It Again 📺

ESPN runs the same saga again and again — because drama never gets old.

It’s true in the bedroom. It’s true in the market. It’s true in the music.

Timing is everything.

Do the same:

Post your old wins on a red day to lift spirits (and stop your followers from overtrading).

Drop those amazing earnings from two years ago - a week before earnings.


Share stories.  remember your new followers haven’t seen yet.

Every retelling is a teaching point, a learning point. 
Become legend

Keep it “FOXEY”.

Next up was phantom 👻. If you notice I still have my original AH coin on there🥰

 I jokingly referred to it as a leap. 

I bought it and never sold it. So I don’t consider I lost money on the coin. It’s more of a souvenir of fun times long gone.


Last is BLOFIN that’s where I feel most comfortable trading leveraged crypto. If a token is not on there, I don’t trust it as a coin.

Again, crypto is relatively new to Robin Hood. In the US, you cannot trade leverage crypto on Robin Hood but I hear that is coming.

Depending on that interface, I may get out of bluefin altogether

But for now, I will just move all my Solana and Ethereum off of the phantom and Coinbase onto RobinHood. It’s just easier, simpler, more accessible. This is an example of why $HOOD will do well overtime. I think they beat all these other platforms hands-down. It’s only a matter of time before everybody makes this trade. Especially if crypto is gonna grow in the US market.

title: NSFW: 😈💍 the downsides of commitment, 💍 😈
body:
😈 A Madam 8 Loss Porn Production 😈 

🎧🎶 “ Should  I stay or should I go (remastered, )🎶 🎧 - the clash

Darling, you got to let me know Should I stay or should I go?
If you say that you are mine I'll be here 'til the end of time

💍 They say it’s whatever everyone should aspire to:

Find a good one. Settle down.
And if you choose your options correctly… you might even get paid in the process.
That’s right passive income— it can pay your bills, take care of the kids, cover brunch with the girls. 
Weekly, monthly, quarterly? 
Girl —  just say YES.
A good partner’s got you covered.
 I’m talking about covered calls.

🧨 But… It’s Not All It Seems

There’s a contract involved. And this week’s Loss Porn is about the dark side of commitment

Covered calls are a double-edged sword that cuts both ways.
In the beginning, everything seems great. 

You anticipate some growth. 
Maybe not a huge move, but something sweet and stable.
Then life happens.
Maybe there’s a hotter ticker that catches your eye. Or maybe it’s your partner (the stock) that glows up so hard… you can't afford to keep them anymore.

To hold on, you’ll have to pay up. Or lock them in with a new promise.
So now you’re stuck wondering

🎤🎧🎶
Should I stay or should I go?
🎤🎧🎶


💔: $QBTS & $OKLO

$QBTS — The One I Underestimated
I listened to the gossip. Thought it wouldn’t amount to much. So I sold a $4 covered call for a lil’ income. You know, just in case.
Back to the bedroom and  👀 $QBTS is now over $26.78. That call I sold? It’s worth $22.73, and I'm sitting on a -972% return.


To close it now would cost me over $2,200. What did I collect? A measly $2.12 credit. 😐
I didn’t think I’d want to hold on.
I had already made enough money off these shares. But now that it’s all grown up, 
suddenly... I’m emotionally attached. Classic.

🎤🎧🎶
It's always tease, tease, tease
You're happy when I'm on my knees
One day it's fine and next it's black
So if you want me off your back

🎤🎧🎶


$OKLO — The One I Did Everything Right With… and Still Lost Control

From the beginning, I knew $OKLO was going places. It was a referral from a friend I trust — strong bones, sexy chart, nice family.

So I did the “responsible” thing:
👉Bought 100 shares at $27.88
👉Sold a $80 call expiring in 2027
And now? Stock is at $136.30.
 That call I sold? Sitting at -171.83% loss on its own. I already rolled it up and out once… and now it’s miles ITM again.

$OKLO is just getting too pricey to keep up with. Sure, I’ve got a couple years to figure it out… But it’s already weighing on my soul


🎤🎧🎶
If I go, there will be trouble 
And if I stay it will be double

🎤🎧🎶


Life lessons😔💍

💎I’ve learned that if you’re expecting rapid growth, it’s best to leave them uncovered. I’ve done this now with $SOFI and $ASTS.

💎Try not to sell calls or your shares during earnings, anticipated news, or dividend payout weeks

my decision? 

👉Whether I buy to close
👉 Whether I roll up or roll out
👉 Or if I just let go with grace

I’ll keep you posted

🎤🎧🎶

This indecision's bugging me
 (esta indecisión me molesta)
If you don't want me, set me free
 (si no me quieres, líbrame)
Exactly whom l'm supposed to be 
(dime, ¿qué tengo ser?)

🎤🎧🎶

title: Decisions : pt 2- Downside to commitments ￼
body:
This is a follow up to my “loss porn” I posted yesterday.

https://afterhour.com/883Ismygovtname/1aM/nsfw-the-downsides-of-commitme

The TLDR for the broke folks

Sometimes it’s best to let a good thing go💍

💎If you’re covered call gets deeply ITM. Do not roll it.

Just let the shares be exercised.

💎If you have the capital and you think that the stock will trend upward even further, just buy shares right than there and continue to follow the trend upwards. 

👉 my vote is Do not buy back the call. 

I call this laying another contract down in preparation for your shares to be exercised

💎Swing the shares for profit. 

Or wait till it hits its peak, then sell a covered call at the top.

Let the shares drop down in price and you pick up free premium from your cc. 

💎Small portfolios : You will not see options chain values for your covered calls until they are moving. 

So believe your thesis and conviction for high growth stocks. 

Lots of people with large portfolios cannot understand this. Stocks like $GOOG, $MSFT , $NFLX or $TSLA have large options chains. They’e literally priced out in 50 Cent increments.

They cannot understand how options strikes or certain premiums, may not be available at certain times. For instance, $OKLO was not priced out to $80 when I first purchased it much less $130 . People with large portfolios, may not understand how you can pick the wrong strike.

Do not wait for the options Chain to reflect your thesis.

💎Deltas change with news.

👀High growth stock ( high IV ratio) will take a .01 Delta to a .8 Delta in a week. 

💎So if you’re expecting a volatile week. Do not chance it just don’t put a covered call on your shares.

In 1841, the Russian-American Company sold Fort Ross to John Sutter, a Mexican citizen of Swiss origin,. The agreed price was $30,000, but some Russian historians claim the amount was never fully paid—leaving the legal title in question.

However, a later biography of Sutter reports that Peter Burnett, acting as his agent, paid $19,788 in gold and notes to the Russian agent William M. Steuart on April 13, 1849, settling the outstanding debt.

After passing through several private owners (including George W. Call), the Fort Ross stockade and 3 acres were purchased by the California Historical Landmarks Commission in 1903. By 1906, the site was turned over to the State of California for preservation as a state historic monument.

no matter what they say,

Other tracks to set the mood:
 🇼🇸 Tele I’a O Le Sami – The Five Stars (Samoa)

👉 https://youtu.be/hO7OZc_S8w8?si=4gv-3WE7qw5cAzdb


💚💚💚💚💚💚
So we continue our geography lesson—finding American places that hint at international lineage. 

but pause

America doesn’t just mean the 50 states. How about the territories.


Could you imagine being American and people not believe you?

actually, scratch that 🤔

Let's try a different angle
 when it comes to territories, I always wonder what that world in limbo feels like.


Territories pay some U.S. federal taxes (not full federal income tax—local versions instead).
Residents cannot vote for president in the general election.
They elect a non-voting delegate to the U.S. House of Representatives.
They have no U.S. Senators.
They can serve in the U.S. military.


And yet—this here is STILL ￼America. 🇺🇸

The Territories & Their Price Tags

Puerto Rico
Acquired: 1898 (Spanish–American War)
From: Spain
Cost: Bundled in Treaty of Paris with Guam & Philippines. (U.S. paid $20M, mostly attributed to the Philippines. Puerto Rico had no separate purchase price.)
Guam
Acquired: 1898 (Spanish–American War)
 From: Spain
Cost: Part of Treaty of Paris package; no distinct price.
Philippines (no longer U.S. territory)
Acquired: 1898 (Spanish–American War)
 From: Spain
 Cost: $20M (primary focus of the payment).
Note: Became independent in 1946.


U.S. Virgin Islands
Acquired: 1917
 From: Denmark
Cost: $25M in gold
Why: Strategic purchase during WWI to block German expansion in the Caribbean.


American Samoa
Acquired: 1899 (Tripartite Convention: U.S., Germany, Britain)
From: Partition of Samoa (U.S. got east, Germany got west, Britain withdrew).
Cost: Diplomatic deal—no money exchanged.


Northern Mariana Islands
Acquired: After WWII
 From: Japan (previous League of Nations mandate)
 Cost: None—placed under U.S. admin as Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands.
Status Change: 1975 vote for U.S. commonwealth.

title: 🥑 How I Buy the Dip (Salsa Verde Style) 🥑
body:
Because cooking & trading both take patience 💚📉➡️📈

Don’t worry, this is SFW 😎

(Yes, I do have a domestic side. I cannot be all skank all the time.😜)


Today for my followers, I reviewed some quick facts about Santa Fe, New Mexico. 

I recognize that I may have never shared how I approach buying the dips when they present themselves in the market.


Here is a fun recipe for salsa Verde, which will help with the analogy of buying the dip. 👇

https://www.marthastewart.com/1542777/easy-chile-verde

You may have your own strategy or recommendations for buying the dip. 

Or maybe you have your own personal salsa Verde tips feel free to list those too.

💚How I buy my dips💚

🥒: Make A List

Before shopping, you write ingredients.

Before trading, write a list of stocks & options you’d love to buy and the price you want them at.

🌶️ Gather Your Cash

You can’t cook without groceries.

You can’t dip-buy without cash.

Decide which options you may want to close out early if you anticipate a big dip in the market. or keep cash on hand so you’re ready when the market serves a sale.


🍅 Look for Discounts
At the store, you hunt for sales.

In the market, I look for 5%, 10%, even 20% dips to scoop up bargains.


🧄 Repeat Good Recipes

If a dish tastes good, cook it again.

If a stock or option was profitable, why not buy it again on the dip? Just add more time (theta).

🫔: Be Patient

Salsa needs to simmer.

So does your dip buy.

Seeing red is nerve-wracking, but patience pays—let the recipe finish.

🌮 Enjoy the Feast


The best part? Sharing the green gains with friends on AH.
Cooking, trading, and winning—always better together.


😳This recipe does have pork in it . Many apologies -feel free to leave it out and adapt as needed.

title: Trailing stop orders for $ASTS and $TSLL
body:
These are in the IRA

Trailing stop orders are great for time management. If you cannot be around your phone all day watching trades that are profitable.

I am swinging a few shares here. 

$ASTS is a long-term hold for me in ￼ my taxable account. 

But in the IRA, I don’t have to worry about taxes. I can just chase profits. So I’ve decided to change my strategy up just a little there. 

Set trailing stop losses for $TSLL for 5%. If it triggers, I will still be in profit if it sells at $21 I’m only selling five shares with this trailing. Stop loss. Why? $TSLL is 2X Tesla. Tesla is not going anywhere. Despite all the hate And drama surrounding it. If my 100 shares of $TSLL tank no big deal I will just sell covered calls on the way back up. This is the power of owning more than 100 shares. You can make money while your shares Are below their cost basis.

$ASTS in the IRA I only have 32 shares. So I cannot sell a covered call if the shears drop. For that trailing stop I have elected to sell 31 shares or nearly my entire position to lock in profits as needed. That one has a tighter stop loss at 3% Because I do want to sell at a profit. 
￼
Stop losses are difficult because they can interfere with your ability to gain. No stock has a smooth trajectory upward. It bounces and wiggles on the way up to blue sky. 


So as it bounces and wiggles, it might trigger your stop loss and then reverse course and continue upward. It’s painful. It’s a learning lesson. Don’t get too stressed out about it. Just learn your stock and equity and how it moves. And put an appropriate trailing stop loss on. 

Legitimate risk is an excellent follow. He does not trade options. He just does shares and he has a nice rule of thumb for trailing stop losses. I really like it. And I keep it in mind going forward.

body:
🎧 “ Deep in the heart of Texas” –  Perry Como OR Gene Autry 🎧

So I thought I’d end the week with two special cases, 

As a reminder this week’s geography lessons focused on foreign entities that once owned a part of the United States and the cities that represent their presence. 

These last two “foreign countries” weren’t really purchased they were annexed. legally added.

Today is Texas. Yes Texas was its own republic at one point.👀


And as history goes, when you take over territory without everyone’s blessing… war follows. Lives were lost, so yes, Texas came at a cost — just not the kind written on a check.


Texas broke away from Mexico in 1836, calling itself the Republic of Texas. Mexico shrugged, but the Republic held its ground until 1845, when it struck a deal to join the U.S. Mexico wasn’t thrilled — cue the Mexican–American War (1846–1848).

Pssst. Let’s not forget- from yesterday -the Alamo😇￼ ￼

Under the Compromise of 1850, the U.S. assumed about $10M in Texas’s public debt to settle things. Not a purchase, but definitely not free.

If one city screams Texas, it’s Dallas — cowboy hats, oil money, Friday night football, and a booming business scene.

📈 Market Facts about Texas

1. #1 U.S. producer of crude oil & natural gas — energy is king.

2. Nation’s leader in wind power — big hats, bigger turbines.

3. Austin & Dallas are magnets for real estate, tech, and Fortune 500 relocations.


🎶 And about our music:

 “Deep in the Heart of Texas” is the state’s anthem-in-spirit.

🧈 What’s a Spread?

In food: a spread is butter, jam, or guac on bread. In trading: a spread is two options combined to balance risk and reward.

🥑 Call Debit Spread (Bullish Recipe)

Use when: Stock is trending up but you want to limit cost. Like layering avocado + lime — keeps it fresh and affordable.
 👉 Buy a call at-the-money 👉 Sell a call further out-of-the-money

🥯 Put Credit Spread (Bullish Recipe)

Use when: Stock is steady or rising slowly.
 Like cream cheese on a bagel — smooth & steady. 👉 Sell a put at-the-money 👉 Buy a lower strike put for protection

🥩 When to Use Spreads

Best on bullish-moving stocks:
 Strong fundamentals (good ingredients) Technical support (steady pan to cook on) Not too volatile (don’t burn the dish)

🌶️ Managing the Spread

Like adjusting seasoning while cooking: If stock moves your way, let it simmer. If flavor (stock trend) changes, close early before it spoils.

🍯 Enjoy the Meal

Spreads give flavor & balance — just like food.
 You don’t always need a whole entrée (buying straight calls/puts).
 Sometimes a good spread makes the perfect bite.😋

Hawai‘i was its own kingdom. 👑
For centuries, the islands were ruled by native monarchs, culminating in the unified Kingdom of Hawai‘i (1795).

Enter the U.S. sugar barons and missionaries. By the late 1800s, economic interests outweighed royal power.

In 1893, Queen Liliʻuokalani was overthrown. In 1898, the U.S. officially annexed Hawai‘i.

Statehood came much later: 1959 — making Hawai‘i the 50th star on the flag.

Cost:— just like Texas, annexation wasn’t free. It didn’t come with a monetary exchange. It came with protests, displacement, deaths and the lingering debate of sovereignty that still exists today.

Here’s a clear breakdown of the four main vertical spreads shown in your image — plus when, why, and on what type of stocks each works best 👇

🧩 1️⃣ Call Debit Spread (Bullish)

What it is:
 You buy a call at a lower strike and sell a call at a higher strike with the same expiration. You pay a net debit (cost).

Goal: Profit when the stock price rises moderately — not necessarily to the moon, just enough to reach your sold call.

Best for: ✅ Stocks that are bullish but not explosive ✅ When you want defined risk and cheaper entry than buying a naked call

Example scenario: $AAPL, $MSFT, $NVDA trending upward but with steady momentum — not meme volatility.

💰 2️⃣ Put Credit Spread (Bullish)

What it is:
 You sell a higher-strike put and buy a lower-strike put. You collect a net credit (income).

Goal:
 Profit when the stock stays above your short put — basically, you’re selling insurance that the stock won’t crash.

Best for:
 ✅ Stocks that are neutral-to-bullish ✅ When implied volatility is high (you collect richer premium) ✅ Traders who like earning steady income on strong names

Example scenario:
 $TSLA, $AMZN, $META right after earnings with solid fundamentals — you expect stability or a slow grind upward.

📉 3️⃣ Put Debit Spread (Bearish)

What it is:
 You buy a higher-strike put and sell a lower-strike put. You pay a debit.
Goal: Profit when the stock drops, but with limited risk and cheaper entry than buying a straight put.

Best for:
 ✅ Stocks that are losing momentum ✅ When you expect a controlled pullback rather than a collapse

Example scenario:
 $NVDA or $QQQ when overbought on RSI or near resistance; you want to short carefully without unlimited risk.

🧱 4️⃣ Call Credit Spread (Bearish)

What it is:
 You sell a lower-strike call and buy a higher-strike call. You collect a credit.

Goal:
 Profit when the stock stays below your short call — or drifts sideways.

Best for:
 ✅ Stocks that are neutral-to-bearish ✅ When implied volatility is high and you want consistent premium income

Example scenario:
 $SPY, $QQQ, or overextended tech names near highs — you expect consolidation or minor correction.

💚 Madame 8 Tip
💋 Think of spreads like cooking:

Debit spreads = You spend to make something hot — you’re betting on movement.

Credit spreads = You get paid to let things simmer — you’re betting on stability.

Both reduce risk compared to going naked — the trick is choosing the right “recipe” for the stock’s behavior.

2. 📊 Risk vs. Return Scatter Plot
Concept: Plots different assets based on expected return and volatility (standard deviation).

Math: Risk measured by ( \sigma ) (standard deviation).

Why it matters: Visualizes the efficiency— helping investors pick assets that maximize returns for a given level of risk

Have you ever worried if a trade is really worth it.

Wonder no more.

Yep they have math for that. 👀

The R:R ratio is a real thing that professional investors use.

Most aim for a 1:3 ratio

This means for every $100 risk the potential reward should be at least $300.

With this ratio, you don’t have to win all the time. If you just win 25% of your trades, you still will be profitable overall 

I’m a keep it basic here. But if want to learn more about this concept, here is a nice simple to understand article from our world neighbors in India👇

body:
Busy domestic Saturday for me.

But I wanted to do an update on that crypto leverage play for any people who are learning 

I also appreciate those who are checking on me 🤣
@TradesOnTheRocks  When I went back to look at that post, it looks like I don’t even think I posted a picture

And I was pretty brief, not very descriptive but I never intended anyone to follow me. I was just being transparent on what I was doing in the background.

Anyhow

Obviously, this trade is not going well. No magical X post from daddy T. We all know he can be stubborn so no big deal.


Hindsight, I probably could have set a crypto short. And probably I can still do so as it’s approaching some support levels that look like they might break.


I put arrows because the screen for BLOFIN, ￼ for noobs might be kind of confusing.

But yes, I did set a stop loss.

👉 it’s at 170. It is abbreviated with the initials SL at the bottom left-hand corner.

BLOFIN is nice because it also tells you the liquidation price. For me SOL would have to get down to 151. My SL as well above this.

👉 because I knew I would be busy and not monitoring this one. I also set a take profit. It is abbreviated with the initials TP. Also in the bottom hand left hand corner that one set at 220. I did this because some random X post might make this rip through the roof. And I wanted to get my profit off the table.

👉Note I only put $20 down. Yes, it is at 5X leverage.
Note, although I’m at about 28% loss🤪The actual USDT lost is about two dollars

￼ sometimes tight stop losses for crypto are detrimental. Because it can bob around for a while before it makes a move upward. I didn’t really check any levels before setting this trade. To avoid this, you can go in with known levels of support and resistance. But the problem is during random news these previously established levels of support and resistance get altered a bit. The TLDR is that the coin or equity might move differently when the weather changes. So your previous support resistant levels may not truly apply.

I put arrows next to the current price of SOL that’s in the middle of the screen to the right hand side.

The leverage is usually at the top left side. But it’s easily identifiable with 5X.

It’s an isolated trade. Meaning I’m not going to liquidate my whole crypto portfolio on here with one bad trade. This one will stop out and just take only the amount of money I have in futures. ￼

Now that I’m looking at it, I’m tempted to set a short, but I’m just gonna leave it alone. I don’t like to lose a lot of money. And these things can reverse quickly.

Lots of great people on here who trade leveraged crypto.
Mastergroove, ADIOKING, auratrader, marketMogul

body:

we are both on substack. 
For myself, this is where my memorable creative material will be stored for easy access😎

subscription is free.

adding that @squeezekid  is an excellent follow and may present a bull case article for $ORBS as well. Please consider giving him a follow if you enjoyed this post want DD that is balanced.



---

Dear AH,

As you know, I’m a simple-minded pink horse.

So I will do my best to keep things simple.

I believe playing the market is like playing chess

it’s not my style to go around hating celebrities, people just because they’re rich and powerful, or money

I’m a madam. I do enjoy money.

If this is a game of chess

I’m just trying to figure out the best moves to win without sacrificing too many pieces.

---

$ORBS : ￼Let’s Define the Players ♟️

The Orb is a spherical device that scans your iris or retina. 

Most people already know the back of your eye is like a fingerprint — unique. Retinal scanning for high-tech security has been featured in countless movies.

The Orb maps your eye’s features into a digital signature. Assigning you a World ID.

recently in￼ exchange for submitting your scan early, ORBS / Worldcoin offered ￼free tokens dropped straight into your wallet — an obvious move to drive adoption.

To date, millions of people have lined up around the world to get their eyes scanned. The company claims over 12 million  scans so far, with reports ranging between 10 and 12 million verified users.

---

♟️, ￼Let’s Define the Game

ORBS is the rebranded identity of Eightco Holdings Inc. (formerly trading under the ticker $OCTO). The company officially changed its Nasdaq ticker from OCTO → ORBS to reflect a new strategic direction.

The change marks the company’s adoption of a Worldcoin (WLD)-based treasury strategy and alignment with the “Proof of Human” / identity-verification narrative.

♟️ Key Pieces:

The company conducted a private placement of ~171.2 million shares at $1.46 each (plus a $20 million strategic investment) to raise ~$270 million in gross proceeds.

The plan is to use those funds to accumulate Worldcoin (WLD) for its treasury, making WLD its primary reserve asset.

The rebrand to ORBS is a symbolic alignment with the “Orb” iris-scanning hardware 👆 that underlies Worldcoin’s proof-of-human system.

The narrative now positions ORBS as a front-runner in the emerging AI / identity / authentication infrastructure space.

The TLDR:  $OCTO was a micro-cap company focused on packaging, logistics, and e-commerce services. It is now aggressively repositioning itself as a crypto / identity / authentication play.

---

♟️ A Bit of History

Around early September 2025, OCTO’s share price exploded. Reports indicate:

The stock surged over 5,600 % intraday after the announcement of the $250 million financing and the pivot toward a Worldcoin treasury.

Some sources say it went from $1.45 (Sept 5 close) to intraday highs of $82+ before closing much lower (near $45 ).

That rally was largely triggered by the announcement of the private placement, the crypto pivot, the rebrand, and the association with Worldcoin / identity tech.

Other factors included the appointment of Dan Ives as chairman, backing from BitMine (Tom Lee) and heavy retail / social-media excitement.

---

♟️What the Chessboard Looks Like Today

October 12 closing price (Friday): ~$8.00
Before all this, the stock traded around $1 – $2.

Given the magnitude of the move and the narrative shift, the share price is now extremely sensitive to **sentiment, execution, and credibility** rather than underlying fundamentals.

---

Let’s Figure Out Our Next Move

🕳️ Bear Case Thesis for ORBS

---

1️⃣ Do Not Be a Pawn in the Game of Chess

One major risk is that many new participants or speculators are being recruited purely as exit liquidity.

That is:

Investors FOMO in at or near the peak, driven by hype and momentum.

Once the price stalls or reverses, those late entrants are left bag-holding.

Early players or seasoned bag holders may orchestrate hype posts and “look how great we are” narratives to coax more buying — then unload quietly into weaker hands.

Because most retail traders don’t disclose entry prices or position sizes, it’s impossible to know who’s holding what and at what cost — a perfect setup for a shakeout.

Afterhour hype and social media promotion often signal a top before a sharp reversal.

In short: 👉Hype begets FOMO, FOMO begets recruitment, and recruitment becomes exit liquidity for earlier holders.

---

2️⃣ Open Your Eyes to the Rules

Even if the identity / authentication thesis is compelling, U.S. adoption faces major headwinds:

This here is America — we tend to be more privacy-conscious and skeptical of biometric data collection. Our Constitution and culture value individual rights and privacy.

👉 There’s a reason we’re “behind the world.” it’s because we are first. Mandating or encouraging iris scans for digital access could spark resistance, regulatory scrutiny, and public backlash.


👉 The U.S. has strict laws around biometrics (e.g., HIPAA, state privacy acts). Any violation — real or perceived — can trigger legal and reputational damage.

👉. Many Americans simply don’t trust centralized identity systems. Adoption requires time, trust, and transparency — not overnight hype.

Just because other nations adopt faster doesn’t guarantee the U.S. will follow.

---

3️⃣ In Chess, Who Customarily Makes the First Move?

Not trying to make anyone mad — it just is what it is.

👉Now that your eyes are open: Entities (corporations, governments, platforms) might use identity data to gate access, profile users, or exclude groups. The technology can be co-opted.

👉“Nothing to worry about,” right? Even if ORBS / Worldcoin claims data is deleted, the system still creates a verified identity layer that others can exploit.

👉 History says otherwise: the promise “you own your data” rarely holds once identity becomes a tradable commodity.

👉 Over time, incentives may push toward **mandatory verification**, reducing anonymity and expanding central control.

Some pics here. 


How chat has helped me point 👇



Designing the Call Debit Spread

A call debit spread = Buy a call at a lower strike + Sell a call at a higher strike, same expiration.

You pay net premium (buy leg premium minus sale leg premium). Your max risk = that net premium × 100 (for 1 contract). So to cap cost <$300, you want net premium ≤ $3.00.


Here are candidate spreads:
Example Spread A

Buy 11.00 call
Sell 13.00 call
Using midpoints:
11.00 call ~ $0.525
13.00 call ~ $0.30
Net cost ≈ $0.525 − $0.30 = $0.225 per share → $22.50 for 1 contract
That is well under $300, leaving you room for slippage or using multiple contracts.
Upside potential = (13 − 11) * 100 − cost = $200 − $22.50 = $177.50
Break-even = 11.00 + 0.225 = 11.225


Example Spread B (more aggressive)
Buy 12.00 call
Sell 14.00 call
Using midpoint:
12.00 call ~ $0.30
14.00 call (very cheap, maybe ~$0.225 or lower) — data shows 14.00 call at ~$0.225 midpoint. 
ADVFN
+1
Net cost ≈ 0.30 − 0.225 = $0.075 → $7.50 per contract
Upside = (14 − 12) * 100 − cost = $200 − $7.50 = $192.50
Break-even = 12.00 + 0.075 = 12.075

This is lower cost but requires the stock to move above ~12.08 by expiration to be profitable.

What to Consider & Adjust

Expiration date: I used near-term data. Longer expirations cost more in premium. Pick an expiration where you believe the move may occur, but ensure the premium stays low enough.

Liquidity & bid/ask spreads: The midpoints I used are idealized. You may pay closer to the ask to buy, and receive lower for the leg you sell. Always check real quotes.

Contract size: If net cost is ~$0.225, you could potentially use up to 13 contracts before hitting ~$300 (0.225 × 100 × 13 = $292.50). But that’s a lot of exposure — risk scales.
Risk vs reward: These spreads cap your maximum gain but limit your loss. Make sure that the return potential is worth the chance.

title: SFW: 🤭So many miners? Where is the Canary?? 👀
body:
😈 A Madam  8 Production 😈

🎧  Sixteen tons – Tennessee Ernie Ford 🎧


🎶 🎤
You load 16 tons
And what did you get?
Another day older
And deeper and debt 

🎤 🎶


Dear AH,

Burly, bearded men 

who may or may not be from the southern states 

have never scared me.
 I’m a Madam after all.

But I’ve found myself in a new place — the market.
 And everywhere I turn there’s another miner.

$IREN, $MARA, $RIOT, $HUT,  $BMNR, $HUT …
 They all whisper the promise of future riches

Hmm 

Well, ladies

When there are this many miners, 

I think it’s time to look for the canary.



🎶 🎤
A poor mans made out of muscle and blood
Muscle and blood
And skin and bones
A Mind thats weak
And the back thats strong
🎶 🎤



🪙 Hello, Miners

A Bitcoin miner is basically a very expensive, very loud computer that plays sudoku with lightning speed.
 Whoever finishes the puzzle first gets paid in Bitcoin — currently 3.125 BTC per block (about $190,000 at $60k BTC).

Think of it as the world’s biggest math competition with 24/7 caffeine, electricity, and fans. 

Not OF. 

But actual fans 🪭🪭 that cool the machines down.

The first miner to solve the sudoku block?
 They get the coin and the glory.
 Everyone else gets… 
heat. 🥵

Lots of it.

So that’s why there’s interest in state of the art cooling systems
 😎



🎶 🎤
I was born one morning 
when the sun didn’t shine
I picked up a shovel 
and walked to the mine

I loaded 16 tons
Of number nine coal 
And the star boss said 
“Well, bless my soul”
🎶 🎤



⛏️ Miners Make Their Money 3 ways

   🤗let’s review shall we

1️⃣ Self-Mining — digging for their own gold

This is pure mining — using their own gear to win Bitcoin.
 Example: A site with 50,000 machines running nonstop can earn roughly 135 BTC/month (~ $8.1 million at $60k BTC).

But remember — 
someone’s got to pay the power bills. 
That same site might spend $4–5 million a month just keeping the lights on.

🐤 Canary #1: if power costs rise above $0.05 per kWh, their profits can vanish faster than your Tinder match after you mention crypto.

2️⃣ Hosting — renting out space to others

Some miners act like landlords. They rent out power and cooling to other miners at about $70–$110 per kW each month.

A 40 MW facility can earn $3–4 million/month just keeping other miners’ rigs running.

🐤 Canary #2: if the site’s uptime drops below 97 %, expect angry tenants — and lost revenue.

3️⃣ Diversified Compute — flirting with AI

A few smart miners have started renting their servers to AI companies.
 Why? Because those GPU contracts can pay more than mining BTC itself.
 They’re basically saying, “Sure, I’ll mine Bitcoin — unless someone hotter comes along with an NVIDIA chip.”

🐤 Canary #3: if a miner can’t pivot into new tech, their business model ages faster than organic vegetables.


🎶 🎤
I was born one morning 
when it was drizzling rain

🎶 🎤


💸 3 Costs That Keep Miners Sweating

1️⃣ Electricity

Their biggest addiction.
 If your power bill at home makes you wince, try 150 MW at $0.045 per kWh — that’s around $5 million a month.
 Any higher, and profits start smoking like a blown fuse.

2️⃣ Equipment

Each machine (ASIC) costs around $10,000 – $15,000 and lasts maybe 3 years before it’s ancient history.
 So Imagine replacing your car every two years just to stay competitive.

3️⃣ Debt

Many miners borrow heavily to grow fast.
 Healthy miners keep debt below 2× their annual earnings; beyond that, they’re flirting with bankruptcy.

🐤 Canary #4: If a miner’s debt-to-profit ratio climbs above 3×, or their cash on hand can’t cover six months of bills, start backing away. Slowly.

🎶 🎤
Fighting and trouble 
are my middle name
🎶 🎤

🪶 Listen for Silence

What could go wrong while mining digital gold?
 Pretty much everything.

😱Bitcoin drops → miners can’t cover costs.

😱 Too many miners join → competition skyrockets, rewards shrink.

😱 Power prices rise → their margins melt.

😱 Old equipment → they can’t keep up with faster rigs.

😱 Government rules tighten → permits get pulled, sites shut down.

😵
When profits vanish, they start unplugging rigs.
 The Canary goes silent🪶


🫰🫰🫰🫰



🎶 🎤
If you see me coming
You better step aside
A lot of men didn’t
And a lot of men died
🎶 🎤


🔦 Competition : Is there breathing room?

AH loves to point at quantum and bring up comparisons to Dot com bubble. 🥱

Will there be a bitcoin miner bubble?
🧐

Seriously - Can all the bitcoin miners survive.?


⛏️In bull markets: many can print profits (BTC ↑, fees ↑), but spread of margins remains wide—cheap power + efficient fleets win bigger.

⛏️ In neutral/bear phases: the industry tends to consolidate; only the lowest-cost, best-financed players sustain positive cash flow and keep upgrading.


🎶 🎤
one fist of of iron
The other of steel
If the right one didn’t get you
Then the left one will
🎶 🎤


⛏️ A quickie: How to Spot the Survivors

Quick Reference: 🐤 Benchmarks 
☑️Power: ≤ $0.045/kWh blended
☑️ Fleet efficiency: ≤ 25 J/TH (target), upgrade path ≤ 20 J/TH
☑️ Scale: ≥ 100–200 MW deployed; multi-site
☑️ Liquidity: Cash runway ≥ 6–12 months fixed costs
☑️ Leverage: Net debt/EBITDA ≤ 2.0×; Interest coverage ≥ 3.0×
☑️ Current ratio: ≥ 1.5×
☑️ Hosting price: $70–$110/kW-mo (service component)
☑️ Capex: $250k–$700k/MW (infra build); $8–$20/TH (ASICs)
☑️ Depreciation lives: ASIC 2–4 yrs; infra 7–20 yrs

If they score well on those, they can likely survive the next crypto winter.🤩

If not — they’re the ones gasping for air when the canary stops singing.📉


💡 Pro Tip — Where to Do Your Own Research
When digging for the numbers:

👉Check SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) — every public miner must disclose this data.
👉￼ Visit Investor Relations pages for company presentations and operational updates.
👉 Browse HashrateIndex. com and Luxor Mining for standardized miner metrics.
👉 Follow Earnings Calls or Slide Decks for fleet upgrades, hash rate, and power contracts.


🎶 🎤
Saint Peter don’tcha call me 
because I can’t go 

I OWWWWE my soul to the company store
🎤 🎶
