🏛️ The US Constitution

The Constitution established the framework of the federal government, defining a system of checks and balancesamong the legislative, executive, and judicial branches.

At its founding, it provided limited protections for poor or marginalized groups.

💫￼Voting rights were left to the states.

 💫 Slavery remained legal under the Three-Fifths Compromise and fugitive slave clauses.

💫 Women, enslaved Africans, Native Americans, and non-property-holding men had no political power or guaranteed rights.

💫 Expanded rights came later through constitutional amendments:

13th – Abolished slavery
14th – Guaranteed equal protection
15th – Secured voting rights regardless of race
19th – Granted women’s suffrage

👩‍⚖️The framers were largely wealthy, educated men in the top 1–2% of society.
 👩‍⚖️Most were lawyers, planters, or merchants, not artisans or laborers.
 While a few, like Benjamin Franklin, rose from modest backgrounds, most were born into privilege or married into wealth.
 Their average age was 42, and about half were landowners who enslaved people, linking their political influence to economic power.

🏛️ Executive Branch 

The Executive Branch enforces the laws of the United States and is led by the President, who serves as both Head of State and Commander in Chief of the armed forces.

It also includes the Vice President, the Cabinet, and numerous federal agencies that carry out national policies, from defense to education to environmental protection.

The President is elected to a four-year term and limited to two terms by the 22nd Amendment. 

The office was designed to balance power with Congress, not dominate it — a system of checks and balances.

While the Constitution (Article II) outlines broad presidential powers — signing or vetoing laws, appointing judges, directing foreign policy, and commanding the military — those powers have expanded greatly over time, especially during crises and wars.

👉Historically, the presidency has been held mostly by wealthy, educated men, many with backgrounds in law, military service, or business. Only a small number have come from working-class origins.

🏛️ Judicial Branch 

The Judicial Branch interprets the laws and ensures they align with the U.S. Constitution. 

It serves as the final safeguard in the system of checks and balances, protecting individual rights and limiting government overreach.

At its core is the Supreme Court of the United States, made up of nine justices — one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices — appointed for life terms by the President and confirmed by the Senate. 

This design helps shield them from political pressure, allowing decisions based on law, not popularity.

Beneath the Supreme Court are the federal appellate and district courts, which handle the majority of cases. Together, they form a three-tier system ensuring fair application of federal law across the nation.

While designed to be impartial, the Court’s makeup and decisions often reflect broader political and cultural divides, reminding citizens that justice, though blind, is never separate from society itself.

🏛️ Legislative Branch 

The Legislative Branch makes the laws and represents the will of the people through Congress, which is divided into two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate.

This bicameral system was designed by the framers to balance power between large and small states — known as the Great Compromise.

👉The House reflects population, with 435 members elected every two years.

👉The Senate gives equal representation, with two senators per state serving six-year terms.

Congress has the power to write and pass laws, approve budgets, declare war, and oversee the executive branchthrough hearings and investigations — a key element of checks and balances.

Members of Congress are elected directly by citizens, making this branch the most representative of the public — though historically, this is not the case. 
 It wasn’t until later amendments and civil rights movements that women and minorities gained full representation.

🏛️ Independence Day

🇺🇸 When Did the US national anthem become Official?

The Star-Spangled Banner was  Written by Francis Scott Key on September 14, 1814, after witnessing the British bombardment of Fort McHenry during the War of 1812.

Originally titled “The Defence of Fort M’Henry.”

The lyrics were later set to the tune of a popular British song called “To Anacreon in Heaven.”

It became the official U.S. national anthem in 1931 by an act of Congress, signed by President Herbert Hoover.

👉That’s 155 years after the Declaration of Independence (1776).

🇺🇸 When Did the U.S. Flag Become Official?

The first official U.S. flag (the “Stars and Stripes”) was adopted on June 14, 1777, by the Second Continental Congress, stating:
 “That the flag of the United States be thirteen stripes, alternate red and white; that the union be thirteen stars, white in a blue field…” 
June 14 → Flag Day, celebrated every year in the U.S.

The flag has been updated 27 times — once for each new state, with the current 50-star version adopted on July 4, 1960, after Hawaii joined the Union

title: Altar call : come to selling options
body:
I see the sentiment and I want to join in the altar call 

Please learn to sell options

Embrace this method as the major way to grow a portfolio

I don’t care what “flavor of money” you do this with.

I do it on my own
You can do it with a paid discord
You can do it with a free discord
You can get really skanky and use (YouTube )videos

Please 🙏 Just learn how to sell options. It is a powerful way of making money for any size account. 

You can make lots of money buying options, but it is quite risky.

A buying strategy should only be 1 -5% percent of your portfolio. 

In fact, some people set up totally separate accounts just to use them to buy options with. 

Meanwhile, most of their money is passively growing in another larger account.😳

I am not a hater

If you choose to buy options as a majority of your portfolio growth. Please have a way of stacking your gains.

If you won. $100 at the casino. 

Don’t take that same hundred dollars and put it back at the table. 

Give $80 to a reliable friend (ETF) and you take $20

 if you’re really that good 

you can head back to the table with $20 and be just fine. ￼

Totally new to the market

I’m getting lots of questions on why would I buy OTM puts & calls 

Let me be clear 
👀: I recommend and prefer a selling options strategy

Please do not try to make most of your money buying options 

Buying options ￼should be like icing on a cake. It should not be your whole cake, especially if you have a small port.

You work hard for your money. Do not risk it please. 🙏 

Instead, make your money work hard for you 

Anyhow👇
Here is an example of an OTM $SPY call I bought 

Noticed that $SPY never breached above $705 but I made money on this 

Why? 

Because I bought the call when spy was going down.
The call contracts were cheap 

I did this with the knowledge that usually spy will bounce back and sometimes even strike all time high in a few days.

I don’t need it to hit my strike because just the expansion of IV ratio alone makes my call more pricey 

Please note I allow plenty of time for this to get there. 
The DTE was at least seven days if not, two weeks.👀

Make THETA your friend with investing.. 
0DTE calls are super risky. And you have to be quick. 😬

Again I recommend selling options, not buying options for a smaller port. ￼

I bought to open this call 
. So I sell it to close and I keep the profit .

I can sell to close for profit 

I only expect 30% profit or so . ￼

I only do this if I’m expecting wide swings in price.

No one can predict the future. But I think it is safe to say that $NVDIA will not have a smooth line going upward until January it would be $500 or greater

title: 💚 Weird science : Back to school 1️⃣🔬💚
body:
🎧 “Born Under a Bad Sign”-  Albert King 🎧

💚💚💚💚💚💚💚

Good morning class. 

Don’t let Monday get you down

Retrain your emotional responses

 Make Mondays something to look forward to

Yes, there is a pop quiz today.

Why do you ask?
😇


🧪🧪🧪

The classic Experiment: Walter Cannon (1915) — “fight-or-flight” response research showing adrenaline + cortisol spikes under threat.

1. Cats with severed spines or removed wrinkly surface of the brain (cortex) still displayed emotional expressions (like hissing and arching their backs) when provoked.
 → This showed that emotional reactions could occur without that wrinkly part of the brain (cortex) — supporting the thalamus as a key structure.

2. Electrical stimulation of the thalamus in cats caused immediate emotional-like responses.
 → This suggested that thalamic activation was sufficient to produce emotional behavior.

Cannon published his findings in 1927, and Bard expanded on them in his doctoral dissertation in 1928, leading to what’s now known as the Cannon–Bard thalamic theory of emotion


Here’s some extra reading👇

Psycholog breaks down the anatomy
https://www.psychologs.com/cannon-bard-theory-of-emotion/?amp=1

The classic Experiment: Solomon Asch Conformity Test (1951) — participants knowingly gave wrong answers just to match the group.

🔬Participants:

123 male college students were recruited.

Each group had 7–9 people — but only one was the true (test) subject. The others were confederates - not soldiers -but actors who knew the experiment’s purpose. 


🔬The task:

Everyone was shown a standard line and three comparison lines (A, B, C).

They had to say aloud which line matched the standard line in length — a task with an obvious correct answer.

🔬The test:
The confederates were instructed to give the same wrong answer on certain trials.

The real participant :was seated so they answered after several confederates, hearing their incorrect responses first.

🔬The results

About 75% of participants conformed at least once by giving the wrong answer.

Overall conformity rate: roughly 33% of the trials.

When tested alone (no group pressure), participants made almost no errors.


Say what?!

Why would a test subject knowingly give an incorrect answer.

1. Normative influence — the desire to fit in and avoid social rejection.

2. Informational influence — the belief that the group might know something the individual doesn’t.
This showed how social pressure can distort perception and decision-making, even in unambiguous tasks.


Here’s some extra reading👇

https://www.simplypsychology.org/asch-conformity.html


💚TLDR Lesson: Social pressure can override logic.

The classic Experiment: Baumeister et al., Ego Depletion (1998) — mental effort drains willpower and decision quality.

Participants:

College students (roughly 60 total) participated in a lab study at Case Western Reserve University.

They were told it was a taste perception study, not a test of willpower.

The task: 

Participants entered a room that smelled strongly of freshly baked chocolate-chip cookies.

On the table were two dishes — one with cookies and chocolate, the other with radishes.

Each participant was assigned to one of two groups:

🍪Cookie group: allowed to eat the cookies.

🧅Radish group: could only eat radishes and resist the cookies.

The second phase (the hidden test):

After the “taste test,” participants were asked to work on unsolvable geometric puzzles — supposedly to measure problem-solving ability, but actually to test 

persistence and self-control.

Researchers secretly measured how long they persisted before giving up.


The results

🍪Cookie eaters (no self-control required) persisted on the puzzle for about 19 minutes on average.

🧅 Radish eaters (who had to resist temptation) gave up after only about 8 minutes.

🍴A control group (no food exposure) performed similarly to the cookie group.

This showed that resisting temptation depleted willpower, reducing persistence in a completely different task soon after.


🍆Baumeister concluded that:

Self-control draws from a single limited pool of mental energy.

Once that energy is used up, performance on later tasks requiring discipline or focus declines.

It’s like a “mental fatigue effect.”

🌟This became known as ego depletion — the idea that willpower is a finite resource that can be temporarily “used up.”

The ego-depletion model was hugely influential in psychology, shaping studies on dieting, decision-making, and addiction.



Here’s some extra reading👇

https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/how-do-you-know/202011/how-willpower-wasnt-the-truth-about-ego-depletion/amp


💚TLDR Lesson: Every choice burns energy (glucose) ; tired brains make bad decisions 

😬 If  you think it doesn’t apply to you:  Try sitting through a long day of lectures  and then taking an exam after the last one.

Pattern recognition:
The classic Experiment: Kleinhans et al. (2011) — humans and even monkeys “see” faces or meaning in random images.

Participants:

30 adults — 15 diagnosed with high-functioning autism (HFA) and 15 neurotypical controls.
 All participants had comparable IQs and no neurological disorders beyond autism.
 Conducted at the University of Washington using fMRI technology.

The task: 

Participants were shown photographs of human faces displaying three emotions:
 Fear
Anger
 Happiness

Each face appeared briefly on screen while the participant lay in an fMRI scanner.
 They were asked to identify the gender of each face (not the emotion) — a clever way to ensure natural emotional processing without directly prompting it.

The second phase (the hidden test):

The researchers were not interested in gender recognition at all. Instead, they measured brain activation patterns in emotion-related regions such as:
The amygdala
The fusiform gyrus (face-processing area)
The prefrontal cortex
They wanted to see how individuals  with autism differ from neurotypical individuals when subconsciously processing emotions.

The results

Neurotypical participants showed strong activation in certain parts of the brain (the amygdala and fusiform gyrus) when viewing emotional faces.

 Participants with autism showed significantly less activation in these regions — particularly to fearful faces.

However, they often showed increased activation in other brain regions, suggesting they may use alternative cognitive pathways to process faces.

This may mean that people with autism rely more on conscious reasoning than automatic emotional understanding when reading faces.


🧠 Kleinhans concluded that:

Emotional face processing in autism involves different neural circuitry, NOT simply “less emotion.”

This helps explain social communication challenges in autism — not as a lack of feeling, but as a difference in how emotional signals are processed.

🌟The study became a landmark in autism research, illustrating that:

The autistic brain is organized differently, not deficiently.

Emotional understanding may be achieved through cognitive, rather than intuitive, routes.

The human brain is hardwired to recognize faces. But what if you can't? - capradio.org

🧪🧪🧪

The classic Experiment: Zuckerman Sensation-Seeking Scale (1979) — identified people who crave risk for biochemical reward.

Participants:

Hundreds of adult volunteers participated across several validation studies.

Included both men and women from diverse backgrounds, often college students and community samples.

Designed and led by psychologist Marvin Zuckerman at the University of Delaware.


The task: 

Zuckerman developed a self-report questionnaire to measure an individual’s tendency to seek novel, intense, and risky experiences.
 The test asked participants to choose between paired statements reflecting different comfort levels with stimulation and danger.

Examples:

 “I like to explore strange places.” vs. “I prefer familiar surroundings.”

“I enjoy wild parties.” vs. “I prefer quiet evenings at home.”

“I sometimes like to do things just for the thrill of it.” vs. “I avoid things that are dangerous.”

Their answers created a Sensation-Seeking Score, ranking participants from low to high.

The second phase (the hidden test):

Zuckerman wasn’t just interested in personality — he was studying the biology of thrill-seeking.

He proposed that people high in sensation-seeking have a lower baseline level of arousal in the brain’s limbic system and need stronger stimulation to reach optimal excitement.

This biological drive pushes them toward risky behaviors like extreme sports, gambling, or even fast driving — all in search of a chemical “high.”


The results

High sensation-seekers were more likely to enjoy novelty, danger, and unpredictability.
Low sensation-seekers preferred routine, stability, and predictability.

Men scored slightly higher on average than women, especially in thrill and adventure-seeking dimensions.

Later studies linked high sensation-seeking to dopamine activity — the brain’s reward chemical.


🧠 The study became a foundation for modern personality and behavioral neuroscience, influencing research on:

Addiction and risk-taking,

Adventure sports and creativity, and

Occupational choices (e.g., firefighters, entrepreneurs, pilots).


Zuckerman’s scale remains a powerful reminder that our appetite for excitement is written into our biology — a calibrated balance between curiosity and control.

🏃‍♀️‍➡️The Form

A good call-debit spread is like a perfect split — two points of balance:

One leg (buy call → $11) forward in hope,
One leg (sell call → $13) anchored in discipline.

Too far apart, and you pull something.
 Too tight, and you never see the full stretch.


🏊The Attempt ($ASPI)

Ticker: ASPI Isotopes Inc ($9.20)
 Play: $11 / $13 Call Debit Spread 11/7 Exp
 Cost: ≈ $1.10 each × 2 contracts = $220.16

Loss:  Closed early: sold near $0.10–$0.12 for ~ $98–$100 loss.


🚴Translation:
 I jumped into the split before the muscles were warm.
 Price ($9.20) never stretched anywhere near $11,
 so my spread stayed locked tight — no extension, no gain.


👿Where I Went Wrong

Entered too soon — momentum was cooling, RSI already stiff. 
 Strike too wide — $11 / $13 needed a major move (40 % +) in four weeks.
 Expiration too short — barely time for muscles to warm up.
 Didn’t roll or adjust when ASPI paused at $9.

🩰 In fitness terms:
 I tried to drop into a split cold and pulled a hamstring of my P/L.  

I should have found a coach who could guide me down and massage me after. 

😈

Next Time

💪 Widen gradually. Start with closer strikes ($9/$10 or $10/$11). I see some do 0.50 strikes 
 🧘‍♀️ Warm up. Wait for confirmation of the trend : the volume 1.5 times the average daily volume. RSI 50 to 65.
 ⏰ Give time. Longer expirations = better range of motion. 
 🪞 Mirror my form. Check delta ≈ 0.5 on entry; adjust my legs if it stalls.


⭐️The market rewards slow stretchers, not show-offs..

3️⃣ Cash Flow — Your Respiratory System 🌬️

What it means:
 Cash flow reveals whether a company can fund operations and growth without relying on outside money.

👉Check: 

Free cash flow (FCF): The cash generated by a company’s normal business operations — before any financing or investing.

🏊‍♀️It’s the “real money” the company produces from running its business.


Operating cash flow trends: The cash left after the company pays for equipment, buildings, and other capital expenses (CapEx).

🏊‍♀️This is the cash that can be used to pay dividends, reduce debt, or reinvest in growth.

👉Healthy sign: Positive, steady cash flow even during downturns.

I am assuming you mean selling options 

I personally think this is where everyone should start. Not buying options. You learn so much “ safely “  on the sell side 


There are some pretty decent stocks less than $500 for 100 shares that have options availability . For instance $VZLA is growing . Cheap . Not gonna go to zero type of penny stock /biopharma . 

But tbh - i would recommend a diversified portfolio to start with- 4 stocks, different sectors. Just so you can see how different equities move in the market as a whole 

So that would be minimum of 2k 
Not financial advice but if I were starting a family member off some tickers with decent options availability, cheap, low likelihood of going to zero would be 

$NIO
$ONDS
$FUBO
$BBAI 
$TGEN
$ACHR
$NVTS 
$AAL 
$QUBT

In no particular order would be a few to choose from.  Sectors move differently. They offer different premiums. 

Having 4 at once for 6 months would give you a lot of practice. After that you can get into buying calls and be ahead of the game . You will be familiar with the greeks 

Instead of buying options on &SPY - try buying options on the stocks you have watched for 6 months, the ones you have sold options on.  THEN move to your SPY 

Or hold a fraction of & SPY then watch it move for 6 months then get into buying options. 

My last tip is don’t run from red. 
I see things from a dating perspective- remember i am a madam 😈

You learn SO much about your stock on red days. Watch it- see what the bottom looks like. See what the company does. It helps you with buying and selling options. It also helps you learn if it is marriage material.

title: 🍭 sold to open a CSP $WEN🍭
body:
🍭how to sell a cash secured put

- remember you need enough cash in your account for 100 shares.

Selling options without the shares or the cash is called selling naked options 

This may be the one time in life that you will hear me , Madam 8, speak out against being naked😎

Yes, this madame wants you to be covered. 

Always have 100 shares if you’re gonna sell a call, that is called a covered call 

Always have the cash in your account if you’re going to sell a put, that is called a cash secured put 


🍭Briefly to sell a CSP or cash secured put for $WEN 

I opened up the options chain on my $HOOD account 
👉Trade
👉Trade Options
👉I made sure to select a weekly date of expiration. 

👉Make sure you’re selecting SELL above And PUT
Because that’s what you wanna do🤪

With this market, I feel more comfortable and weekly options. 

So my DTE is November/21. This Friday.


But some people choose to sell them 30 to 45 days out for slightly less income overall but also less work from week to week

🍭I chose a strike that I was comfortable getting 100 shares of $WEN and I felt like it would be a deal. For me that strike is $8.50. 

I get instant payment for putting up 100 times $8.50 or $850. I get $15 right off the top instantly in my account. 
This is for one contract. If you were selling multiple contracts, you would just multiply the $15 by how many chunks of $850 you had in your account. 

🍭You can select your own bid ask Price. If you notice the ranges between $15 and $20. The experts usually say choose a price in the middle so maybe $18 or $17. 

but since the liquidity is kind of low, they force you into five cent increments. So you must choose either $15 or $20. I chose 15 because there was a high fuel rate. This means that the contract is the hot thing right now, and it will close quickly. 

After putting in .15 or $15 for 100 shares. I review all the information and just swipe up. 

🎉Done. I’ve sold a car secured put for $WEN. 

If the share price stays below this strike by market close, I will have the fresh shares of WEN. The cash in my account, $850 will be taken out instantly and given them to the contract holder. 

In the US, it is true people can exercise the contracts early. Usually this happens closer to two days next to the date of expiration or if a stock is moving rapidly in One Direction, or the other, or has upcoming earnings

European options can only exercise on the date of expiration for my understanding 

again, you can make a pretty good premium selling puts on red days.

you should only sell options on stocks, you know, and feel comfortable owning . You never know which direction the market may swing. And you don’t want to feel uncomfortable holding shares you did not want ￼

title: $SOFI : example of buying back your covered call
body:
So today I introduced the idea that when selling covered calls , you can buy the position back when you’re in significant profit.


Some people buy it back at 50% profit 

I like to buy it back at 80% profit 


Another option is you can buy it back in profit when you think the narrative is changing. You think for whatever reason your shares might stop going down, you’re covered call is no longer profitable, the stock price might start going up. And you want to release your shares as collateral. 


🥁The TLDR: is do not be scared of selling covered calls. 🥁

With a carefully selected strike price and knowing your stock well. You can use them as money generators. 


You can buy and sell options on a stock that you own and you know that best. No more risking your capital on stocks you don’t know or callouts if you don’t want to. 

The cover call I sold on $SOFI. I bought back at profit.
I may do the same for $OPEN 

Usually, I just let these expire for 100% profit at the end of the week but giving you a different version of what you can do


Of course to buy back the car, I do have to spend money. I use some of the premium that was given to me originally.

title: 🍆NSFW:  Excuse me. Do These Look Real to You?🍆
body:
Beyond Meat vs. Real Meat: Tasty bits for those who love to gobble up controversies . 

🎧Put it in your mouth- Akinyele (feat Kia Jefferies) 🎧

🫦 Don’t act like you didn’t want it

On October 21, 2025, Beyond Meat ($BYND) announced a major distribution expansion with Walmart across the U.S. — its products (like the new “Beyond Burger 6-Pack”, Beyond Chicken Pieces, and Korean BBQ-style “Beyond Steak”) would now be available in over 2,000 Walmart stores nationwide.

The news triggered big energy : $BYND shares reportedly jumped over 80% in a single day, hitting intraday highs of around $2.91 from very soft , flaccid levels just days before.

The Walmart deal was deliciously irresistible. A strong distribution and demand catalyst — this meant: more shelves → more sales → potential business turnaround.

🤩Wam

Must have been good. 

We are still talking about it.

Beyond Meat went public on May 2, 2019.

The IPO was priced at $25.00 per share.

They offered 9.625 million shares (plus a 30-day over-allotment option on ~1.44 million additional shares) as part of the offering.

The IPO raised roughly $240 million, valuing the company at approximately $1.4–$1.5 billion at the time. 

🤩Bam

It was love at first sight. Shares opened around $46, far above the IPO price.

By the end of that day, the stock closed near $65.75 — a 163% increase from IPO price.

🤩Thank You, Maam

Within weeks: $BYND went over $100, and at its peak in July 2019, it soared to as high as ~$234.90. 

That made it one of the biggest debut success stories in recent IPO history — for a “plant-based meat” company. 


👀 Now let’s talk anatomy - 

💦$BYND meat : Engineered max fun 

Beyond Meat is a plant-based engineered protein, made from:

Pea protein isolate

Coconut & canola oils

Binders (methylcellulose)

Natural flavors

Beet juice + apple extract for color

It’s designed to look like meat, cook like meat, and bleed like meat —
 but the DNA is strictly lab-built and factory-shaped.

It’s true 😎

Beyond Meat is the culinary equivalent of a high-end dildo.
Purpose-built. Engineered for sensation. Designed to imitate the original. Innovative, sleek, and efficient. Environmentally lighter.

 But absolutely, undeniably… not the real thing.

Have you ever tried it? 

Did it feel real to you?


💦Real Meat-The Complicated, Organic Partner 

Real meat comes from real animals with:
Real biological systems

Real environmental costs

Real emotional & cultural ties

Real unpredictability

It’s the messy, high-maintenance long-term relationship version:kauthentic, familiar, natural, and resource-intensive.

Where Beyond Meat is “engineered intimacy,” real meat is “organic intimacy.”

🔥 Oooo Drama 

❤️ Team $BYND says
Engineered meat has relationship benefits 
Lower environmental impact
No animals harmed
Lower greenhouse gas footprint
Modern, sustainable, efficient￼ Life expectancy
Good for flexitarians

🐂 Team Organic  meat says:
I“Ultra-processed” ≠ “healthy”
Real food > engineered imitations
Cleaner labels
Simpler ingredient list
Less manufacturing required

Both sides think they're morally correct.
 Both sides have science they can weaponize.
 Both sides believe their version is the “real relationship.

But here’s where things get spicy …

👄where should we put it?
This is the part nobody talks about, but Madam 8 will:

If you put it here:

Product placement of $BYND next to organic meat . 
It sells better. It attracts meat-eaters reducing intake, not vegans. It becomes a “protein alternative,” not a niche food. It feels like a choice — not a statement.

This is like keeping a silicone toy in the nightstand next to your actual partner: accessible, playful, supplemental.

vs if you slide it in over there 
Product placement of $BYND in the vegetarian section 
Sales drop. The vibe shifts from mainstream to niche. Only dedicated plant-based consumers go looking for it. It stops being a “meat alternative” and becomes a “specialty food.”

This is like keeping the toy in a separate drawer under lock and key: out of sight, out of mind.
Ï
People think it’s to. Much work if they need  a quick fix. 


🎤🎶Put it in your mouth 🎤🎶

The retailers (Walmart, Kroger, Target, etc.)
Store managers + corporate merchandising teams decide where items go.

Brands can pay for better placement (slotting fees):
Eye-level shelves
End caps
Meat aisle vs. vegan aisle
Feature coolers This is known as “trade marketing,” It is not not government regulation by the FDA or state agencies

Category, managers decide whether a product is considered “meat,” “vegan,” “frozen entrée,” “organic,” etc..  This single decision can change sales dramatically


Lets compare 🍆, shall we 


Beyond Meat Sausage (≈4 links)
Production cost: ~$2.40–$3.20 Environmental cost:
Water: 1–2 gallons
Land: minimal
GHG emissions: ~90% lower than pork
Waste: industrial byproducts + packaging

Think: a sleek, rechargeable, silicone accessory. Low environmental guilt. High industrial input. Designed to replicate the original experience as efficiently as possible.

 😎Real Pork Sausage (≈1 pack)
Production cost: ~$1.80–$2.50 Environmental cost:
Water: 400–600 gallons
Feed: 4–6 lbs of grain
email Land: large footprint
GHG emission: 20–30× higher
Waste: manure, methane, runoff


Think: a real relationship with real needs. High maintenance. High environmental demand. But undeniably “natural.”

💞 oh babe, let’s not fight 
Beyond Meat is the engineered companion — purposeful, modern, sustainable, and efficient.
 Real meat is the traditional partner — resource-heavy, complex, culturally rooted, and emotionally familiar.

Neither is “fake.” 
Life expectancy Both serve a purpose. But they fundamentally change identity depending on where you put them.
On a grocery shelf… or in a bedroom drawer.
So next time you’re in Walmart or Whole Foods staring at the sausage aisle, ask yourself:

“Do these look real to you?”

Because in markets — just like in relationships — the answer depends on what you’re actually craving.

I am guilty as charged. 

Welp now that’s over

😇Here is my attempt to get out on parole 


👮What Are Warrants & Why They Matter

A warrant is basically a “buy-option” issued by a company itself — it gives you the right (but not the obligation) to purchase new shares of that company at a predetermined price (strike price), up until a specified expiration date. 

So it is like if I would have bought a call. Company just decided to give it to me for free without paying a  premium.

Unlike regular options (which are contracts between investors), a warrant is company-issued. If exercised, the company issues new shares — which means dilution is possible. 


If the stock price soars above the strike price, a warrant can become a very cheap, leveraged way to own stock — because you lock in a lower entry price today for potential upside later.



👮How Warrants could have helped me

Cheap upside exposure — If you expect the share price to rise, a warrant costs less than buying shares outright but still gives upside participation.

Lower cash used — Especially useful for investors who want exposure without investing full equity now.

Options, not obligation — You hold the right; you don’t have to exercise if the view doesn’t pan out.

Company funding tool — From the company’s side: issuing warrants can raise capital (when exercised) without immediate cash outlay. 



🚔 I had the right to remain silent $OPEN 

In my personal case, I was unaware OPEN recently announced a plan to issue tradable warrants to shareholders. 

I was distracted with personal things. I did not have the time or mental energy to investigate this. 

In fact, I thought I bought them by accident. And I even made a post about it.👇

https://afterhour.com/883Ismygovtname/bawT/dollaropen-undergoing-a-stock-


Traditional warrants carry exercise-prices at defined levels (e.g., $9, $13, $17 depending on the series). 

The idea: If OPEN’s stock recovers or rallies beyond those strikes, warrant-holders get a free ticket to additional upside — without paying full price upfront.




👮Why would a company do this?

This kind of move can shake up the mood : It gives shareholders more options , can reward long-term holders, and — if enough investors believe in the future— it can fuel demand.




🚔 What I say could be used against me

💚Risks of my warrants 

👉Dilution — When warrants are exercised, new shares are created. That can dilute the value for existing shareholders.

⭐️This is important. This may be why Browndog is upset.  ⭐️ I’m setting a bad public example to have shares diluted- which would negatively affect $OPEN shareholders in the long run.

Keep in mind I am a long-term holder of $OPEN. I currently have 430+ shares in my taxable account.

👉 Expiry risk — If the stock never reaches or exceeds the strike by expiration, the warrants become worthless.

⭐️This is important- even though I paid no money for these warrants. I don’t like the idea of losing money. If they’re in profit now. I’m in the current mood of “see  profit take profit” and I posted that multiple times before. This is commonly called “risk off behavior”. I’m not sure how long the market will keep profits around with the current trends. So if I see something profitable, you’ll see me take it off the table quickly.

👉 Volatility & time decay — Value of a warrant can drop over time if the stock stagnates.

👉 Not guaranteed returns — It’s a bet on future performance, not a sure thing.

If I did not know, I could’ve asked. 
Or just researched a little bit much more.

But again was just in a personally challenging time. 

It still is . I’m just trying to get back on the saddle early 

Anyhow, Because of this, I tried to minimize trades. 

But since I was already irritated by them being in my port. I just sold when they were in profit. I apologize to the jury.

title: 🥁A quick post for those learning selling options : Cashed out
body:
A quick post for those learning along selling options

Remember, my $HOOD, $SOFI were assigned and I I posted this upcoming assignment and what it looked like.

https://afterhour.com/883Ismygovtname/bbwI/covered-call-assignment-dollar

You don’t have to be scared, or upset

You don’t lose money. What you may lose is value 🙃

When you get the cash. You sell a cash secured put


Even though market’s not open, you can take a quick peek at what you want to do with the cash by looking at the options chain for your cash secure puts 

For those learning , So you won’t feel under pressure you can do this while market is closed . A little bit like window shopping - just know the prices are in constant flux. So they will change at market open.

Think of it as trying to locate a boat to jump on while it is in an ocean. -what you see is constantly moving according to the stocks underline trend⛵️

Make sure you select a date.  I do weekly options because of the volatility in the market under this current administration.. But note you can scroll out for a 30 or 45 days. 

👉Traditionally speaking, you should select a delta of 0.3 for the wheel 

👉If you wanna be aggressive and get back into the shares, no matter what you can select a 0.4 or 0.5 Delta 

👉If you’re just selling for premium , you don’t want to get assigned. Or perhaps you want to be assigned the shares at a very good deal ,(like only during a correction or dip for the stock ). select a Delta of 0.2 or 0.1 

I want to be back into my shares.  Around the same price that I was forced to exit -personally $HOOD. The price does not have to be a particularly good deal. Because in my mind, I already believe this company is on sale and there’s no need to be greedy.

So my Delta might be around 0.3 or 0.4 depending on how the week is feeling to me.

title: 😈So he is $ONDS -stoppable? Oh really 🙄
body:
😈This is a Madam 8 : dating lesson😈

🎧No Scrubs -TLC, (the intro - Whispering Playa is 👌)🎧



Ladies… why is it:

We dress to kill.

Girls sitting up high.

Waist snatched.

Legs *legging.*

With the **a$$ that says hello as we say goodbye.**

Toes on TEN.

But the moment *that one guy* walks up —
the one who claims he’s your MATCH,
your equal,
your future…

We immediately look for ways to **cut him down**.

Or maybe you see him chatting up your girlfriend, 

bragging🙄

how much money he’ll make,

All the places he can go,

what he can “do” in and out of the public eye…

You know that guy.

It’s not jealousy.

It’s just:

**no one is unstoppable.**

So instead of sitting quietly listening to him drone on (pun intended) about how rich he’ll be and all the awards he’ll win…

😈
Let me be that snarky friend

who pokes holes in his story

*just to see what comes out.*

Maybe the chemistry’s not there —

or maybe I’m wrong and he really is husband material.

But just for funsies…

*Let’s explore a bear-case lens on $ONDS.* 👇

🛻 🚁🛩️

Ugh — Now who RU again?

**What $ONDS actually is**

Ondas Holdings ($ONDS) is a U.S. tech company that builds **drones** and **wireless networks** used by:

railroads
police
the military

It owns several smaller companies that do things like:

👉build **autonomous drones** that take off, land, and charge themselves

👉create **counter-drone systems** that spot or stop bad drones

👉design **rail communication networks** so trains can talk to each other safely

Think of Ondas as a mix of:

**“Robots for the sky” + “Wi-Fi for trains.”**

Trying to sell to governments and big transportation giants.

🛻 🚁🛩️

1️⃣

**Girl — he is doing the MOST**

Every woman knows a man with **five side hustles** who swears he’ll be a *millionaire any day now.*

That’s Ondas.

They bought a whole collection of tech firms (Optimus, Iron Drone Raider, Sentrycs, Apeiro Motion, 4M Defense) AND they’re trying to upgrade the entire U.S. rail system with dot16/FullMAX.

That’s… a lot.

And when you have **too many moving parts**, things get messy:

It’s hard to combine all the businesses
Costs rise faster than income
Even with record sales, profits don’t show up

Ondas is selling more than ever, but it’s still spending too much to make a profit.

 Its everyday costs are growing faster than its income, so even though the company is expanding, it’s not earning real money yet.

**Q3’25:**
Record sales: **$10.1M**
Still lost money: **negative EBITDA, negative operating income**

Translation?

“His résumé looks great… but he still lives with his mama.”

🛻 🚁🛩️

2️⃣
# **Girl — you know he got four ex-wives and five kids already**

That’s **dilution.**

Ondas raised **$840 million**, but to do that they printed a TON of new shares.

👉Before fundraising: $433M in cash
👉After fundraising: ~$840M in cash
👉Shares increased by **130%** — from ~160M to ~370M
👉Each share is now a **smaller piece** of the company

This is called **dilution**, like adding water to your juice so it tastes weaker.

👀Why this matters:

If Ondas doesn’t grow fast enough to justify all those new shares, investors will pull the plug — and the stock can fall hard.

Right now the market is valuing Ondas like he already bought the mansion, the jet, and the Lambo…

But sis — he still financing his **Chevy truck**.

🛻 🚁🛩️

3️⃣
# **He say the Lambo next, but you see he still paying off his truck**

Railroads *do* want to upgrade to Ondas’s tech…
but railroads move SLOWER than a man who refuses to break up but also refuses to commit.

Even though the Association of American Railroads picked **dot16** as the future standard, none of that money hits Ondas until:

Class-1 railroads test the system
Approvals come in
Procurements get signed
Installations begin

Ondas themselves said:

 “Yeah, some of this is delayed.”

Railroads take years to approve new tech.
If anything slips, Ondas won’t see that money until way later.


🛻 🛩️🚁

4️⃣
# **He say he’s just waiting on her to sign the papers**

Ah, yes — the **FAA relationship status: “it’s complicated.”**

Ondas needs FAA approval (Part 108) to fly drones **beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS)**.

That’s basically letting drones fly without a human watching them.
It’s essential for scaling their business.

But the rule isn’t final yet.

Until FAA rules are finished, Ondas can only fly in special areas or with permission slips.

This slows down real-world use and delays growth.

If the FAA tightens the rules or delays more, Ondas waits.

🛻 🛩️🚁

5️⃣
# **Yes, he says he’s your type because he doesn’t date outside the race**

Cute… but also a red flag.

This is the **NDAA ban** on Chinese drones.

It helps Ondas because the government can’t buy DJI/Autel.
But switching gear is SLOW.

The government can’t buy drones with Chinese parts.

That helps Ondas.

But replacing old systems takes forever, so sales take a long time to show up.

🛻 🛩️🚁

6️⃣
# **His twin sister lives around the corner and hopes you two will be besties**

That’s the **rail safety system.**

Railroad tech has to pass:

FRA
FCC
AAR
safety standards
spectrum policy
interoperability tests

Railroads change slowly because everything must be extremely safe.

Any delay pushes Ondas’s revenue further into the future.

🛻 🛩️🚁

7️⃣
# **His main check is from the factory — and they just hired 20 young dudes last week**

Ondas is **overly dependent** on big government buyers.

If ONE of those contracts gets pushed or canceled?
Revenue tanks.

🛻 🛩️🚁

8️⃣
# **Your ex called with an apology and mentions his promotion**

Yes — there IS competition.

Why try something new when you have **tried and true**?

Ondas faces competitors like:

AeroVironment
Kratos Defense
Leonardo DRS
DroneShield

These companies are larger, proven, and already deeply tied into defense programs.

🛻 🛩️🚁

9️⃣
# **And then… what if**

We imagine dating this man on Hell Date.
Let’s talk scenarios.

💅

# **Scenario A — The Stress Case (aka “Girl, RUN.”)**

If investors lose confidence:

They value Ondas at only **2× 2025 sales** ($36M).
That equals an EV of **$72M**.
With 350–370M shares, the stock could fall to:

**💥 $0.25 – $0.75 per share**

This is the “everything goes wrong” scenario.

💅

# **Scenario B — They hit the goal, but trust is low**

(Ondas is cute, but no one believes his story.)

They reach **$110M** in 2026 sales
But investors still value them at only **2× sales**
That equals an EV of **$220M**
With dilution and doubt, stock could be:

**💥 $0.75 – $1.75 per share**

🛻 🛩️🚁

# **🧠 Big Picture**

1️⃣ Ondas is priced like a **future superstar**.

2️⃣ If they stumble even slightly, investors may value it like a **normal company** again.

3️⃣ That means the stock could fall:

**💥 60% – 90% from recent prices**

Not because it’s fake —

but because the expectations were **way too high**.

🛻 🛩️🚁

# **What Could Fix the Bear Case**

FAA approves nationwide BVLOS drone rules

Railroads begin buying dot16 systems in bulk

Multiple large government clients reorder Ondas drones, proving real-world value

🛻 🛩️🚁

# **Bottom Line**

* This bear case is about delays, regulations, dilution, and sky-high expectations.
* Competitors are real and experienced.
* A realistic risk-weighted price range:

 **$0.25 – $1.75 per share**

This is NOT a 12-month prediction —
just what the math says if investors get nervous.

🛻 🛩️🚁

🔟

**Girl — you saw him talking nasty to the waitress…**

Not in a sexy, confident, Madam 8 way.
 No… this was the kind of ugly that stops the whole restaurant.

He didn’t tell the waitress :
“I bet you taste as good as those potato wedges…”


He said:

“What took you so effing long? YOU people are why it’s hard to go out to eat these days.”

And instantly every girlfriend at that table thought: Oh. He’s that guy. 🚩

Because sometimes the red flag isn’t how a man treats you…
 but how he treats people he thinks can’t offer him anything.

And THIS is exactly the vibe when a company bragging about being “unstoppable” suddenly reveals how sloppy, frustrated, or reckless it really is behind the scenes.

Watching a company talk big in public while showing harmful behavior in the shadows is like watching technology being used against communities who already feel vulnerable.

A recent example that caused national outrage:

🔥 The George Floyd Protests (2020):

Widespread anger when police agencies used drones to surveil predominantly Black and minority protest groups.

The public reaction was intense because many saw it as:

high-tech tools being used in racially charged settings,

mimicking historical patterns where authorities weaponized tools against minorities.

This moment echoed — emotionally and symbolically — the way Americans felt watching the 1963 Birmingham attacks,

🛻 🛩️🚁

Soooooooooo AH
Will you give him your number or not?

title: A toy I don’t play with enough 😎: A quickie
body:
So the “simulate my returns” feature of $HOOD is quite interesting. I’m ashamed to admit I don’t use it enough.

I watch list this $SPY put to learn the moves here so I can make better short-term trades in the future. 

It’s good to play with this feature to determine what Price does $SPY need to drop to to make 30% return 

So by moving the bottom bar and watching either the whole dollar amount or if you wish you can switch it 2% change, you can determine the exact level that spy needs to fall to to hit your target. 

30% would be just lovely and I would likely take profit on a $SPY put at that level. That would give me about $267 of profit. 

So what I did was because my next couple of days are busy I just went ahead and set an alert for 682 using the top right corner feature. 

For those that have busy lives and cannot watch the market all day. This is very helpful. You can even set it for a couple of dollars beyond what you’re looking for. 

It’ll send you an alert when $SPY falls below that level. And then you can just open up your app to make the tree that you’re looking for. 

Obviously, you can do this for lots of different things.

I will also shout out AH user -Warren Buffett, who has a similar tool 
And definitely, you can give him a follow and learn about the way that works as well. 😎

title: 🙄My $HOOD rat mindset
body:
🎧 **“Around the Way Girl” – LL Cool J** 🎧

**My $HOOD-rat mindset**
Still trying to get my life together

Some days it feels like it’s never gonna happen.

But instead of go silent, I’ll just post about it so people can be entertained ￼

😎

🚌 The Bus Stop Lesson

This time in  the market?
Deals are everywhere — and most of them are **temporary**.

After one real year in the market, I’ve learned something important:
👉 **The ticker that’ll likely make you the most money is already in your portfolio.**

You’re already at the bus stop.
The bus that’s gonna take you *there* is coming.
You don’t run to the gas station for a candy-bar callout and miss it.

You sit.
You wait.
You stay patient.

So I will take my own advice

**Double down on what I already own.**

😎

📊 Portfolio Self-Check

title: Not trying to brag 😈how I keep track of my positions $HOOD
body:
This post is for NOOBS who use the Robin Hood brokerage account and are looking for ways to better manage multiple positions as they sell options 

￼
So those who use Robin Hood may not be using all of its features if you’re a noob 

I just want to briefly show you how you can adjust your options so that it reflects percentages 

This is important if you decide to sell options on multiple stock ticker

If you said it to the percentage mode. On a red days, it can save you time. 

Remember, if you sell options, red days are quite profitable. . How are they profitable? All of the contracts that you sold are now like getting free premium. Your shares are not likely to be exercised because the sheer price is dropping below your strike price.

If you want to be greedy. You can wait till your contract is 50%, 60%, 80% in profit. You buy back the contract at a total net profit of premium. And then you wait till the next day and maybe sell another copper call that you think will exercise in free premium 

I particularly like the 80% mark. 

Going forward if I see a covered call that is an 80% profit. I will probably try to buy it back at a net premium gain. Wait till the next day and then sell a covered call that will expire in two days.

For those who like pictures I’ve included how to change this option for you. 

This allows you to scan a list and see how much profit all of your covered calls a.k.a. SELL calls are in for the day

title: A quick update selling options 🥁put , calls
body:
So here’s an update from this morning.

Do you see my covered calls are nearly at 80% profit. 

Of course, when you sell an option, you get the premium instantly. You don’t really have to give it back. 

But it’s fun to see how your contract will exercise worthless to the buyer. Or 100% premium for you. 

If you change your option setting, when you see, your options are nearly at 80% profit. That is a time where if you’re greedy, you can buy your contract back and sell another covered call perhaps tomorrow when the market is a little bit green and premiums are high again. 

You do want to set a strike where your contract will not be exercised at a place you don’t want it to be 

Lastly, look at the cell put option that I did for $HOOD 

Definitely a risky move that invited a lot of questions 

But market sentiment is making $HOOD sell off heavily. I was on the fence of getting $118 strike. But I got a little greedy. I said I would get my shares back at $115 and be happy. 

Remember, I sold these shares for $120 last evening. I sold 86 shares. 

Here I have the opportunity if things work out and Robin Hood falls below 115, I would get 100 shares at $115. 

Plus, I sold an option to get to that point. So that decreased Price is in addition to the premium. I’ve already pocketed

I would not consider that losing money if that occurs. 

Worst case scenario. My option expires worthless. I do not get 100 shares. But I get the opportunity to buy back my $HOOD at less than $120 a share. 

TLDR: use market sentiment , bearish , and down trend markets to make money on selling options. ￼

🎧 Ivory Tower- Giorgio Moroder 🎧

Yes grief is a place. 

A very physical place

Your body will change from being there. Your mind will react. 

You can’t avoid it. You must go.

But you also can’t stay there. 

A ruined landscape is not where you spend your life 

That’s not your story 

You have a journey, a mission, a greater purpose. 

🎁Grief is a gift showing that to you. 


🌟 2. Grief clarifies what truly matters
Its a gift that helps you to reject the glitter and noise, and strip life back to the essentials:

Love
Presence
Memory
Connection

It teaches you to hold onto people while you have them, and to value moments over material things.

Yes, Sometimes you lose a horse.

title: YEAR IN REVIEW — No Brevity, But Honest
body:
It’s the end of the year, so here we are.

A little background: 
I’m a pretty private person. Very new to the market. Had no idea what an option was outside of dating terminology 😎. I’ve never been big into social media, I’m stubborn, independent, not easily influenced, and I don’t look for followers. I also have small kids and shared custody, so cyber-safety is always on my mind.


🐴I started this journey thinking I wouldn’t add much to my portfolio. Then I discovered the power of selling options… and I became obsessed with building 100-share “workhorses.” 


🤩Because once you have 100 shares, you can literally put them to work on your “farm toward early retirement”  AND earn you passive income. 

🤯That may sound obvious to veterans, but for someone new, especially with a smaller portfolio, it’s life-changing.

💅I don’t want my money to work me. I want them to work for me.

🤪I’m not against day trading or buying options, but they require time, risk tolerance, and emotional bandwidth I’m not comfortable with. 


Selling options taught me a lot about the market—and about myself.🙏

⭐️Madam 8 Lessons Learned ⭐️
 • Have a thesis. Price moves because of  buyers and sellers.  That’s it. • Understand risk-to-reward. Don’t run onto a  highway in heels to pick up a penny. • Even “perfect” companies don’t move in smooth perfect straight lines. Like dating, Don’t let volatility scare you away from a good thing.  • Know what you want your money to actually do for you.  • If you can’t afford the LV, don’t force it—sometimes the “knockoff” works. Eg: Tesla options too pricey? Try TSLL 

•Selling options gives steady income. 

•Higher-quality stocks usually do best—but I suggest you practice on the lower quality names, 

🤨Why?  because those “lower quality” plays can grow into your diamonds. If you learn on them early, you’re better prepared when they evolve.🧠

🤔Why not only rely on dividends? Because for meaningful dividend income you need massive capital. Dividends stocks are fine—I still hold them. But combining stocks with selling options can help beat the market.

Watching others win, lose, explain, and reflect has been incredibly valuable. I most appreciate people who post their thesis before and after.

😎Looking Ahead to 2026
 I’ll keep selling options. I’ll also be more aggressive adding capital because I want to reduce work hours. 

I love my small portfolios—they fit who I am. I don’t chase luxury; I prefer casual leisure. I’ll keep my cheeky humor, my emotional trading moments, and yes… music stays part of my market mood.

I’m pretty confident in where I landed. 

I’ll be around to answer questions tonight.

Most importantly! 

This community has helped me more than you know. Yes, there’s drama. Yes, there is controversy happens. 

Jbh. But that exists everywhere—in workplaces, in families, in life. AH feels like family to me. 

Ignore the noise, learn what you can, and remember: if you follow someone, understand how they built their portfolio. Lottery money thinking doesn’t always translate into disciplined strategy.

I learn best by “cross-training”—following different personalities, viewpoints, and strategies. Even when I disagree, I grow.

🙏Huge appreciation to: sirjack • NPO • the entire OA army • Allie • mastergroove • adioking • Vivian • Alloy • bobdog • the theta daddies • x52x • squeezekid •finkle • excontrader • geo21028 • Afterwhores • Carly BME and all the AH ladies who tolerate my foolishness. 

And because MADAM never forgets her roots… 😘KVPears who says he’s not forgotten about me, but I don’t know some days.😎

Yes. There are no secrets here. 

Here’s to doing it better, smarter, and cheekier next year. 🤗💚🫦

title: 🥁buying back the covered call on $ASTS
body:
looking at Price action this afternoon. 
A couple of my covered calls are in profit. 

And Robin Hood you’ll see this in green. Depending on how you set up your holdings. 

But note this $ASTS cover call is in 80% profit. So if you’re someone who likes to sell two covered calls in a week for maximum premium if it’s a good time to buy it back. 

I first learned about this through SMB capital the YouTube . They have a very nice collection of videos I do recommend. Especially for the day traders out there.

A little bit dry, but I appreciate dry humor and they’re a very nice break from the usual people trying to sell you something. 

Anyhow, tomorrow, I will likely sell another covered call. Just for two days that I think will expire in free premium. That doubles the yield on the amount of money I made off the shares. But obviously, I have to select the strike very carefully. 

Another option is to roll it in the same day. 
Rolling the position means you’re buying back the cover call and you’re selling another one simultaneously. 
you could choose to roll this option down and strike. And you would get a net premium. 

The reason I don’t like to do this on the same day is because Price action may flip on you. And that can be unpredictable. 

Unless you know something I don’t know. So for me, I feel safer just waiting until market. Open tomorrow to watch Price action and see what price to sell my second covered call for free premium.

title: Cost basis for $ASTS
body:
So as everyone who follows me probably knows I enjoy transparency

If you ever have a question or had a question as long as it’s not too personal, feel free to ask. 

(IRL. I don’t mind personal questions either. I’m just about safety on social media Internet lol )

This is a frequent question and for noobs I wanted to demonstrate something 

⭐️Your cost basis for shares will be high if you’re wheeling the stock . 

If you just buy and hold through the dips and downturns, sure your cost basis￼ will be low. If you start off high, you can always buy the dip and that will lower your cost basis. 

But if you’re committed to wheeling the stock all the way up and you have a small account. I don’t want you to be afraid of having a higher cost basis. 

Because if you’re wheeling￼correctly, what you’re doing is always taking profit and buying back in. 

Posting my current cost basis for $ASTS

I also wanted to post two screenshots of when I started buying the shares for this. In the IRA and my taxable account. I was first made of the stock by Finkle and that was when the cost was around $28.

This is a very important point. It demonstrates to anyone knew how much a stock can grow in just a year.

If you are new to the market.👀
I encourage you to look what people say at good companies when they were starting out. Look at all the hate that they receive. Look at all the nay sayers .- if you’re going to be a buy and be a long-term holder, you’re gonna have to learn how to ignore the noise and just hold through it.


Remember last year was my first year in the market so I was new had no idea. But this year I have a little bit more confidence on how to make the most money off of a quality stock that is volatile. 

Again there, 1,000,000+ ways to make money in the market. There is nothing wrong with buying and holding. An AH user named legitimate risk demonstrates this with his account. 

I am opting to sell and strategically buy options on my shares to help squeeze more money on the stock as it climbs to the top.

title: Bought to close $ASTS covered call 🥁
body:
So for those learning selling options. 
￼
One technique that I learned from SMB capital on YouTube is to buy back your covered calls when they are approaching 80% in profit. 

You could always sell another call at the end of the week that you think will expire. 

I tried this last week and my shares were assigned 😬

So it just makes sense for me to try it again this week🤪

So what you see here, $ASTS has taken a little bit of a nose dive. Nothing to be worried about. It’s just market sentiment. 

What I’m going to do is buy back the covered call for cheaper than what I sold it Resulting in a net profit. This will uncover my shares and release them from the contract. Note this resulted in $115 of profit. 

I wasn’t quick enough. This cover call dropped to one cent in value. Meaning I could’ve gotten back 97% of my premium back. This sale is for about 80%. I had to pay $15 to buy back this cover call.

I have zero cash in my portfolio. So to afford this, I had to sell one share of $SCHD.

Tomorrow may be a better day. I could sell another covered call for a 2 to 3 day expiration. I may be even able to sell it at the same strip price depending on price action. $ASTS may rise at the end of the day Resulting in better or return of the premium amount. 

Buying back and selling options can increase your return overtime. I was slow to realize this concept. But I’m passing it along to you. 

Again, thank you to SMB capital ￼￼

title: Bought to close $LYFT, $ASTS covered calls:IRA
body:
Again, the idea behind doing this is you close your calls early

You take 80% of the premium 

Yes, it’s not the entire 100%. But keep in mind you have enough days to sell another covered call and let that explore 100% so it is like overlapping premiums. Overlapping profits on shares you own. 

Another bonus is if you expect a big breakout move that might spike your share price above your covered call over the next couple of days. 

Like a rebound or rubber band effect. You don’t have to worry about your covered calls being assigned . 

You’ve already taken it off for 80% profit. You can sleep good at night not worried about what the market will open like for the rest of the week. ￼

Sometimes you have to be quick to close these covered calls. 

Remember these contracts for $ASTS were at 97% profit this morning. But they’ve since rebounded somewhat. 

So it’s a little bit like playing day trading from the other side 

So tomorrow. What I will try to demonstrate is selling a covered call that will expire for 100% premium on both of these contracts.

title: Its only logical : 4️⃣ ﻿﻿﻿ Ad ignorantum
body:
Its only logical : 4️⃣ ﻿﻿﻿ Ad ignorantum

🎧Ive fallen and I can't beam up - Michael Giacchino 🎧

This is one fallacy I usually just walk away from in a debate. just not worth the energy for me.

But here are some examples for you using $TSLA and $ASTS 👇

“There’s no proof $TSLA’s valuation is a bubble, so it must be fairly priced.”

“No one has proven that $ASTS won’t replace Tesla’s satellite connectivity long-term, so $ASTS is obviously the better investment than $TSLA.”

Why this is a fallacy: The claim assumes something is true simply because it hasn’t been disproven. Lack of evidence against a claim ≠ evidence for the claim.

OR 

“There’s no proof $TSLA’s valuation is a bubble, so it must be fairly priced.

OR

“Until someone proves $ASTS can’t deliver global satellite broadband at scale, I’m treating it as guaranteed.”

OR

More recently on X - “I am convinced you are a transsexual man”

The last one I asked, what proof could I even provide to prove otherwise. No response.

usually these arguments begin with, but  “I have never heard of this”

and that’s where I end the argument because I don’t wanna be the one to educate you. just too much work. 

so this one gets added to the 👇￼￼

To Err is Human: logical fallacy list.

1️⃣- Ad Hominem Attacks on personal character instead of thesis 

2️⃣ Hasty Generalizations -small numbers to represent everything

3️⃣ Post Hoc  - because something occurred before it must be the cause

4️⃣ ﻿﻿﻿ Ad ignorantum -arguing that because of our ignorance, a claim must be true or false.

title: Its only logical : 5️⃣ Non sequitur
body:
🎧heart to heart conversation - Michael Giachino 🎧

Valentine’s Day is over
So it is only logical we get back to work.

Do you see that ? Thats a Non sequitur

Non sequitur = “It does not follow.”
The conclusion doesn’t logically connect to the premise

I will give you two more using stock examples. 

Again, I do not own any $TSLA currently. I do own $ASTS  and a very big position. 

Just demonstrating I’m able to poke fun of myself. I’m comfortable with doing so. I already know I’m in a illogical traitor, and I own up to it.

“Tesla makes the most advanced EVs.
Therefore, $TSLA stock must go up this year

Why this is a non sequitur:

Product quality ≠ stock price performance.
Stock price depends on:
    
Valuation
 Interest rates
  Margins
  Competition
  Market sentiment
  Liquidity


The conclusion (stock must go up) doesn’t logically follow from the premise (great cars).

The argument jumps a step.

“AST SpaceMobile is partnering with major telecom companies.Therefore, $ASTS is a guaranteed 10x.”

Why this is a non sequitur:

Partnerships ≠ profitability
 Revenue ≠ free cash flow
Potential ≠ execution

The leap from “big partnership” to “guaranteed massive return” has no logical bridge.

Don’t get this confused with post hoc

Post hoc = false cause-and-effect assumption based on sequence

Non sequitur = logical disconnect between premise and conclusion

body:
🎧Who Dat? - Dejan’ Olympia Brass Band 🎧

Straw man is when a challenger misrepresents or exaggerates a person's argument in order to make it easier to attack.  

The term strawman dates back to medieval times where military armies would practice on human figures made of straw. It’s a weak, poor representative of the enemy

In my mind I called this  the bar man debate. It’s something you would see from a gentleman who’s had too much and a bit pompous. 

The argument rebuttal ￼ seems on the surface  very masculine but really it’s just a weak attack. It does nothing for the debate.

“Oh, so you think $ASTS is guaranteed to replace every telecom company and make everyone rich overnight?”

Real argument:

“$TSLA has strong vertical integration and energy growth that could support future earnings.”


Strawman version:
“So you’re saying Tesla can never fail and will dominate every industry forever?”

Kills productive debate
Turns analysis into tribal warfare
Prevents you from stress-testing real theses

title: Its only logical :🔟 Bandwagon fallacy
body:
🎧This is America- Childish Gambino🎧


Ahh
The bandwagon fallacy

 It is poor form to argue that because a premise is popular, it must be true. 

Welp. 😅

No need for lots discussion here . There have been lots of examples on this app of this. And they will continue to be.

To be honest, this is the heart of  social trading in general sooo

Some examples for you $TSLA and $ASTS 👇

“Everyone on X is bullish on $TSLA right now. It must be going higher.”

OR 

“All the retail investors I follow are loading $ASTS. It has to be the next big thing.”

Why this is faulty thinking?

 Social sentiment can be wrong.
Crowds often pile in near tops.
Viral conviction is not valuation analysis.
Community enthusiasm ≠ execution success.
Echo chambers amplify optimism.
Retail momentum can detach from fundamentals.


Remember being popular  doesn’t equal sustainable earnings and Just because a stock is trending doesn’t mean it’s underpriced 

🚀We have arrived, Captain 

we are at 10. 

Logically that concludes this attempt to boldly go were no other AH user goes🤪

I was thinking about pinning this to my X feed

But I really do like illogical arguments, and emotional trading.

Like I said, I do it all the time. I’m very transparent. I KNOW I am crazy. 

What I don’t do - go  around making emotional decisions and trying to make logic out of them. - to do that you’ve got to be out of your Vulcan mind. 

🤪
To Err is Human: logical fallacy list.

1️⃣- Ad Hominem Attacks on personal character instead of thesis 

2️⃣ Hasty Generalizations -small numbers to represent everything

3️⃣ Post Hoc  - because something occurred before it must be the cause

4️⃣ Ad ignorantum -arguing that because of our ignorance, a claim must be true or false.

5️⃣ Non sequitur - this follows that when there is no logical connection between the two.

6️⃣ Straw man -  misrepresent or exaggerate a person's argument in order to make it easier to attack.  

7️⃣. Begging the question - Arguing a position by assuming one of its premises is true.

8️⃣False Dichotomy - reduces a complex situation into only two extreme options, when many outcomes exist in between.

9️⃣ Burden of proof reversal- laying the burden of proof onto the person that is questioning the claim.

🔟 Bandwagon fallacy- saying because a premise is popular, it must be true.

title: Pillow Talk :  Worried about the markets? We must reinstate tariffs
body:
Madam 8: Tariffs Are the Prenup of Global Trade 💍📈

A five-minute read

🤗💚🤗

If you have followed me on AfterHour for any length of time, you know I love a good dating analogy for economics. 

Going to start a weekly series - more predictive, market opinions, sometimes TA- Madam 8’s Pillow Talk

This has been posted to substack - which is free. 
AH always will get dibs though 
Likely a futile desperate attempt to bring more people to the app.

😈

Markets are emotional. Countries compete. And trade relationships?
They are like complicated marriages.

Been there 
done that
I have the cropped shirt. 

Right now the United States is in a messy relationship with China, and the policy tool everyone keeps arguing about is tariffs — the strategy strongly associated with President Donald Trump.

Whether you love him  or hate him, tariffs were the centerpiece of the economic strategy.

Removing them without a plan is a bit like tearing up a prenup during a rocky marriage.

It may feel good in the moment.

But it leaves you exposed later.

🌎 Tariffs: The Prenup of Global Trade

Yes Ladies and Gentleman, tariffs like a prenup agreement before marriage.

Nobody enters a relationship expecting it to fail.
 But smart people prepare for the possibility that interests might diverge.

Tariffs serve a similar role in international trade.

They:
• protect domestic industries • discourage unfair price dumping • encourage companies to produce inside the United States (yep Making America Great Again) • reduce dependency on foreign supply chains ( ahem no more Chinese mistress)


Without tariffs, domestic industries can easily be undercut by cheaper imports produced under very different labor and regulatory systems.

In other words:

A prenup doesn’t destroy a relationship.
 It simply protects if things get messy.

❤️🧢Why Tariffs Were the Cornerstone of Trump’s Economic Policy

The economic philosophy behind tariffs was simple.

For decades the United States prioritized cheap imports and global supply chains.

The trade-off was that many manufacturing jobs moved overseas.

Tariffs attempted to reverse that dynamic by making imported goods more expensive relative to domestic production.

The idea was to push companies toward:
• American factories • American workers • American supply chains
Supporters believed this would rebuild strategic industries.

It also leads us less open to security risks. As most women can relate to, if someone is controlling all your money and how you get goods and services. Well, in fact, they’re controlling you.

America says they’re done with the potential of being controlled by China. 

Critics argued tariffs would increase consumer prices. This is a fair argument. If a wife leaves a husband who previously paid for everything. She will have to pay.

But regardless of which side you prefer, tariffs were clearly the central pillar of the strategy.

Remove that pillar and the entire framework changes.

🇨🇳The China Factor

Trade policy today is no longer just economics.
It is geopolitical competition.

China dominates large portions of global manufacturing, including:

• electronics • solar panels • batteries • rare earth processing • pharmaceutical ingredients

When tariffs were introduced, the message was clear:

The United States was willing to push back economically. Ladies, you can imagine how China feels.

Even if tariffs were removed tomorrow, the signal has already been sent.

And global competitors rarely interpret policy reversals as generosity. Lets be honest, what would Putin and Xi think if America reversed on tariffs.

They interpret them as weakness.

In negotiation — whether dating or geopolitics — signals matter.

If one side thinks the other is backing down, they often push harder.

👩‍⚖️🤝Two Ways Tariffs Could Be Reinstated

If policymakers decide tariffs are still necessary, there are two realistic paths.


1. Bipartisan Legislation

Congress could pass legislation reinstating or expanding tariffs on strategic industries.

This approach would:
• create long-term stability • ensure tariffs cannot easily be reversed • demonstrate bipartisan support

Trade policy that survives multiple administrations tends to have stronger negotiating power internationally.

2. Executive Action
A president also has the authority to impose tariffs through existing trade laws.

For example:
• national security tariffs • penalties for unfair trade practices


An example would be Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act (for national security threats, e.g., steel/aluminum tariffs) or Section 301 of the Trade Act (for unfair trade practices, e.g., against China). 

These have been used before but face their own legal scrutiny and require specific findings. 

President Trump could attempt to reimpose tariffs under a narrower IEEPA reading or appeal lower court refund decisions, though the Supreme Court’s ruling limits this path. 

These tools allow faster action but are more vulnerable to political reversal.

Still, they provide a way for a president to act without waiting for Congress.

⛽️📉Why Ending the Trade War Quickly Matters

Prolonged economic conflicts rarely stay limited to tariffs.

They expand into:
• technology restrictions • financial sanctions • military alliances ( remember that war with Iran) • supply-chain blocs

Oh and let’s not forget the most important thing, it can mess with our money. That would be the stock market.

The longer a trade confrontation lasts, the more likely other powers step in to support one side or the other.

“A enemy of my enemy is my friend.” 
We are in a war with Iran. You don’t have to be an geographical genius to know who their biggest neighbors are.

And when multiple countries begin supplying resources, technology, or weapons to competing blocs, conflicts become much harder to resolve. The World War III scenario.

History shows that economic wars rarely stay economic forever.

😈Madam 8’s Final Thought

Every relationship needs boundaries.
Dating. Marriage. Global trade.

Tariffs were designed to function as the boundaries of international commerce.

They were never meant to be permanent punishment.

They were leverage.

And leverage only works when the other side believes you are willing to use it.

In dating terms:
If someone knows you will always fold… they stop negotiating and start taking advantage.

In economics, the same rule applies.

Sleep tight sweetie . Market open at 9:30 EST 💋

title: When will I learn?  7️⃣
body:
When will I learn?  7️⃣

🎧 Mistakes (Ground Zero Edit) – Bulletproof 🎧

7. Jim Simons (Renaissance Technologies)

The Medallion Fund—his legendary quantitative hedge fund, launched in 1988—experienced its only net losing year in 1989, posting about a -4% return after fees while the S&P 500 surged over 30%.

Early versions of the fund’s models in the late 1980s (including a weak 1988 debut of ~9% net) delivered underwhelming or negative results, leading to client complaints, internal tensions, and the buyout of key partner James Ax in 1989. 

These early setbacks forced a major overhaul of the trading system (led by Elwyn Berlekamp), which proved costly in time, trust, and resources—but ultimately paved the way for the fund’s extraordinary long-term performance: average annual returns of ~66% gross / ~39% net from 1988–2018, with no other net losing years and over $100 billion in total trading profits. strategy.

title: When will I learn? 5️⃣

🎧Thats A mistake – Riley Green 🎧

5️⃣ Ray Dalio

In 1982 (early in Bridgewater’s history), Dalio bet heavily on a global debt crisis and market crash, expecting unsustainable lending—especially to Latin America—to trigger defaults and economic collapse. Mexico’s debt default in August 1982 initially seemed to confirm his view, but the Fed responded by cutting rates and providing liquidity, sparking a strong market rally instead. The opposite outcome caused massive losses, nearly bankrupting the firm. He was forced to lay off all his employees (leaving only himself) and even borrowed $4,000 from his father to cover family bills.

This humbling failure became a turning point: Dalio later called it “the best thing that ever happened to me” because it taught him humility, the dangers of overconfidence, and the value of radical open-mindedness—principles that rebuilt and scaled Bridgewater into one of the world’s largest hedge funds.

title: When will I learn? 4️⃣
body:
🎧My own worst enemy- Lit 🎧


4️⃣ George Soros (Quantum Fund)

In 1999, Soros’s Quantum Fund heavily shorted internet/tech stocks, expecting a dot-com bubble burst. The rally continued (Amazon, Yahoo, etc. soared), causing ~$700 million in losses early in the year—his worst period amid a booming market.

The fund reversed course mid-1999, going long on tech and finishing the year up ~35% (though lagging the Nasdaq’s ~85%). In early 2000, still bearish, it sold out then capitulated by buying back in heavily just before the March peak, leading to sharp losses (~22% YTD drawdown by April) and over $5 billion wiped from Soros funds overall.


This mistimed contrarian bet triggered Druckenmiller’s retirement, a firm restructuring toward lower risk, and acceptance of more modest returns—despite Soros’s stellar long-term record (~32% average annual from 1969–1999).

title: When will I learn 3️⃣
body:
🎧Moral of the Story - Ashe  🎧

3️⃣ Peter Lynch (Fidelity Magellan Fund)

Peter Lynch has repeatedly cited his biggest recurring mistake as selling winning stocks to￼o early while holding onto losers—what he famously called “cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.”

This behavioral pattern—trimming strong performers bprematurely (e.g., he mentioned selling Home Depot too soon and missing massive subsequent gains)—limited compounding on long-term winners during his legendary 1977–1990 tenure, when Magellan averaged ~29% annual returns. Though no single event ties to exact dollar losses, Lynch described it as a major opportunity cost that prevented even greater outperformance.

The ironic twist: Warren Buffett loved the phrase so much he called Lynch for permission to quote it in a Berkshire Hathaway annual report. Lynch’s advice remains: let winners run (as long as fundamentals hold) and cut losers decisively.
